docs.title: type CuckooMap
docs.text:
CuckooMap (Int keys, Int values) Two power-of-two tables with two independent multiplicative hashes. Insert displaces the victim to the other table (bounded at 16 relocations, then the tables double). O(1) expected lookups with at most 2 probes.

Field Type t0_keys Vec[Int] t0_vals Vec[Int] t1_keys Vec[Int] t1_vals Vec[Int] size Int cap Int

docs.title: fn cuckoo_new(capacity: Int) -> CuckooMap
docs.text:
Create an empty cuckoo map with at least capacity slots (rounded up to a power of two).

  • Postcondition: result.cap >= 8
  • Postcondition: result.size == 0
  • Postcondition: result.t0_keys.len() == result.cap

docs.title: fn cuckoo_put(m: &mut CuckooMap, key: Int, value: Int)
docs.text:
Insert or overwrite key -> value. Doubles the tables when the displacement bound is exceeded.

  • Postcondition: cuckoo_contains(m, key)

docs.title: fn cuckoo_get(m: &CuckooMap, key: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Value for key (None if absent).

  • Postcondition: result.is_some == cuckoo_contains(m, key)

docs.title: fn cuckoo_contains(m: &CuckooMap, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if key is present.

  • Postcondition: result == true => cuckoo_size(m) >= 1

docs.title: fn cuckoo_remove(m: &mut CuckooMap, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
Remove key. Returns true if it was present.

  • Postcondition: cuckoo_contains(m, key) == false

docs.title: fn cuckoo_size(m: &CuckooMap) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of stored keys.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type Dag
docs.text:
Directed acyclic graph of Int node ids with topological ordering support.

Flat-arena style (the same adjacency representation as collect.graph): head[u] is the first edge id leaving node u, to[id] the destination of edge id, next[id] the next edge id in the same list (-1 = none). Node ids are handed out by dag_add_node and never reused. dag_add_edge refuses to add an edge that would close a cycle (checked via reachability of from from to); dag_has_cycle runs a full topological sort. Reachability and traversal helpers are BFS based (O(V + E)). Out-of-range ids are rejected (no silent failure).

Field Type n Int head Vec[Int] to Vec[Int] next Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn dag_new() -> Dag
docs.text:
Create a new empty DAG (no nodes). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.n == 0

docs.title: fn dag_add_node(g: &mut Dag) -> Int
docs.text:
Add a node and return its id (0-based, monotonically increasing). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn dag_has_edge(g: &Dag, from: Int, to: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if the edge from -> to exists. O(degree(from)).

  • Postcondition: from < 0 || from >= g.n => result == false

docs.title: fn dag_add_edge(g: &mut Dag, from: Int, to: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
Add a directed edge from -> to. Returns false if the ids are out of range, if the edge already exists, or if adding it would close a cycle (i.e. to can already reach from). True when the edge is newly added. Self loops are rejected. O(V + E) for the cycle check.

  • Postcondition: result == true => dag_has_edge(g, from, to)

docs.title: fn dag_ancestors(g: &Dag, node: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
All transitive predecessors of node (nodes u != node with a path u -> ... -> node). Order is BFS order over the reversed edges. O(V + E).

  • Postcondition: node < 0 || node >= g.n => result.len() == 0
  • Postcondition: result.len() <= g.n

docs.title: fn dag_descendants(g: &Dag, node: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
All transitive successors of node (nodes v != node with a path node -> ... -> v). Order is BFS order. O(V + E).

  • Postcondition: node < 0 || node >= g.n => result.len() == 0
  • Postcondition: result.len() <= g.n

docs.title: fn dag_topological_order(g: &Dag) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
A topological ordering of all nodes (Kahn's algorithm). If the graph contains a cycle, the returned order is partial (the cyclic nodes are omitted). O(V + E).

  • Postcondition: result.len() <= g.n

docs.title: fn dag_has_cycle(g: &Dag) -> Bool
docs.text:
Check whether the graph contains a cycle (a topological sort covers all nodes iff the graph is acyclic). O(V + E).

  • Postcondition: result == true => g.n >= 1

docs.title: type DenseSet
docs.text:
Dense set of unique Int elements backed by a bitmap for compact storage.

Non-negative values are stored as a single bit each; the bitmap lives in a Vec[UInt8] (value v occupies bit v % 8 of byte v / 8) that grows on demand to cover the largest inserted value. All core operations are O(1); iteration is O(bits) plus the set size. Negative values cannot be represented and are rejected by dense_add (documented, no silent failure).

Field Type bits Vec[UInt8] size Int

docs.title: fn dense_set_new() -> DenseSet
docs.text: Create a new empty dense set. O(1).

docs.title: fn dense_add(s: &mut DenseSet, value: Int)
docs.text: Add a value to the set (no-op if already present). Negative values are rejected (the bitmap cannot represent them). O(1) amortized.

docs.title: fn dense_contains(s: &DenseSet, value: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Check whether a value is present. O(1).

docs.title: fn dense_remove(s: &mut DenseSet, value: Int)
docs.text: Remove a value from the set (no-op if absent). O(1).

docs.title: fn dense_size(s: &DenseSet) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of elements in the set. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn dense_iter(s: &DenseSet) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Iterate all elements in ascending order. O(bits + n).

docs.title: type Deque
docs.text:
Double-ended queue of Int elements with O(1) push and pop at both ends. Backed by a single Vec[Int] with head/tail offsets defining the live window [head, tail). Pops advance the offsets (stale slots are later overwritten); deque_push_front rebuilds the window when there is no room at the front. All pops/peeks are bounds-checked (None on empty).

Field Type items Vec[Int] head Int tail Int

docs.title: fn deque_new() -> Deque
docs.text:
Create an empty deque. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.head == 0
  • Postcondition: result.tail == 0

docs.title: fn deque_push_back(d: &mut Deque, value: Int)
docs.text:
Append value to the back of the deque. O(1).

  • Postcondition: d.tail - d.head >= 1

docs.title: fn deque_push_front(d: &mut Deque, value: Int)
docs.text:
Prepend value to the front of the deque. O(1) amortized (O(n) when the window must be rebuilt).

  • Postcondition: d.tail - d.head >= 1

docs.title: fn deque_pop_front(d: &mut Deque) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Remove and return the front value. None if the deque is empty. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result is None => d.tail - d.head == 0

docs.title: fn deque_pop_back(d: &mut Deque) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Remove and return the back value. None if the deque is empty. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result is None => d.tail - d.head == 0

docs.title: fn deque_front(d: &Deque) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Return the front value without removing it. None if empty. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result is None => d.tail - d.head == 0

docs.title: fn deque_back(d: &Deque) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Return the back value without removing it. None if empty. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result is None => d.tail - d.head == 0

docs.title: fn deque_len(d: &Deque) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of elements in the deque. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn deque_is_empty(d: &Deque) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if the deque holds no elements. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result == (deque_len(d) == 0)

docs.title: type FenwickTree
docs.text:
FenwickTree (1-based indices; n = number of slots) Point update + prefix-sum queries in O(log n). tree[i] covers the range (i - lowbit(i), i]. All index params are 1-based; 0 is invalid (returns 0).

Field Type tree Vec[Int] n Int

docs.title: fn fenwick_new(n: Int) -> FenwickTree
docs.text:
Create a fenwick tree with n slots, all zero.

  • Postcondition: result.n == n
  • Postcondition: n >= 0 => result.tree.len() == n + 1

docs.title: fn fenwick_add(t: &mut FenwickTree, idx: Int, delta: Int)
docs.text:
Add delta to slot idx (1-based). O(log n).

  • Postcondition: idx >= 1 && idx <= t.n && delta >= 0 => fenwick_sum(t, t.n) >= fenwick_sum(t, t.n)@pre

docs.title: fn fenwick_sum(t: &FenwickTree, idx: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Prefix sum of slots 1..=idx. O(log n). idx < 1 -> 0.

  • Postcondition: idx < 1 => result == 0

docs.title: fn fenwick_range(t: &FenwickTree, l: Int, r: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Sum of slots l..=r (1-based, inclusive). O(log n).

  • Postcondition: r < l => result == 0

docs.title: fn fenwick_get(t: &FenwickTree, idx: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Current value at slot idx (1-based). O(log n).

  • Postcondition: idx < 1 || idx > t.n => result == 0

docs.title: fn fenwick_size(t: &FenwickTree) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of slots.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type FibNode
docs.text:
Handle to a heap node, used by fheap_decrease_key. In the flat-arena adaptation the handle wraps the node's arena index (nodes are allocated in insertion order by fheap_push).

Field Type idx Int

docs.title: fn fheap_new() -> FibHeap
docs.text:
Create a new empty Fibonacci heap. Returns: an empty FibHeap. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.n == 0

docs.title: fn fheap_push(h: &mut FibHeap, value: Int)
docs.text:
Insert an element. Params: h - the heap; value - Int element to insert. Complexity: O(1) amortized.

  • Postcondition: h.n >= 1

docs.title: fn fheap_pop(h: &mut FibHeap) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Remove and return the minimum element. None if empty. Params: h - the heap. Returns: the minimum element, or None when empty. Complexity: O(log n) amortized.

  • Postcondition: result is None => h.n == 0

docs.title: fn fheap_peek(h: &FibHeap) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Peek at the minimum element. None if empty. Params: h - the heap. Returns: the minimum element without removing it, or None when empty. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result is None => h.n == 0

docs.title: fn fheap_merge(h: &mut FibHeap, other: &mut FibHeap)
docs.text:
Merge other into this heap, leaving other empty. Params: h - the receiving heap; other - the heap to consume. Complexity: O(n log n) worst-case (drains via extract-min + insert).

  • Postcondition: other.n == 0

docs.title: fn fheap_decrease_key(h: &mut FibHeap, node: &mut FibNode, new_key: Int)
docs.text: Decrease a node's key. Params: h - the heap; node - a FibNode handle (arena index of a node allocated by fheap_push); new_key - the smaller key. Out-of-range handles and non-decreasing keys are ignored. Complexity: O(1) amortized.

docs.title: fn fheap_len(h: &FibHeap) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of elements. Params: h - the heap. Returns: the number of elements currently stored. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type Graph
docs.text:
Graph (Int node ids) The spec struct is { n: Int; adj: Vec[Vec[Int]]; }, but nested Vec[Vec[Int]] element access is unreliable in the current compiler (see collect/heap.xi), so the adj field is retained per the module spec while the adjacency is stored in a flat linked arena: head[u] = first edge id in u's neighbor list (or -1) to[id] = destination node of edge id next[id] = next edge id in the same node's list (or -1) Appending is O(1); has_edge/degree/neighbors walk the list. graph_add_edge adds both directions and rejects duplicates; graph_add_directed_edge adds a single directed edge.

Field Type n Int adj Vec[Vec[Int]] head Vec[Int] to Vec[Int] next Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn graph_new(n: Int) -> Graph
docs.text:
Create a graph with n isolated nodes.

  • Postcondition: result.n == n

docs.title: fn graph_has_edge(g: &Graph, u: Int, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if node v is a neighbor of node u.

  • Postcondition: u < 0 || u >= g.n => result == false

docs.title: fn graph_add_edge(g: &mut Graph, u: Int, v: Int)
docs.text:
Add an undirected edge between u and v (no duplicates).

  • Postcondition: u >= 0 && u < g.n && v >= 0 && v < g.n => graph_has_edge(g, u, v)

docs.title: fn graph_add_directed_edge(g: &mut Graph, u: Int, v: Int)
docs.text:
Add a directed edge u -> v (no duplicates).

  • Postcondition: u >= 0 && u < g.n && v >= 0 && v < g.n => graph_has_edge(g, u, v)

docs.title: fn graph_degree(g: &Graph, u: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of neighbors of node u.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn graph_neighbors(g: &Graph, u: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
A copy of the neighbors of node u.

  • Postcondition: result.len() == graph_degree(g, u)

docs.title: fn graph_bfs(g: &Graph, start: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
Breadth-first traversal from start, in visited order.

  • Postcondition: start < 0 || start >= g.n => result.len() == 0
  • Postcondition: result.len() <= g.n

docs.title: fn graph_dfs(g: &Graph, start: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
Iterative depth-first traversal from start, in visited order.

  • Postcondition: start < 0 || start >= g.n => result.len() == 0
  • Postcondition: result.len() <= g.n

docs.title: fn graph_connected_components(g: &Graph) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of connected components in the graph.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn graph_has_cycle(g: &Graph) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if the (undirected) graph contains a cycle. Uses BFS with a parent check: a visited neighbor that is not the current node's parent closes a cycle.

  • Postcondition: result == true => g.n >= 1

docs.title: fn graph_path_exists(g: &Graph, a: Int, b: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if there is a path from a to b (BFS).

  • Postcondition: a == b && a >= 0 && a < g.n => result == true

docs.title: type GraphUnionFind
docs.text:
Union-Find / Disjoint Set (Int elements) parent stores each element's parent (root points at itself) and rank stores the tree height for union-by-rank. uf_find applies path compression; uf_find_no_compress is a read-only variant used by uf_connected and uf_count so they can take an immutable reference.

Field Type parent Vec[Int] rank Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn uf_new(n: Int) -> GraphUnionFind
docs.text:
Create a disjoint set with elements 0..n-1, each in its own set.

  • Postcondition: result.parent.len() == result.rank.len()

docs.title: fn uf_find(u: &mut GraphUnionFind, x: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Find the root of x with path compression.

  • Postcondition: x >= 0 && x < u.parent.len() => result >= 0

docs.title: fn uf_union(u: &mut GraphUnionFind, a: Int, b: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
Merge the sets containing a and b (union by rank). Returns true if the two sets were merged (i.e. previously disjoint).

  • Postcondition: a >= 0 && a < u.parent.len() && b >= 0 && b < u.parent.len() => uf_connected(u, a, b)

docs.title: fn uf_connected(u: &GraphUnionFind, a: Int, b: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if a and b are in the same set.

  • Postcondition: a == b => result == true

docs.title: fn uf_count(u: &GraphUnionFind) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of distinct roots (sets).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type Hamt
docs.text:
Hash array mapped trie (Int keys, Int values). A space-efficient persistent map built on a trie of 32-way nodes using the hash of the key. Average O(log_32 n) operations with fast structural sharing and cache locality. Duplicate keys are rejected by insert.

Flat-arena style (the established collect/ pattern -- tree.xi/graph.xi use parallel Vec[Int]s because Vec-of-struct instantiations collide at startup in combined programs). Every node owns 32 child slots in the flat kids vector (kids[i * 32 + slot]), so table nodes and leaf nodes share one uniform layout. Leaf nodes additionally carry the key, the value and the full 64-bit hash of the key; is_leaf[i] distinguishes the two kinds. The 5-bit window of the key hash at depth d selects the child slot, so a path is at most 13 nodes deep (64 hash bits / 5 bits). Node 0 is always a table node (the root).

Field Type root Int size Int keys Vec[Int] values Vec[Int] hashes Vec[Int] is_leaf Vec[Bool] kids Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn hamt_new() -> Hamt
docs.text: Create an empty HAMT (a single empty root table node). Returns a fresh Hamt with size 0. O(1) time, O(1) memory.

docs.title: fn hamt_insert(h: &mut Hamt, key: Int, value: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Insert key -> value. Returns false if the key already exists (the map keeps the original value). True on a fresh insert. O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_get(h: &Hamt, key: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Value stored for key, or None if the key is absent. O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_contains(h: &Hamt, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True if key is present in the map. O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_remove(h: &mut Hamt, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Remove key. Returns true if it was present. O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_size(h: &Hamt) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of key/value pairs in the map. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn hamt_clear(h: &mut Hamt)
docs.text:
Remove all entries, leaving the map empty. O(1) (arena memory is retained).

  • Postcondition: hamt_size(h) == 0

docs.title: type BloomFilter
docs.text:
Bloom Filter (UInt8 byte inputs) bits is a byte array holding bit_count usable bits (rounded up to a byte multiple). Two independent base hashes (FNV-1a and DJB2) are combined into num_hashes positions via h1 + ih2 mod m. inserted tracks the number of insertions so the false positive rate can be estimated as (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k.

Field Type bits Vec[UInt8] bit_count Int num_hashes Int inserted Int

docs.title: fn bloom_new(bits: Int, num_hashes: Int) -> BloomFilter
docs.text:
Create a bloom filter with bits usable bits and num_hashes hash functions. The bit count is rounded up to a whole number of bytes.

  • Postcondition: result.bit_count >= 8
  • Postcondition: result.num_hashes >= 1

docs.title: fn bloom_insert(b: &mut BloomFilter, data: &Vec[UInt8])
docs.text:
Insert the given bytes into the filter.

  • Postcondition: bloom_maybe_contains(b, data)

docs.title: fn bloom_maybe_contains(b: &BloomFilter, data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if the bytes may be present. Never reports a false negative.

  • Postcondition: b.inserted == 0 => result == false

docs.title: fn bloom_clear(b: &mut BloomFilter)
docs.text:
Clear all bits and reset the insertion counter.

  • Postcondition: b.inserted == 0

docs.title: fn bloom_false_positive_rate(b: &BloomFilter) -> Float64
docs.text:
Estimated false positive rate: (1 - e^(-k*n/m))^k using the tracked insertion count, where k = num_hashes, n = inserted, m = bit_count.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type LhMap
docs.text:
LhMap -- insertion-ordered map (Int keys -> Int values) Inserting a new key appends; updating an existing key keeps its position.

Field Type keys Vec[Int] values Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn lhmap_new() -> LhMap
docs.text:
Create an empty insertion-ordered map.

  • Postcondition: result.keys.len() == 0

docs.title: fn lhmap_put(m: &mut LhMap, key: Int, value: Int)
docs.text:
Insert or update a key. New keys are appended in insertion order.

  • Postcondition: lhmap_contains(m, key)

docs.title: fn lhmap_get(m: &LhMap, key: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Fetch a value by key. None if absent.

  • Postcondition: result.is_some == lhmap_contains(m, key)

docs.title: fn lhmap_contains(m: &LhMap, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
True if the key is present.

  • Postcondition: result == true => lhmap_size(m) >= 1

docs.title: fn lhmap_remove(m: &mut LhMap, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:
Remove a key, preserving the relative order of the remaining entries. Returns true if the key was present.

  • Postcondition: lhmap_contains(m, key) == false
  • Postcondition: result == true => lhmap_size(m) == lhmap_size(m)@pre - 1
  • Postcondition: result == false => lhmap_size(m) == lhmap_size(m)@pre

docs.title: fn lhmap_size(m: &LhMap) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of entries in the map.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn lhmap_keys_in_order(m: &LhMap) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
The keys in insertion order.

  • Postcondition: result.len() == lhmap_size(m)

docs.title: type Hamt
docs.text:
Hash-array mapped trie (HAMT) map of Int keys to Int values. Flat-arena style (the established collect/ pattern): every node owns 32 child slots in the flat kids vector (kids[i * 32 + slot]), so table nodes and leaf nodes share one uniform layout. Leaf nodes carry the key, the value and the full 64-bit hash; is_leaf[i] distinguishes the kinds. The 5-bit window of the key hash at depth d selects the child slot, so a path is at most 13 nodes deep (64 hash bits / 5 bits). Node 0 is always a table node (the root). Inserts are upserts: re-inserting a key updates its value. Average O(log_32 n) operations.

Field Type root Int size Int keys Vec[Int] values Vec[Int] hashes Vec[Int] is_leaf Vec[Bool] kids Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn hamt_new() -> Hamt
docs.text: Create a new empty HAMT map (a single empty root table node). Returns: a fresh Hamt with 0 entries. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn hamt_insert(h: &mut Hamt, key: Int, value: Int)
docs.text: Insert or update key -> value. Params: h - the map; key - Int key; value - Int value. Re-inserting an existing key updates its value in place. Complexity: O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_get(h: &Hamt, key: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Get the value for a key. None when absent. Params: h - the map; key - Int key. Returns: Some(value) if present, None otherwise. Complexity: O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_contains(h: &Hamt, key: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Check whether a key is present. Params: h - the map; key - Int key. Returns: true if key maps to a value. Complexity: O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_remove(h: &mut Hamt, key: Int)
docs.text: Remove a key. Params: h - the map; key - Int key. Absent keys are a no-op. Arena memory is retained. Complexity: O(log_32 n) expected.

docs.title: fn hamt_size(h: &Hamt) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of entries. Params: h - the map. Returns: the number of key/value pairs. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: type HashSet
docs.text:
Hash set of unique Int elements using open addressing (linear probing) with a power-of-two table. A parallel used flag vector allows every Int value (including INT_MIN) as an element. The table doubles at 50% load. Hashes are multiplicative and use shifts/multiplies plus a modulo index, so the compiler's large-Int AND bug (BUG 25 #7) is avoided. hashset_remove rebuilds the table (correct under tombstones; O(n) but simple and safe). NOTE: the API parameter type is HashSet: naming it Set collides with the xiom.collections.Set[T] generic and crashes the binary at startup (0xC0000005); the fn names and value signatures match the frozen spec.

docs.title: type IntervalTree
docs.text:
Interval tree (Int start/end, Int value). Stores [start, end] intervals and answers stabbing queries (which intervals contain a point) and range queries (which intervals overlap [start, end]) in O(log n + k) where k is the number of reported intervals. Intervals are inclusive on both ends.

Flat-arena style (the established collect/ pattern). The tree is a BST keyed by start; each node also tracks max_ends, the largest end in its subtree, which prunes subtrees that cannot intersect a query. Equal starts are inserted to the right (multi-map semantics). Removed intervals are marked dead (alive = false) and skipped by every query, so removal never disturbs the tree shape. Queries skip a subtree when its max end is below the query point (stabbing) or below the query low bound (overlap).

Field Type root Int size Int starts Vec[Int] ends Vec[Int] vals Vec[Int] left Vec[Int] right Vec[Int] max_ends Vec[Int] alive Vec[Bool]

docs.text: Values of the intervals containing point (inclusive bounds). O(log n + k) expected.

docs.title: fn interval_range_query(t: &IntervalTree, start: Int, end: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Values of the intervals overlapping [start, end] (inclusive; an interval [a, b] overlaps when a <= end and b >= start). O(log n + k) expected.

docs.title: fn interval_remove(t: &mut IntervalTree, start: Int, end: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Remove the first interval matching [start, end]. Returns true if one was found. Intervals are removed lazily (skipped by later queries). O(n) worst case.

docs.text:
Number of live intervals. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn interval_contains_point(t: &IntervalTree, point: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True if any live interval contains point. O(log n + k) expected.

docs.title: fn interval_overlaps(t: &IntervalTree, start: Int, end: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True if any live interval overlaps the range [start, end]. O(log n + k) expected.

docs.title: type IntMap
docs.text:
Optimized keyed maps. int_map uses a flat open-addressing table sized for the expected capacity (Int keys -> Int values); string_map uses a string-keyed variant. Both reject duplicate keys and iterate over stored keys in insertion order via int_map_iter.

Flat-arena style. The int_map table stores parallel keys/vals/occ/ tomb vectors of cap slots with linear probing and a multiplicative hash (high 32 bits of key * golden ratio, forced non-negative) so INT_MIN and other pathological keys are safe. Deleted slots become tombstones so probing chains stay intact; the table doubles when the load factor reaches 1/2. A separate order vector tracks the insertion order of live keys for int_map_iter. string_map is a simpler linear Vec[Str] map (strings are compared via bound locals, compiler BUG 8 workaround).

docs.title: type KdTree
docs.text:
2D k-d tree of Int points with values, supporting nearest-neighbor and rectangular range queries.

Flat-arena style (the established collect/ pattern -- tree.xi/graph.xi use parallel Vec[Int]s because Vec-of-struct instantiations collide at startup in combined programs). Node i lives in the parallel vectors xs/ys/vals plus its left/right children; the splitting axis alternates by depth (x at even depth, y at odd depth), which is re-derived during every walk so no depth field needs to be stored. Distances are squared Int distances, so no floating point is involved. kdtree_insert is an incremental insert (O(h) with h the tree height); the worst case is O(n) per insert for degenerate orders, expected O(log n).

docs.title: type LfuCache
docs.text:
Least-frequently-used cache with Int keys and values, evicting the least frequently accessed entry when full.

Flat-arena style. keys/values/counts are parallel vectors; every access bumps the entry's frequency. seq is an insertion-sequence vector used as a deterministic tie-break: when several keys share the lowest frequency, the least recently inserted one is evicted first. next_seq hands out increasing sequence numbers. lfu_get / lfu_put increase the frequency of the touched key (a get on a hit counts as an access).

docs.title: type RadixTrie
docs.text:
Compressed prefix tree over decimal digit strings mapping keys to Int values.

Flat-arena style. Every node carries the label of its incoming edge (labels[i], the empty string at the root), a terminal flag plus the stored key/value for nodes that end a key, and a child list threaded through child_head[i] / sibling[i] (linked list of child node ids). Insertion follows the classic radix-trie algorithm: match a child whose label shares a prefix with the remaining key, split that label at the divergence point, and re-link the pieces. Removal marks a terminal node non-terminal (the node itself and its labels stay, so no recompaction is needed). All string reads go through xiom.string; Vec[Str] elements are bound to locals before comparison (compiler BUG 8 workaround).

docs.title: type IntervalSet
docs.text:
Interval tree storing Int intervals with values, supporting point queries.

R44 same-leaf: the public type leaf here is IntervalSet (renamed from IntervalTree, which collided with the real tree in collect/interval.xi). Function names stay interval_*; both modules share the call surface, so always use the module you call.

Flat-arena style. Intervals are stored in insertion order in parallel Vec[Int]s (starts/ends/vals) with a parallel liveness flag alive. Point queries scan the intervals and return the values of the live intervals covering the point; removal marks the first matching interval dead (lazy deletion). This keeps the API simple and insertion/removal O(1) amortized at the cost of O(n) queries, which is appropriate for the small interval sets this module targets. Intervals are inclusive on both ends; start > end intervals are rejected by insert.

docs.text: Remove the first live interval matching [start, end]. Returns true if one was found and removed. O(n).

docs.title: type SegTree
docs.text:
Segment tree over an Int array (0-based indices). Builds in O(n), supports point updates and range queries (sum, min, max) in O(log n). Indices are inclusive; out-of-range queries return identity values (0 for sum, INT_MAX for min, INT_MIN for max).

Flat-arena style. The tree is stored in three parallel Vec[Int]s of size 4n (sums, mins, maxs) using the classic recursive heap layout: node k covers [l, r] with children 2k+1 and 2k+2. Leaves hold a single slot, internal nodes pull from their children. Out-of-range update indices are rejected (no-op); out-of-range queries are clamped and return the identity value when the clamped range is empty.

Field Type n Int sums Vec[Int] mins Vec[Int] maxs Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn segtree_query_min(t: &SegTree, l: Int, r: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Minimum over [l, r] inclusive. An empty clamped range returns INT_MAX (the min identity). O(log n).

docs.title: fn segtree_query_max(t: &SegTree, l: Int, r: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Maximum over [l, r] inclusive. An empty clamped range returns INT_MIN (the max identity). O(log n).

docs.text:

docs.text:

Classic two-array representation: sparse[value] holds the index of value inside dense, and dense holds the set members in an arbitrary but stable order. Removal swaps the last element into the removed slot, so all three core operations are O(1). The sparse array grows on demand to cover the largest inserted value; negative values cannot be indexed and are therefore rejected by sparse_add (documented, no silent failure).

docs.title: type ThreadPool
docs.text:
Thread pool. Spawns a fixed number of worker threads that drain a shared job queue. pool_submit enqueues a closure; pool_join waits for all pending jobs to finish; pool_shutdown stops the workers and releases their threads.

Pure-XIOM data structure (no OS threads): the pool tracks workers worker slots, an idle/busy split and a FIFO queue of Int job handles. Each submit hands the job to an idle worker if one is free (busy++), otherwise the handle waits in the queue; pool_join completes every pending job instantly (no real work runs) and returns all workers to idle. Submit after shutdown returns false.

Field Type workers Int idle Int busy Int queued Vec[Int] next_id Int completed Int closed Bool

docs.title: fn thread_pool_new(workers: Int) -> ThreadPool
docs.text: Create a pool with workers worker slots. Params: workers - fixed number of workers (clamped to >= 1). Returns: a new pool with all workers idle and no pending jobs. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn pool_submit(p: &mut ThreadPool, job: fn() -> Unit) -> Bool
docs.text: Enqueue a job; false if the pool is shut down. Params: p - the pool; job - a closure (accepted but not executed; the pool is a pure-XIOM simulation over Int job handles). Returns: true on acceptance, false if the pool is shut down. Complexity: O(1) amortized.

docs.title: fn pool_join(p: &mut ThreadPool)
docs.text: Wait until all submitted jobs have completed. Params: p - the pool. Completes every queued job (they finish immediately in the simulation) and returns all workers to the idle state. Complexity: O(n) where n is the number of pending jobs.

docs.title: fn pool_shutdown(p: &mut ThreadPool)
docs.text: Stop workers and release threads. Params: p - the pool. Closes the pool (submit returns false afterwards) and drains the pending queue as pool_join does. Complexity: O(n) where n is the number of pending jobs.

docs.title: fn pool_size(p: &ThreadPool) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of worker threads. Params: p - the pool. Returns: the fixed worker count. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn pool_idle_count(p: &ThreadPool) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of workers currently idle. Params: p - the pool. Returns: workers not currently assigned a job. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn pool_busy_count(p: &ThreadPool) -> Int
docs.text:
Number of workers currently running a job. Params: p - the pool. Returns: workers currently assigned a job (does not include queued work). Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.text:

docs.title: type Trie
docs.text:
Trie (Str keys, lowercase a-z only; other chars are rejected) Flat-arena style (the established collect/ pattern -- tree.xi/graph.xi use parallel Vec[Int]s because Vec-of-struct instantiations collide at startup in combined programs, COMPILER_BUGS.md BUG 16). Node n's child for letter c is children[n * 26 + c] (-1 = none); ends[n] is 1 for a complete word. trie_complete returns all words with a prefix, in DFS lexicographic order. Node 0 is the root.

docs.title: type UnionFind
docs.text:
Disjoint-set (union-find) over Int element ids with path compression and union by size.

Flat-arena style: parent[i] points at the parent of element i (a root points at itself), size[i] is the component size valid at the roots, and count tracks the number of disjoint sets. uf_find applies path compression (both passes) and takes &mut; the immutable read-only traversal uf_find_no_compress backs uf_connected / uf_component_size / uf_components so they accept &UnionFind. Union by size keeps trees shallow, giving ~O(alpha n) amortized operations. Out-of-range element ids are rejected (no silent failure).

Field Type parent Vec[Int] size Vec[Int] count Int

docs.text: LZ77 compression using a simple sliding-window search. Emits tokens as flat triples in a Vec[Int]: [literal_len, match_offset, match_length, ...]. A match_offset of 0 means no match found; literal_len bytes follow directly. Window size limits the backward search distance. Complexity: O(n * window), n = data length.

docs.title: fn lz77_decompress(tokens: &Vec[Int]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: LZ77 decompression of token triples produced by lz77_compress. Each triple: [literal_len, data, match_length_or_zero]. If literal_len == 0: data = match_offset, third = match_length. If literal_len == 1: data = literal byte, third = 0. Complexity: O(t), t = number of tokens.

docs.title: fn rle_encode_bytes(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Simple byte-level run-length encoding. Format: [count: UInt8, byte: UInt8] for runs of identical bytes. Count represents the number of repetitions (1 means 1 byte). Differs from rle_encode which uses control-byte format with bit 7 markers. Complexity: O(n), n = data length.

docs.title: fn huffman_freqs(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[Int]

docs.text: level 0 => STORED blocks (real, uncompressed); levels 1-9 => FIXED Huffman blocks.

docs.title: fn deflate_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]

docs.title: fn deflate_bound(len: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Worst-case compressed size for len input bytes under the fixed-Huffman encoder: per byte at most 9 code bits + headers + match overhead is always below this bound. O(1).

docs.title: fn deflate_compress_stream(reader: Int, writer: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Stream-compress between two file descriptors: reads all bytes from reader, compresses them, writes the container to writer, and returns the number of bytes written. Errors (empty input, read/write failures) are returned as Err.

docs.title: fn gzip_crc32(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> UInt32
docs.text: Compute the CRC-32 checksum (IEEE 802.3 polynomial) of data. O(n).

docs.title: fn gzip_header_new(mtime: Int, os: Int) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Build a bare gzip header: magic (1F 8B), method (08), flags (00), MTIME (mtime, LE, may be 0), XFL (00) and OS (os, masked to 8 bits; use 255 for unknown, 3 for Unix). Returns 10 bytes.

docs.title: fn gzip_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Wrap data in a gzip stream: header (mtime 0, OS 255) + DEFLATE payload + CRC32 trailer + ISIZE trailer.

docs.title: fn gzip_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Unwrap and validate a gzip stream. Parses the optional header fields, decompresses the payload, and verifies the CRC32 and ISIZE trailer values. Returns Err on any mismatch or malformed input.

docs.title: fn gzip_decompress_capped(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_out: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress with a hard ceiling on output size (decompression-bomb guard). The header's declared ISIZE is rejected up-front when it exceeds the cap; the payload cap is enforced inside the deflate stages.

docs.title: fn gzip_compress_file(path: Str) -> Result[Unit, Str]
docs.text: Gzip a file to <path>.gz. Returns Err when the source cannot be read or the target cannot be written.

docs.title: fn gzip_decompress_file(path: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Gunzip a file into raw bytes. Returns Err on read failures or invalid gzip data.

docs.title: fn gzip_validate(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool

docs.title: type HuffmanTree
docs.text:
Huffman tree: per-symbol code lengths and canonical codes (index = byte value).

Field Type code_lengths Vec[Int] codes Vec[Int] max_len Int

docs.title: fn huffman_canonical(codelengths: &Vec[Int]) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Derive the canonical prefix-free codes from per-symbol code lengths. Canonical order: shorter codes first, ties by symbol index. O(256).

docs.title: fn huffman_build(frequencies: &Vec[Int]) -> HuffmanTree
docs.text: Build a Huffman tree from a 256-slot frequency table (index = byte value). The tree holds per-symbol code lengths and canonical codes. Empty or single-symbol inputs are handled (single symbol gets length 1). Complexity: O(n^2) in the number of distinct symbols (<= 256).

docs.title: fn huffman_code_lengths(tree: HuffmanTree) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Extract the per-symbol code lengths as a fresh 256-slot Vec[Int].

docs.title: fn huffman_table_new(codelengths: &Vec[Int]) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Pack a flat canonical decode table: entries [0..255] are the canonical codes, entries [256..511] are the matching code lengths. O(512).

docs.title: fn huffman_encode_symbol(tree: HuffmanTree, sym: Int) -> Vec[Bool]
docs.text: Return the code bits of one symbol as booleans, MSB first. An uncovered symbol yields an empty Vec (documented).

docs.title: fn huffman_encode(tree: HuffmanTree, data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Pack data into an MSB-first bit stream using the tree's codes. O(n * avg code length). Requires the tree to cover every input byte.

docs.title: fn huffman_decode(tree: HuffmanTree, bits: &Vec[UInt8], len: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decode exactly len bits of the MSB-first stream back into bytes. Returns Err on invalid bit patterns or stream exhaustion.

docs.title: fn huffman_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: One-shot Huffman compression: builds the frequency table and tree, packs the bits, and emits the self-describing container (header documented at the top of this module). Empty input yields a valid empty container.

docs.title: fn huffman_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress Huffman-coded data; Err on malformed input.

docs.title: fn huffman_decompress_capped(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_out: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress with a hard ceiling on output size. The container's declared length is rejected up-front when it exceeds the cap; the decode loop re-checks per symbol, so a lying header cannot allocate past the cap.

docs.title: fn rle_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Byte-level run-length encoding: [count: UInt8, byte: UInt8] pairs for runs of identical bytes (count 1..255; runs longer than 255 split). Complexity: O(n), n = data length.

docs.title: fn rle_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Undo byte-level run-length encoding (rle_compress format). Returns Err on a truncated pair (odd trailing byte) or a zero count.

docs.title: fn lz4_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Compress data into a full frame (magic, FLG/BD, block size, payload).

docs.title: fn lz4_compress_frame(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Alias for lz4_compress: the frame IS the full container in this module.

docs.text: Compress data into a frame using the high-compression block encoder.

docs.title: fn lz4_bound(len: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Worst-case compressed size for len input bytes (literals expand by at most 1 byte per 255 input bytes plus token/header overhead). O(1).

docs.title: fn lz4_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress an LZ4 block; Err on malformed input.

docs.title: fn lz4_decompress_capped(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_out: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress with a hard ceiling on total output size (bomb guard). Checked after each block's expansion.

docs.title: fn lz4_decompress_frame(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Alias for lz4_decompress: parses and decompresses an lz4_compress frame.

docs.title: fn lz4_compress_block(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Compress a raw block payload (no frame header) using the LZ4 block format. Greedy search with a 4KiB window; matches need length >= 4. Complexity: O(n * 4096).

docs.title: fn lz4_compress_hc_block(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: High-compression block variant: 64KiB search window, longer match scan. Uses the same block format, so lz4_decompress_block decodes either output.

docs.title: fn lz4_decompress_block(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress a raw LZ4 block. Returns Err on truncation, an invalid offset, or malformed extended lengths.

docs.title: fn lz77_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Compress data with a greedy 32KiB sliding-window search into the control-byte token stream documented above. O(n * 32768).

docs.title: fn lz77_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress LZ77 data; Err on malformed input.

docs.title: fn lz77_decompress_capped(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_out: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress with a hard ceiling on output size. Every expansion step is checked BEFORE writing, so a hostile token stream cannot allocate beyond the cap even momentarily. Returns Err("lz77: output exceeds cap") when exceeded.

docs.title: fn lz77_find_longest_match(data: &Vec[UInt8], pos: Int, window: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Locate the longest match for the byte at pos searching back at most window positions. Returns (length, distance); (0, 0) when no match of length >= 3 exists. Out-of-range positions yield (0, 0). Complexity: O(window * match_length).

docs.title: fn lz77_token_encode(length: Int, distance: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Pack a (length, distance) pair into a single token: (length << 16) | distance. Both fields are clamped to 16 bits (0..65535). Pure-Int token.

docs.title: fn lz77_token_decode(token: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Unpack a token produced by lz77_token_encode into (length, distance).

docs.title: fn snappy_uncompressed_len(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Int, Str]

docs.title: fn snappy_max_compressed_len(len: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Upper bound on the compressed size of len input bytes (varint + up to 1/6 expansion for incompressible data). O(1).

docs.title: fn snappy_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Compress data into a raw snappy stream (varint length + elements). Greedy matches with a 4KiB window; literals batch until a match is found. Complexity: O(n * 4096).

docs.title: fn snappy_decompress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress Snappy data; Err on malformed input.

docs.title: fn snappy_decompress_capped(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_out: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress with a hard ceiling on output size (bomb guard). The varint-declared length is rejected up-front when it exceeds the cap; every literal/copy element re-checks before writing.

docs.title: fn snappy_compress_frame(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Compress data into a framed stream: varint(compressed payload length) followed by the raw snappy stream (which itself starts with the varint uncompressed length). The frame is self-delimiting.

docs.title: fn snappy_decompress_frame(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decompress a snappy_compress_frame stream. Validates the outer varint against the remaining bytes. Returns Err on any mismatch or malformed data.

docs.title: fn zlib_header_new(level: Int) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Build the CMF/FLG header bytes for a level (0-9, clamped). Returns 2 bytes.

docs.title: fn zlib_adler32(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> UInt32
docs.text: Compute the Adler-32 checksum of data. O(n).

docs.title: fn zlib_compress(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]

docs.title: fn zlib_compress_level(data: &Vec[UInt8], level: Int) -> Vec[UInt8]

docs.text: Sanity-check the zlib header (method and CMF/FLG checksum). O(1).

docs.title: fn atoi(s: Str) -> Int
docs.text: Parses a decimal integer, returning zero on failure. C atoi semantics: leading whitespace is skipped, an optional sign is accepted, and parsing stops at the first non-digit. Overflow clamps to INT_MAX/INT_MIN. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn atoi_radix(s: Str, radix: Int) -> Int

docs.title: fn atoi_or(s: Str, default: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Parses a decimal integer with a fallback value: returns default when no digits can be parsed (a genuine "0" still returns 0). Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn to_base58(value: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Converts an integer to its base58 representation ("123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQ RSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz"). 0 yields "1"; negatives get a "-" prefix. Delegates to xiom.num.convert.to_base58 for every value except INT_MIN, whose exact magnitude rendering is pinned here (num's negation overflows). Complexity: O(log_58 n).

docs.title: fn from_base58(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parses a base58 string into an Int. An optional leading '-'/'+' is accepted. Returns Err on an empty string, an invalid character, or overflow. Negative magnitudes accumulate in signed space, so INT_MIN round-trips exactly. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn base58_encode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encodes bytes as a base58 string (big-endian base-256 value written in base 58). Leading zero bytes produce leading '1' characters, matching the Bitcoin convention. Empty input yields "". Complexity: O(n^2) worst case (per-byte long division), O(n * log_58(2^8n)) typical.

docs.title: fn base58_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decodes a base58 string back into bytes. Leading '1' characters map back to leading zero bytes. Returns Err on an invalid character. Empty input yields an empty byte vector. Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.

docs.title: fn base58check_encode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encodes bytes as base58 with a trailing 4-byte checksum, matching the base58check shape. FALLBACK: the checksum is Adler-32, not double-SHA256 (see the TODO(compiler) note) -- the output is NOT Bitcoin-interoperable. Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.

docs.title: fn base58check_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decodes and verifies a base58check string. The trailing 4-byte checksum is recomputed and compared; returns Err on invalid base58, truncated data, or a checksum mismatch. FALLBACK checksum: Adler-32 (see base58check_encode). Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.

docs.title: fn to_base62(value: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Converts an integer to its base62 representation ("0-9A-Za-z"). 0 yields "0"; negatives get a "-" prefix. INT_MIN is rendered exactly via negative- digit extraction. Complexity: O(log_62 n).

docs.title: fn from_base62(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parses a base62 string into an Int. An optional leading '-'/'+' is accepted. Returns Err on an empty string, an invalid character, or overflow. Negative magnitudes accumulate in signed space, so INT_MIN round-trips exactly. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn base62_encode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encodes bytes as a base62 string (big-endian base-256 value written in base 62). Leading zero bytes produce leading '0' characters. Empty input yields "". Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.

docs.title: fn base62_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decodes a base62 string back into bytes. Leading '0' characters map back to leading zero bytes. Returns Err on an invalid character. Empty input yields an empty byte vector. Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.
