docs.text: Duplicate a C string and return the new pointer. Parameters: ptr -- the address of the source C string. Returns: a malloc'd copy the caller must free. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn date_new(year: Int, month: Int, day: Int) -> Date
docs.text: Build a calendar date from year, month and day. No validation is performed (out-of-range fields are carried as-is by the Date type). Parameters: year (proleptic Gregorian), month 1..12, day 1..31. Returns: the constructed Date. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_now() -> Date
docs.text: The current calendar date, computed from the Unix clock. Returns: today's Date (UTC). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_iso8601(d: &Date) -> Str
docs.text: Format a date as ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DD", zero-padded. Parameters: d -- the date to format. Returns: the formatted string (always 10 bytes). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_from_iso8601(s: Str) -> Option[Date]
docs.text: Parse an ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DD" string into a Date. Parameters: s -- the date string. Returns: Some(Date) when well-formed and within calendar range, None otherwise (malformed layout or out-of-range fields). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_weekday(d: &Date) -> Int
docs.text: Day of the week for a date: 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday. Parameters: d -- the date. Returns: weekday index. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_day_of_year(d: &Date) -> Int
docs.text: Ordinal day of the year for a date (1..366, leap-aware). Parameters: d -- the date. Returns: the day-of-year index. Complexity: O(month) in the worst case (small constant).

docs.title: fn datetime_new(year: Int, month: Int, day: Int, hour: Int, minute: Int, second: Int) -> DateTime
docs.text: Build a date-time value from its calendar and clock fields. Parameters: year, month, day, hour, minute, second (24-hour clock). Returns: a DateTime whose weekday is computed from the calendar date. No range validation is performed. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn datetime_now() -> DateTime
docs.text: The current date-time value (UTC clock). Returns: a DateTime for the current instant. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn datetime_iso8601(dt: &DateTime) -> Str
docs.text: Format a date-time as ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS", zero-padded. Parameters: dt -- the date-time value. Returns: the formatted string (always 19 bytes). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn datetime_from_iso8601(s: Str) -> Option[DateTime]
docs.text: Parse an ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" string into a DateTime. Parameters: s -- the date-time string. Returns: Some(DateTime) when well-formed and within range, None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_seconds(n: Int) -> Duration
docs.text: Build a Duration from whole seconds. Parameters: n -- the number of seconds (may be negative). Returns: a normalized Duration (nanos in [0, 1e9)). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_millis(n: Int) -> Duration
docs.text: Build a Duration from whole milliseconds. Parameters: n -- the number of milliseconds (may be negative). Returns: a normalized Duration. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_micros(n: Int) -> Duration
docs.text: Build a Duration from whole microseconds. Parameters: n -- the number of microseconds (may be negative). Returns: a normalized Duration. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_nanos(n: Int) -> Duration
docs.text: Build a Duration from whole nanoseconds. Parameters: n -- the number of nanoseconds (may be negative). Returns: a normalized Duration. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_as_secs(d: Duration) -> Int
docs.text: Whole seconds contained in a Duration. Parameters: d -- the duration. Returns: the seconds field (sub-second parts dropped). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn duration_as_ms(d: Duration) -> Int
docs.text: Whole milliseconds contained in a Duration. Parameters: d -- the duration. Returns: the total milliseconds (sub-millisecond parts dropped). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_be_bytes(n: Int) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Big-endian byte representation of an integer (exactly 8 bytes, MSB first). Negative values render as their two's-complement pattern. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_le_bytes(n: Int) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Little-endian byte representation of an integer (exactly 8 bytes, LSB first). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_be_bytes(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Int
docs.text: Integer read from big-endian bytes. Reads at most 8 bytes; returns 0 for an empty vector or more than 8 bytes. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn from_le_bytes(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Int
docs.text: Integer read from little-endian bytes. Reads at most 8 bytes; returns 0 for an empty vector or more than 8 bytes. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn swap_bytes(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Reverses the byte order of an integer (all 8 bytes). Delegates to the canonical xiom.bits.byte_swap64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn is_little_endian() -> Bool
docs.text: Reports the host byte order. The supported x86-64 targets are little-endian, so this returns true. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn html_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape text for HTML body content: & < > " ' become entities. Parameters: s -- the input text. Returns: the escaped text (strictly longer unless no specials). Complexity: O(n), n = input length.

docs.title: fn html_unescape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Decode HTML entities back to characters: the named set (& < > " ' ') and numeric forms (&#NN; decimal, &#xHH; hex). Parameters: s -- the escaped text. Returns: the decoded text; unrecognized sequences pass through. Complexity: O(n), n = input length.

docs.title: fn html_escape_attr(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape text for use inside HTML attribute quotes: same entity set as html_escape plus both quote characters are always escaped. Parameters: s -- the attribute value text. Returns: the escaped text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn xml_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape the five predefined XML entities: & " ' < >. Parameters: s -- the input text. Returns: the escaped text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn xml_unescape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Decode the predefined XML entities back to characters. Parameters: s -- the escaped text. Returns: the decoded text; unrecognized sequences pass through. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn csv_escape_field(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape and quote a field for RFC 4180 CSV output: the field is quoted when it contains a comma, quote, CR or LF, and embedded quotes are doubled. Parameters: s -- the raw field value. Returns: the CSV-ready field. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn csv_unescape_field(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Parse and unquote a single CSV field: a quoted field is unquoted and doubled quotes are restored; unquoted fields pass through unchanged. Parameters: s -- a single CSV field (no separators). Returns: the raw field value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn tsv_escape_field(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape tab, CR and LF characters in a TSV field as \t, \r, \n. Parameters: s -- the raw field value. Returns: the escaped field. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn tsv_unescape_field(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Restore tab, CR and LF escapes in a TSV field. Parameters: s -- the escaped field. Returns: the raw field value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn regex_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape regex metacharacters in a literal string with a backslash. Escapes: \ . ^ $ * + ? ( ) [ ] { } |. Parameters: s -- the literal text. Returns: the regex-safe text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn glob_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape glob wildcard metacharacters (* ? [ ] and backslash) in a literal string with a backslash. Parameters: s -- the literal text. Returns: the glob-safe text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn glob_unescape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Restore escaped glob metacharacters: a backslash before a glob character is removed. Parameters: s -- the escaped text. Returns: the literal text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn shell_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape a string for safe use in a POSIX shell command: every character outside the safe set (alphanumerics plus _ - . / , : @ % + =) is preceded by a backslash. Parameters: s -- the raw argument. Returns: the shell-escaped argument. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn shell_quote(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Quote a string with single quotes for a POSIX shell; embedded single quotes are closed, escaped and reopened ('\''). Parameters: s -- the raw argument. Returns: the single-quoted argument. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn cmd_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape a string for safe use in a Windows cmd command line: ^ & | < > ( ) " % are escaped with a caret. Parameters: s -- the raw argument. Returns: the cmd-escaped argument. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn cmd_quote(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Quote a string for a Windows cmd command line: wrap in double quotes and double any embedded quote characters. Parameters: s -- the raw argument. Returns: the double-quoted argument. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn exact_div(a: Int, b: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: a / b, returning Err on division by zero, the INT_MIN / -1 overflow, or a non-exact quotient. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn exact_float(a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: a / b in IEEE arithmetic, returning None on division by zero or when the quotient does not round-trip (q * b != a), i.e. when the division lost precision. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn exact_ratio(a: Int, b: Int) -> Option[(Int, Int)]
docs.text: Reduces a/b to lowest terms as (numerator, denominator) with a positive denominator. Returns None on division by zero. Complexity: O(log max|a,b|).

docs.title: fn float_to_string(f: Float64) -> Str
docs.text: Format a float with 15 significant digits: fixed notation for 1e-4 <= |f| < 1e15, scientific otherwise (C %.15g semantics with trailing zeros stripped). Handles "nan"/"inf". Parameters: f -- the float value. Returns: the formatted string. Complexity: O(|exp10| + 15).

docs.title: fn string_to_float(s: Str) -> Result[Float64, Str]
docs.text: Parse a string to a float. Parameters: s -- the decimal float string (optional sign, '.', 'e'/'E'). Returns: Ok(Float64) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn float_to_fixed_str(f: Float64, decimals: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format a float in fixed-point notation with exactly decimals fraction digits (rounded half away from zero). Handles "nan"/"inf". Parameters: f -- the float value; decimals -- the fraction digit count. Returns: the formatted string. Complexity: O(decimals).

docs.title: fn float_to_sci_str(f: Float64, decimals: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format a float in scientific notation "d.ddde+/-XX" with decimals fraction digits (rounded half away from zero). Handles "nan"/"inf". Parameters: f -- the float value; decimals -- the fraction digit count. Returns: the formatted string. Complexity: O(|exp10| + decimals).

docs.title: fn float_to_int(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncate a float to an integer (toward zero). Parameters: f -- the float value. Returns: the truncated integer. Behavior for NaN/out-of-range input is undefined (use checked variants elsewhere). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_to_float(n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Widen an integer to a float (exact up to 2^53). Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: n widened to Float64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_int(n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Widen an integer to a float (exact up to 2^53). Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: n widened to Float64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_float(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncate a float toward zero to an integer. Parameters: f -- the float value. Returns: the truncated integer. Behavior for NaN/out-of-range input is undefined (use the checked variants elsewhere). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_char(c: Char) -> Int
docs.text: Return a character's code point as an integer. Parameters: c -- the character. Returns: the Unicode code point of c. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_bool(b: Bool) -> Int
docs.text: Render a boolean as 0 or 1. Parameters: b -- the boolean. Returns: 1 when true, 0 when false. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn from_str_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse a string as an integer. Parameters: s -- the decimal integer string (optional sign). Returns: Ok(Int) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn from_str_float(s: Str) -> Result[Float64, Str]
docs.text: Parse a string as a float. Parameters: s -- the decimal float string (optional sign, '.', 'e'/'E'). Returns: Ok(Float64) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn from_str_bool(s: Str) -> Option[Bool]
docs.text: Parse a string as a boolean. Parameters: s -- the string. Returns: Some(true) for "true", Some(false) for "false" (exact, case sensitive), None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn ftos(f: Float64) -> Str
docs.text: Float-to-string shorthand: 15 significant digits in the canonical fixed / scientific layout. Handles "nan" and "inf". Complexity: O(|exp10| + 15).

docs.title: fn ftos_prec(f: Float64, prec: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Float-to-string with exactly prec fraction digits (fixed notation, rounded half away from zero). Complexity: O(prec).

docs.title: fn ftos_sci(f: Float64, prec: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Float-to-string in scientific notation "d.ddde+/-XX" with prec fraction digits. Complexity: O(|exp10| + prec).

docs.title: fn int_to_string(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format an integer as a decimal string. Exact for the full Int range (including INT_MIN). Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: the decimal representation. Complexity: O(log_10 |n|).

docs.title: fn string_to_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse a decimal string to an integer. Parameters: s -- the decimal integer string (optional sign). Returns: Ok(Int) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn int_to_base(n: Int, base: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format an integer in an arbitrary base (2-36, lowercase digits). Parameters: n -- the integer value; base -- the radix. Returns: the base representation; "" for an invalid radix. Complexity: O(log_base |n|).

docs.title: fn base_to_int(s: Str, base: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse an integer string in an arbitrary base (2-36, both digit cases). Parameters: s -- the digit string (optional sign); base -- the radix. Returns: Ok(Int) for well-formed input, Err for an invalid radix, an empty string, an out-of-range digit, or overflow. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn int_to_hex(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format an integer as a lowercase hexadecimal string. Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: the hexadecimal representation ("0" for zero). Complexity: O(log_16 |n|).

docs.title: fn int_from_hex(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse a hexadecimal string to an integer. Parameters: s -- the hex digit string (both digit cases accepted). Returns: Ok(Int) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn int_to_octal(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format an integer as a lowercase octal string. Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: the octal representation ("0" for zero). Complexity: O(log_8 |n|).

docs.title: fn int_to_binary(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Format an integer as a binary string. Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: the binary representation ("0" for zero). Complexity: O(log_2 |n|).

docs.title: fn into_int(n: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncate a float toward zero to an integer. Parameters: n -- the float value. Returns: the truncated integer. Behavior for NaN/out-of-range input is undefined (use the checked variants elsewhere). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn into_float(n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Widen an integer to a float (exact up to 2^53). Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: n widened to Float64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn into_str[T](v: T) -> Str
docs.text: Convert a generic value to a string via its Display to_str implementation. Parameters: v -- the value to render. Returns: the value's to_str() representation. Complexity: O(1) for primitives.

docs.title: fn is_valid_ipv4(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is a valid IPv4 address. Parameters: s -- the candidate address. Returns: true for a dotted-quad with four octets in 0..255. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn is_valid_ipv6(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is a valid IPv6 address (with optional "::" compression; IPv4-mapped forms are not accepted). Parameters: s -- the candidate address. Returns: true for a well-formed IPv6 address. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn ipv4_to_string(octets: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Format four octets as a dotted IPv4 address. Parameters: octets -- at least four octets (only the first four are used). Returns: the "a.b.c.d" representation. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn string_to_ipv4(s: Str) -> Option[Vec[UInt8]]
docs.text: Parse a dotted IPv4 address into four octets. Parameters: s -- the address string. Returns: Some(four octets) for a valid address, None otherwise. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn ip_parse(s: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: Parse an IP address, returning its canonical text form (IPv4 dotted-quad or IPv6 with "::" compression). Parameters: s -- the address string. Returns: Some(canonical) for a valid address, None otherwise. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn ip_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Option[Vec[UInt8]]
docs.text: Parse an IP address into its raw bytes (4 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6). Parameters: s -- the address string. Returns: Some(bytes) for a valid address, None otherwise. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: type Iri
docs.text:
Iri -- parsed IRI components.

Field Type scheme Str authority Str path Str query Str fragment Str

docs.title: fn iri_parse(s: Str) -> Result[Iri, Str]
docs.text: Parse an IRI into its scheme, authority, path, query and fragment. Parameters: s -- the IRI string (non-ASCII characters allowed). Returns: Ok(Iri) on success; Err for an empty IRI. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn iri_to_uri(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Convert an IRI to an ASCII-only URI by percent-encoding every byte >= 0x80 in the authority, path, query and fragment. Parameters: s -- the IRI string. Returns: Ok(URI) on success; Err for an empty IRI. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn iri_normalize(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Normalize an IRI into canonical form (lowercase scheme, non-ASCII bytes percent-encoded in place). Parameters: s -- the IRI string. Returns: Ok(canonical) on success; Err for an empty IRI. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn itos(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Integer-to-string shorthand (decimal). Complexity: O(log_10 |n|).

docs.title: fn itos_padded(n: Int, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Integer-to-string with zero padding to width characters (printf %0Nd style: the sign, if any, precedes the padding). Widths smaller than the digit count are ignored. Complexity: O(width).

docs.title: fn itos_signed(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Integer-to-string with an explicit sign: positive values get a '+' prefix; zero and negative values render normally. Complexity: O(log_10 n).

docs.title: fn json_escape(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Escape a string for embedding in JSON (without surrounding quotes). Handles ", \, \n, \r, \t, \b, \f. Parameters: s -- the raw text. Returns: the escaped text. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn json_unescape(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Unescape a JSON string literal (without surrounding quotes). Handles \, \", \/, \b, \f, \n, \r, \t, and \uNNNN. Parameters: s -- the escaped text. Returns: Ok(text) on success; Err on an invalid escape or a truncated \u sequence. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn json_quote(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Wrap a string in JSON quotes with escaping. Parameters: s -- the raw text. Returns: the quoted, escaped JSON string literal. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn json_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is valid JSON (a single top-level value). Parameters: s -- the candidate JSON text. Returns: true when the whole input parses as one JSON value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn json_pretty(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Pretty-print a JSON string with 2-space indentation. Parameters: s -- the minified JSON text. Returns: Ok(pretty) on success; Err for invalid JSON (unterminated string or unbalanced brackets). Complexity: O(n), n = input length.

docs.title: fn lossy_from_str(s: Str) -> Int
docs.text: Parses a decimal integer string. Returns 0 on malformed input (empty, invalid characters) and clamps to INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow -- the function never fails. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn lossy_from_float(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncates a float toward zero, clamping to INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. NaN yields 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn lossy_to_float(s: Str) -> Float64
docs.text: Parses a floating-point string, returning 0.0 on any parse failure. Supports optional sign, decimal point, and 'e'/'E' exponent. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn lossy_char(s: Str) -> Char
docs.text: Returns the first character of s, or '\0' (the null character) when the string is empty. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mac_parse(s: Str) -> Option[Vec[UInt8]]
docs.text: Parse a MAC address into six octets. Parameters: s -- a MAC address using ':' or '-' separators (e.g. "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff" or "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"). Returns: Some(six octets) for a well-formed address, None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mac_to_string(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Format six octets as a colon-separated lowercase MAC address. Parameters: bytes -- at least six octets (only the first six are used). Returns: the "xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx" representation. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mac_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is a valid MAC address (six hex octets, ':' or '-' separators). Parameters: s -- the candidate string. Returns: true when well-formed. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mac_random() -> Str
docs.text: Generate a random MAC address string (locally administered, unicast). Returns: a 17-character MAC address. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn host_to_network16(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 16-bit host-order value to network order (big-endian). Parameters: n -- a 16-bit value (0..65535). Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn host_to_network32(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 32-bit host-order value to network order (big-endian). Parameters: n -- a 32-bit value. Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn network_to_host16(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 16-bit network-order value to host order (little-endian). Parameters: n -- a 16-bit network-order value. Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn network_to_host32(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 32-bit network-order value to host order (little-endian). Parameters: n -- a 32-bit network-order value. Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn htonll(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 64-bit host-order value to network order (big-endian). Parameters: n -- a 64-bit value. Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn ntohll(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a 64-bit network-order value to host order (little-endian). Parameters: n -- a 64-bit network-order value. Returns: the byte-swapped value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn overflowing_add(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Bool)
docs.text: a + b, returning (wrapped_value, overflowed). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn overflowing_sub(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Bool)
docs.text: a - b, returning (wrapped_value, overflowed). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn overflowing_mul(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Bool)
docs.text: a * b, returning (wrapped_value, overflowed). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn overflowing_neg(a: Int) -> (Int, Bool)
docs.text: -a, returning (wrapped_value, overflowed). INT_MIN negates to itself. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn parse_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parses a decimal integer string. An optional leading '-'/'+' is accepted. Returns Err on an empty string, an invalid character, or overflow. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn parse_int_radix(s: Str, radix: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parses an integer string in the given radix (2-36, both digit cases accepted). An optional leading '-'/'+' is accepted. Returns Err on an invalid radix, an empty string, an invalid digit, a digit out of range for the radix, or overflow. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn parse_float(s: Str) -> Result[Float64, Str]
docs.text: Parses a floating-point string. Supports an optional sign, a decimal point, and an 'e'/'E' exponent. Returns Err on empty input, missing digits, invalid characters, multiple decimal points, or a malformed exponent. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn parse_bool(s: Str) -> Option[Bool]
docs.text: Parses "true" or "false" (exact, case-sensitive). Returns None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn parse_char(s: Str) -> Option[Char]
docs.text: Returns the first character of a single-character string. Returns None for an empty string or a multi-character string (documented: this helper parses exactly one character). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn percent_encode(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Percent-encodes a full URL string. Reserved separators ('/', ':', '?', '&', '=', '+', '#', '@', etc.) pass through; all other non-unreserved characters are percent-encoded per UTF-8 byte. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn percent_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Percent-decodes a URL string: '%XX' escapes are decoded; '+' is left as a literal '+'. Returns Err on a truncated or malformed escape. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn percent_encode_component(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Percent-encodes a single URL component (path segment / query value): only unreserved characters (A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~) pass through; everything else -- including '/', '?', '&', '=', ':' -- is percent-encoded per UTF-8 byte. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn percent_decode_component(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Percent-decodes a URL component: '%XX' escapes are decoded and '+' is converted to a space (application/x-www-form-urlencoded semantics). Returns Err on a truncated or malformed escape. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn punycode_encode(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Encode a Unicode label to Punycode (with the "xn--" prefix). Parameters: s -- the Unicode label (no dots). Returns: Ok("xn--...") for a label with non-ASCII code points; Ok(s) unchanged when the label is entirely ASCII. Complexity: O(n^2) worst case, O(n) typical.

docs.title: fn punycode_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode a Punycode label to Unicode. Parameters: s -- the label; "xn--" prefixed labels are decoded, plain ASCII labels pass through unchanged. Returns: Ok(Unicode label) on success; Err on malformed input. Complexity: O(n^2) worst case.

docs.title: fn punycode_encode_domain(domain: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Encode each label of a full domain to Punycode. Parameters: domain -- a dotted domain (labels separated by '.'). Returns: Ok(encoded domain) on success; Err for an empty label. Complexity: O(n) labels x encode cost.

docs.title: fn punycode_decode_domain(domain: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode each label of an A-label domain to Unicode. Parameters: domain -- a dotted domain. Returns: Ok(Unicode domain) on success; Err for a malformed label. Complexity: O(n) labels x decode cost.

docs.title: fn idna_to_ascii(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Convert an internationalized domain to its ASCII A-label form. Parameters: s -- the Unicode domain. Returns: Ok(A-label domain) on success; Err for invalid input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn idna_to_unicode(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Convert an ASCII A-label domain to its Unicode U-label form. Parameters: s -- the A-label domain. Returns: Ok(U-label domain) on success; Err for invalid input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn idna_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Report whether a domain conforms to IDNA requirements. Parameters: s -- the candidate domain (A-label or U-label). Returns: true when every label is a valid IDNA label. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn idna_uts46_normalize(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Apply UTS-46 mapping and normalization to a domain string: case folding (lowercasing) plus IDNA character validation. Parameters: s -- the raw domain. Returns: Ok(normalized) on success; Err when an invalid character remains. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_encode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encode bytes to Quoted-Printable with default 76-column lines. Parameters: data -- the raw bytes. Returns: the QP-encoded text (ASCII). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_encode_maxline(data: &Vec[UInt8], max_line: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Encode bytes to Quoted-Printable using a custom maximum line width. Parameters: data -- the raw bytes; max_line -- the target column limit. Returns: the QP-encoded text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decode a Quoted-Printable string to bytes. Parameters: s -- the QP-encoded text. Returns: Ok(bytes) on success; Err for a truncated or invalid =HH escape. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_soft_linebreak(s: Str, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Insert soft line breaks (=CRLF) into already-encoded text. Parameters: s -- the encoded text; width -- the maximum line width. Returns: the re-wrapped text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_is_binary(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Report whether the string is too binary for safe Quoted-Printable use (contains NUL or more than a third of its bytes are control bytes). Parameters: s -- the candidate text. Returns: true when the content is too binary. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn qp_escape_byte(b: UInt8) -> Str
docs.text: Return the =HH escape for a single byte. Parameters: b -- the byte. Returns: a three-character "=HH" string (uppercase hex). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn roundtrip_int(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff s is a canonical decimal integer: parsing it succeeds and formatting the result reproduces s exactly. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn roundtrip_float(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff parsing s, formatting canonically, and re-parsing yields the same value (the value is stable under the canonical float formatter). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn roundtrip_fixed(f: Float64, decimals: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff formatting f with exactly decimals fraction digits and parsing the result back reproduces f. Complexity: O(decimals).

docs.title: fn roundtrip_base(n: Int, base: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff formatting n in the given base and parsing it back reproduces n. Returns false for an invalid base (2-36 required). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn saturating_add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a + b, clamping at INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn saturating_sub(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a - b, clamping at INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn saturating_mul(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a * b, clamping at INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn saturating_abs(a: Int) -> Int
docs.text: |a|, clamping to INT_MAX when a == INT_MIN (no positive representation). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn saturating_pow(a: Int, e: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a^e via square-and-multiply, clamping at INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. Negative exponents yield 1 (documented). Complexity: O(log e).

docs.title: fn strftime(spec: Str, d: &Date) -> Str
docs.text: Format a date using a strftime specifier. Parameters: spec -- the format string; d -- the date. Returns: the formatted string. Unknown conversions pass through literally. Complexity: O(|spec|).

docs.title: fn strftime_now(spec: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Format the current date using a strftime specifier. Parameters: spec -- the format string. Returns: the formatted string for today's date. Complexity: O(|spec|).

docs.title: fn strptime(s: Str, spec: Str) -> DateParse
docs.text: Parse a string with a strptime specifier. Parameters: s -- the input string; spec -- the format string. Returns: a DateParse whose is_ok is true when the input matches the spec and the parsed month/day are in range; unsupported conversions and mismatches yield is_ok = false. Complexity: O(|s| + |spec|).

docs.title: fn strptime_iso8601(s: Str) -> DateParse
docs.text: Parse an ISO 8601 "YYYY-MM-DD" date string. Parameters: s -- the date string. Returns: a DateParse with is_ok true when the string is well-formed. Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn swap16(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Swaps the two bytes of a 16-bit value stored in the low 16 bits of an Int. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn swap32(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Swaps the four bytes of a 32-bit value stored in the low 32 bits of an Int. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn swap64(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Swaps the eight bytes of a 64-bit value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn time_now() -> Int
docs.text: Seconds since midnight (local time, which this runtime equates to UTC). Returns: 0..86399. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_now() -> Int
docs.text: Seconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). Returns: the current epoch seconds. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_to_date(ts: Int) -> Date
docs.text: Convert a Unix timestamp (seconds since the epoch) to a calendar date. Parameters: ts -- the timestamp. Returns: the corresponding Date (UTC). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn date_to_timestamp(d: &Date) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a calendar date to the Unix timestamp of its midnight (UTC). Parameters: d -- the date. Returns: epoch seconds for 00:00:00Z of that date. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_now() -> Int
docs.text: Seconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). Returns: the current epoch seconds. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_to_date(ts: Int) -> Date
docs.text: Convert a Unix timestamp (seconds since the epoch) to a calendar date. Parameters: ts -- the timestamp. Returns: the corresponding Date (UTC). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_to_datetime(ts: Int) -> DateTime
docs.text: Convert a Unix timestamp (seconds since the epoch) to a date-time value. Parameters: ts -- the timestamp. Returns: the corresponding DateTime (UTC) with weekday computed. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_from_date(d: &Date) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a calendar date to the Unix timestamp of its midnight (UTC). Parameters: d -- the date. Returns: epoch seconds for 00:00:00Z of that date. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn timestamp_from_datetime(dt: &DateTime) -> Int
docs.text: Convert a date-time value to a Unix timestamp (UTC). Parameters: dt -- the date-time value. Returns: epoch seconds for that instant. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_float(n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Widens an integer to a float (exact up to 2^53). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_float_saturating(s: Str) -> Float64
docs.text: Parses a string into a float, clamping on failure: malformed input (empty, no digits, invalid characters) yields 0.0. Supports sign, decimal point, and 'e'/'E' exponent. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn to_float_checked(s: Str) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Parses a string into a float only when the input is well-formed. Returns None on malformed input. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn to_int(n: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncates a float toward zero. Behavior for NaN and out-of-range values is undefined (use the checked/saturating variants for those inputs). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_int_saturating(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Truncates a float toward zero, clamping to INT_MAX/INT_MIN on overflow. NaN yields 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_int_checked(f: Float64) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Truncates a float toward zero only when the result fits an Int. Returns None for NaN or values outside [INT_MIN, INT_MAX). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_int_from_char(c: Char) -> Int
docs.text: Returns a character's code point as an integer. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_string(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Formats an integer as a decimal string. Exact for the full Int range (including INT_MIN, which the core implementation mishandles by negating in place). Complexity: O(log_10 |n|).

docs.title: fn to_string_float(f: Float64) -> Str
docs.text: Formats a float as a string (15 significant digits, fixed or scientific, handling "nan" and "inf"). Complexity: O(|exp10| + 15).

docs.title: fn to_string_bool(b: Bool) -> Str
docs.text: Renders a boolean as "true" or "false". Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_string_char(c: Char) -> Str
docs.text: Renders a character as a single-character UTF-8 string. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn to_string_radix(n: Int, radix: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Formats an integer in an arbitrary radix (2-36, lowercase digits). Returns "" for an invalid radix. Complexity: O(log_radix |n|).

docs.title: fn try_from_int(n: Int) -> Result[Float64, Str]
docs.text: Widen an integer to a float only when the conversion is lossless. Parameters: n -- the integer value. Returns: Ok(Float64) when n fits exactly (|n| <= 2^53), Err otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn try_from_float(f: Float64) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Truncate a float to an integer only when the value fits an Int. Parameters: f -- the float value. Returns: Ok(Int) for finite in-range values, Err for NaN or values outside the Int range. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn try_from_str(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse a string to an integer if valid. Parameters: s -- the decimal integer string (optional sign). Returns: Ok(Int) for well-formed input, Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n), n = string length.

docs.title: fn unchecked_add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a + b without overflow checking (wraps). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unchecked_sub(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a - b without overflow checking (wraps). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unchecked_mul(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a * b without overflow checking (wraps). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unchecked_shl(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a << n without overflow checking (discards shifted-out bits); n is masked to [0, 64). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unchecked_shr(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a >> n (arithmetic) without overflow checking; n is masked to [0, 64). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: type Uri
docs.text:
Uri -- parsed URI components.

Field Type scheme Str authority Str path Str query Str fragment Str

docs.title: fn uri_parse(s: Str) -> Result[Uri, Str]
docs.text: Parse a URI into its scheme, authority, path, query and fragment. Parameters: s -- the URI string. Returns: Ok(Uri) on success; Err for an empty URI. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn uri_normalize(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Normalize a URI into canonical form: lowercase scheme, remove dot segments from the path, and keep the authority/query/fragment. Parameters: s -- the URI string. Returns: Ok(canonical) on success; Err for an empty URI. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn uri_resolve(base: Str, rel: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Resolve a relative URI against a base URI (RFC 3986 S5). Parameters: base -- the absolute base URI; rel -- the reference (may be absolute or relative). Returns: Ok(resolved) on success; Err when parsing fails. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: type Url
docs.text:
Url -- parsed URL components.

Field Type scheme Str host Str port Int path Str query Str

docs.title: fn url_parse(s: Str) -> Result[Url, Str]
docs.text: Parse a URL into its scheme, host, port, path and query components. Userinfo (user:pass@) is skipped. Parameters: s -- the URL string. Returns: Ok(Url) on success; Err for an empty URL or a missing host. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn url_build(scheme: Str, host: Str, port: Int, path: Str, query: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Assemble a URL string from its parts. Parameters: scheme -- e.g. "https"; host -- e.g. "example.com"; port -- 0 means "no explicit port"; path -- must start with "/"; query -- the raw query string without '?' (empty means none). Returns: the assembled URL. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn url_encode(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Percent-encode a URL (unreserved characters A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ pass through; everything else becomes %HH). Parameters: s -- the text to encode. Returns: the percent-encoded string. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn url_decode(s: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Percent-decode a URL. Parameters: s -- the encoded text. Returns: Ok(decoded) on success; Err for a truncated or invalid escape. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn urn_parse(s: Str) -> Result[(Str, Str, Str), Str]
docs.text: Parse a URN into its (nid, nss, rq) components. Parameters: s -- the URN string. Returns: Ok((nid, nss, rq)) on success, where rq is the concatenation of the r-component and q-component ("" when absent); Err otherwise. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn urn_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is a valid URN. Parameters: s -- the candidate URN string. Returns: true when the URN structure is valid. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn urn_build(nid: Str, nss: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Assemble a URN from a namespace identifier and specific string. Parameters: nid -- the namespace identifier (2-32 chars, alphanumeric plus hyphen, not starting or ending with hyphen); nss -- the namespace specific string. Returns: "urn::". Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16_encode(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt16]
docs.text: Encode a string to native-order UTF-16 code units (no BOM). Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: UTF-16 code units (surrogate pairs for supplementary chars). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16_decode(bytes: &Vec[UInt16]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode native-order UTF-16 code units to a string. Parameters: bytes -- the code units (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for lone surrogates. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16le_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string to little-endian UTF-16 bytes including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16be_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string to big-endian UTF-16 bytes including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16_decode_le(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode little-endian UTF-16 bytes to a string. Parameters: bytes -- the byte sequence (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for an odd length or lone surrogates. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16_decode_be(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode big-endian UTF-16 bytes to a string. Parameters: bytes -- the byte sequence (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for an odd length or lone surrogates. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32_encode(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt32]
docs.text: Encode a string to UTF-32 code points (no BOM). Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: one UInt32 per code point. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32_decode(code_points: &Vec[UInt32]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode UTF-32 code points to a string. Parameters: code_points -- the code points (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for a surrogate or out-of-range value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32le_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string to little-endian UTF-32 bytes including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32be_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string to big-endian UTF-32 bytes including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Report whether every code point of a string fits within UTF-16 (i.e. no character lies in the surrogate range and all are <= 0x10FFFF). Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: true when every code point is encodable in UTF-16. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Report whether a string contains no surrogate or invalid code points. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: true when every code point is a valid scalar value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn code_point_to_utf16(cp: Int) -> (UInt16, UInt16)
docs.text: Split a code point into a UTF-16 surrogate pair. Parameters: cp -- a code point >= 0x10000. Returns: (high surrogate, low surrogate). Code points below 0x10000 or above 0x10FFFF map to (0, 0). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn surrogate_pair_to_code_point(hi: UInt16, lo: UInt16) -> Int
docs.text: Combine a UTF-16 surrogate pair into a code point. Parameters: hi -- the high surrogate; lo -- the low surrogate. Returns: the code point; -1 when the pair is not a valid surrogate pair. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn utf16_encode(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt16]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-16 code units (native order, no BOM). Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: one UTF-16 code unit per BMP code point, surrogate pairs for supplementary characters. Complexity: O(n), n = code points.

docs.title: fn utf16_decode(bytes: &Vec[UInt16]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode UTF-16 code units to a string. Parameters: bytes -- the code units (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for a lone surrogate, an invalid code unit range, or an overlong result. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16le_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-16LE bytes, including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the little-endian byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf16be_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-16BE bytes, including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the big-endian byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32_encode(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt32]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-32 code points (no BOM). Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: one UInt32 per Unicode code point. Complexity: O(n), n = code points.

docs.title: fn utf32_decode(code_points: &Vec[UInt32]) -> Result[Str, Str]
docs.text: Decode UTF-32 code points to a string. Parameters: code_points -- the code points (a leading BOM is skipped). Returns: Ok(Str) on success; Err for a surrogate or out-of-range value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32le_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-32LE bytes, including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the little-endian byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf32be_to_bytes(s: Str) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a string as UTF-32BE bytes, including a BOM. Parameters: s -- the input string. Returns: the big-endian byte sequence. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utf8_encode(c: Char) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Encode a character as UTF-8 bytes. Parameters: c -- the character. Returns: 1-4 bytes forming the UTF-8 encoding of c. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn utf8_decode(bytes: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Option[Char]
docs.text: Decode one UTF-8 character from the start of a byte vector. Parameters: bytes -- a UTF-8 byte sequence. Returns: Some(Char) when the leading sequence is well-formed (including overlong/surrogate/range checks); None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn utf8_validate(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is well-formed UTF-8. Parameters: s -- the string to validate. Returns: true when every byte sequence decodes cleanly. Complexity: O(n), n = byte length.

docs.title: fn utf8_valid_sequences(s: Str) -> Int
docs.text: Count the valid UTF-8 sequences in a string. Invalid bytes advance one position without being counted. Parameters: s -- the string to scan. Returns: the number of well-formed UTF-8 sequences. Complexity: O(n), n = byte length.

docs.title: fn uuencode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encode arbitrary bytes to classic UU format (data lines only). Parameters: data -- the raw bytes. Returns: the UU-encoded text (each line ends with a newline). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn uudecode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decode a UU-encoded string to bytes. Parameters: s -- the UU text (data lines; "begin"/"end" wrappers ignored). Returns: Ok(bytes) on success; Err on malformed input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn uuencode_line(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encode a single UU line of at most 45 bytes (length char + encoded data). Parameters: data -- up to 45 bytes. Returns: the encoded line (without a trailing newline). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn uudecode_line(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decode a single UU line, validating length and padding. Parameters: s -- the encoded line (length char + data, no newline). Returns: Ok(bytes) on success; Err on invalid input. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn xxencode(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Encode arbitrary bytes to XXencode format (data lines only). Parameters: data -- the raw bytes. Returns: the XX-encoded text. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn xxdecode(s: Str) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text: Decode an XXencode string to bytes. Parameters: s -- the XX text. Returns: Ok(bytes) on success; Err on malformed input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn uu_encoded_length(len: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Compute the encoded length for a given input length: each 45-byte block becomes a 61-character line (60 data chars + newline). Parameters: len -- the input byte count. Returns: the UU-encoded text length. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn uuid_v4() -> Str
docs.text: Generate a random RFC 4122 version 4 UUID string (8-4-4-4-12, lowercase). Returns: a 36-character UUID string. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn uuid_parse(s: Str) -> Option[(Int, Int, Int, Int)]
docs.text: Parse a UUID string into its four 32-bit fields. Parameters: s -- a UUID string in 8-4-4-4-12 form. Returns: Some((time_low, time_mid, time_hi_and_version, clock_and_node)) for a well-formed string, None otherwise. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn uuid_is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check that a string is a valid UUID (36 chars, 8-4-4-4-12 layout, hex). Parameters: s -- the candidate string. Returns: true when the layout matches. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn uuid_v4_bytes() -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text: Generate the raw 16 bytes of a random RFC 4122 version 4 UUID. Returns: 16 bytes with the version (0100) and variant (10) bits set. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn is_valid_email(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check the basic email shape (local@domain). Parameters: s -- the candidate address. Returns: true when there is exactly one '@', a non-empty local part, a non-empty domain containing a dot, and no whitespace. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn is_valid_email_strict(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check an email against stricter RFC 5322-shaped rules: local part up to 64 chars, domain labels 1..63 chars, no leading/trailing dots. Parameters: s -- the candidate address. Returns: true for a well-formed address. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn is_valid_phone(s: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Check a phone number for a recognizable format (digits, spaces, + - ( )). Parameters: s -- the candidate number. Returns: true when the number contains 7..15 digits with only allowed separator characters. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn is_valid_phone_e164(s: Str) -> Bool

ChaCha20 State Type

The 512-bit state is arranged as a 4x4 matrix of 32-bit words (16 words total). Layout (RFC 8439 Section 2.3): state[0..3] = constants (row 0) state[4..11] = key (rows 1,2) state[12] = block counter (row 3, col 0) state[13..15]= nonce (row 3, cols 1-3)

docs.title: fn blake3(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text:
Compute the BLAKE3 hash of data (32-byte output).

Spec: https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3-specs

Single-chunk inputs (<= 1024 bytes) compress the chunk directly with CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT. Larger inputs are hashed through the binary tree: each 1024-byte chunk produces a leaf CV (chunk counter = chunk index), leaves are merged pairwise via parent nodes, and the root node carries the ROOT flag. The 32-byte digest is the root output words 7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0 serialized little-endian (reversed word order).

docs.title: fn hkdf_sha256(ikm: &Vec[UInt8], salt: &Vec[UInt8], info: &Vec[UInt8], okm_len: Int) -> Result[Vec[UInt8], Str]
docs.text:
HKDF (RFC 5869) -- HMAC-based Key Derivation Function

HKDF consists of two steps: 1. Extract: PRK = HMAC-SHA256(salt, IKM) 2. Expand: OKM = T(1) || T(2) || ... || T(N) truncated to okm_len where T(0) = empty, T(i) = HMAC-SHA256(PRK, T(i-1) || info || i) i is a single byte counter (1, 2, 3, ...)

RFC 5869 test case 1: IKM = 0x0b0b0b... (22 times) salt = 0x000102030405060708090a0b0c info = 0xf0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9 L = 42 OKM = 3cb25f25faacd57a90434f64d0362f2a 2d2d0a90cf1a5a4c5db02d56ecc4c5bf 34007208d5b887185865

Security notes: - Extract step concentrates entropy from IKM. - Salt should be random but not secret; can be all-zeros. - Info binds derived key to context; must be unique per key.

docs.title: fn chacha20_poly1305_encrypt(key: &Vec[UInt8], nonce: &Vec[UInt8], aad: &Vec[UInt8], plaintext: &Vec[UInt8], ciphertext: &mut Vec[UInt8], tag: &mut Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text:
ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439 Section 2.8)

Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data using ChaCha20 and Poly1305.

Algorithm: 1. Generate 32-byte Poly1305 one-time key from ChaCha20 block 0 keystream. 2. Encrypt plaintext using ChaCha20 keystream starting from block 1. 3. Compute Poly1305 tag over: pad16(AAD) || pad16(ciphertext) || le64(AAD_len) || le64(CT_len).

Key: 32 bytes (256-bit). Nonce: 12 bytes (96-bit), MUST be unique per key. AAD: arbitrary bytes, authenticated but NOT encrypted. Plaintext: arbitrary bytes to encrypt and authenticate. ciphertext: out-param, populated with encrypted data (same length as plaintext). tag: out-param, populated with 16-byte authentication tag. Returns: true on success.

RFC 8439 test vector (Section 2.8.2): key = 808182838485868788898a8b8c8d8e8f909192939495969798999a9b9c9d9e9f nonce = 070000004041424344454647 aad = 50515253c0c1c2c3c4c5c6c7 plaintext = "Ladies and Gentlemen of the class of '99..." ciphertext = d31a8d34648e60db7b86afbc53ef7ec2... tag = 1ae10b594f09e26a7e902ecbd0600691

Security notes: - Nonce MUST be unique for every message under the same key. - Nonce reuse completely breaks confidentiality AND authenticity. - The 16-byte tag provides 128-bit authentication strength.

docs.title: fn chacha20_poly1305_decrypt(key: &Vec[UInt8], nonce: &Vec[UInt8], aad: &Vec[UInt8], ciphertext: &Vec[UInt8], tag: &Vec[UInt8], plaintext: &mut Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text:
ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD -- Decrypt

Algorithm: 1. Re-generate Poly1305 one-time key from ChaCha20 block 0. 2. Compute expected tag over: pad16(AAD) || pad16(ciphertext) || le64(AAD_len) || le64(CT_len). 3. Compare expected_tag with provided tag in constant time. 4. If match, decrypt ciphertext to plaintext using ChaCha20 block 1+ keystream.

Key: 32 bytes. Nonce: 12 bytes. AAD: authenticated but unencrypted data. ciphertext: encrypted data to authenticate and decrypt. tag: 16-byte authentication tag to verify. plaintext: out-param, populated with decrypted data on success. Returns: true if authentication passed and decryption succeeded.

Security notes: - Decryption only proceeds if tag verification passes (encrypt-then-MAC). - Constant-time tag comparison prevents timing oracle attacks.

docs.title: fn poly1305_mac(key: &Vec[UInt8], msg: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text:
Poly1305 MAC -- Main Function

Computes a 16-byte authenticator tag for the given message under the given 32-byte one-time key.

Algorithm: 1. Split key: r = key[0..15] (clamped), s = key[16..31] 2. Initialize accumulator h = 0 (all 5 limbs = 0) 3. Process each 16-byte message block: a. Convert block + 0x01 to 5 limbs (n) b. h = h + n (limb-wise) c. h = h * r mod p 4. Finalize: tag = low 128 bits of (h + s)

Parameters: key: 32-byte one-time key (Vec[Int] where each element is a byte value 0-255, or Vec[UInt8]) msg: message to authenticate Returns: 16-byte tag as Vec[Int] (each element 0-255)

IMPORTANT: The key MUST be used only once per key. Key reuse breaks security. Use with ChaCha20 as ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for authenticated encryption.

docs.title: fn rsa_keygen(bits: Int) -> Result[RsaKeyPair, Str]
docs.text:
Generate an RSA key pair with approximately bits bits of modulus.

Algorithm: 1. Choose two distinct primes p, q of roughly bits/2 each. 2. n = p * q (must fit in i64: n < 2^63) 3. phi = (p-1) * (q-1) 4. e = 65537 (standard RSA public exponent; Fermat prime F4) If 65537 >= phi or gcd(e, phi) != 1, fall back to e = 3 and search. 5. d = e-1 mod phi (modular inverse via extended Euclidean algorithm)

Parameters: bits: desired modulus size in bits (recommended: 16-30 for this impl) Returns: Result[RsaKeyPair, Str] -- the key pair or an error message

Complexity: O(2^(bits/2)) for primality testing due to trial division. Keep bits <= 30 for reasonable performance.

Encrypt a message using RSA.

docs.title: fn hexdump(data: &Vec[UInt8], width: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Produce a formatted hex + ASCII dump string for a byte vector. Each line shows: 8-digit hex offset, 16 bytes in hex (grouped 8+8), then the ASCII representation (printable chars or '.').

Example output: 00000000 48 65 6C 6C 6F 20 57 6F 72 6C 64 21 00 00 00 00 |Hello World!....|

Complexity: O(n) where n = data.len().

  • Precondition: width > 0
  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 0

docs.title: fn trace_point(name: Str) -> Str

  • Postcondition: result.len() > 0

docs.title: fn elapsed_ms(start_ns: Int) -> Float64
docs.text:
Convert a nanosecond timestamp (e.g., from xiom.time) to elapsed milliseconds as a Float64. Use with xiom.time.Instant for measuring code sections.

Example: let start = xiom.time.Instant.now(); // ... work ... let ms = elapsed_ms(start.elapsed().as_nanos());

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

Returns false for any violation. Complexity: O(total length + sum of label^2).

docs.text: Wrap the Err payload of result with a context message, preserving Ok values unchanged. The Err message becomes just context -- the richer context + ": " + e.description() form needs the E: Error bound, which the checker's builtin-interface matching does not support yet (C001: bound resolves against the OK type; interface-as-value gap). The Error interface with Option[Error] returns also defaults to i64 (unknown-type warning). Re-enrich once the checker closes those gaps.

docs.title: fn octal_dump(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str

docs.title: fn binary_dump(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Formats a byte buffer as a 4-bytes-per-line binary dump. Each line: 8-digit hex offset, 8-bit binary per byte, ASCII column. Empty input yields "". Complexity: O(n).

Captured tokens (parallel arrays: convs 0=int(%d/%i/%u), 1=hex(%x/%X), 2=float(%f/%e/%g), 3=str(%s), 4=char(%c)). Plain struct on purpose: the compiler's generic Result[Vec[struct], ] instantiation collides with Result[Int, ] in mono layout (docs/COMPILER_BUGS.md), so the engine returns a concrete named struct instead.

Field Type is_ok Bool convs Vec[Int] texts Vec[Str] error Str

docs.title: fn sscanf(s: Str, spec: Str) -> Result[Vec[Str], Str]
docs.text: scanf-style scan of s per spec: literal chars match exactly, spec whitespace skips any input whitespace run. Conversions: %d/%i/%u (dec), %x/%X (hex, optional 0x), %f/%e/%g (float, optional exponent), %s (token), %c (exact chars incl. whitespace), width caps, * suppresses, %% literal. Returns the captured token strings in order, Err on any mismatch.

docs.title: fn sscanf_ints(s: Str, spec: Str) -> Result[Vec[Int], Str]
docs.text: sscanf + typed integer extraction: converts %d/%i/%u (decimal) and %x/%X (hex) tokens to Int with overflow checking. Non-integer conversions in the spec -> Err. The returned Vec is in token order.

docs.title: type FormatFloatScan
docs.text:
Float results of sscanf_floats. Fixed 8 scalar slots instead of a Vec[Float64] (BUG 12: float container element reads broken -- TODO(compiler) restore a Vec-based API once fixed). Specs with more than 8 float conversions -> is_ok = false ("too many float conversions").

Field Type is_ok Bool count Int v0 Float64 v1 Float64 v2 Float64 v3 Float64 v4 Float64 v5 Float64 v6 Float64 v7 Float64 error Str

docs.title: fn sscanf_floats(s: Str, spec: Str) -> FormatFloatScan
docs.text: sscanf + typed float extraction: converts %f/%e/%g tokens to Float64 (normalized ".5" -> "0.5" for the builtin parser). Non-float conversions in the spec or more than 8 float conversions -> is_ok = false with error. Values land in v0..v7 in token order; count says how many are valid.

docs.title: fn fmt_int_with_separators(n: Int, sep: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Formats an integer with sep inserted every three digits from the right. The sign is preserved: fmt_int_with_separators(-987654, ",") -> "-987,654". n == 0 -> "0". Complexity: O(digits).

docs.title: fn fmt_float_fixed(x: Float64, decimals: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Formats a float with a fixed number of decimals using integer math. Rounds half away from zero: fmt_float_fixed(3.14159, 2) -> "3.14". Because 2.675 is not exactly representable in binary, its scaled value (267.4999...) rounds to "2.67", not "2.68" -- a documented float-math artifact. Negative values keep their sign. Complexity: O(decimals).

docs.title: fn fmt_percent(x: Float64, decimals: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Formats a fraction (0..1) as a percentage with decimals decimals. fmt_percent(0.125, 1) -> "12.5%". Uses fmt_float_fixed for rounding. Complexity: O(decimals).

docs.title: fn fmt_bytes(n: Int) -> Str
