docs.title: fn quat_normalize(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Normalise a quaternion to unit length. If length is zero, returns identity. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_conjugate(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Conjugate of a quaternion. For unit quaternions this is the inverse. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_rotate_vec3(q: Quaternion, v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Rotate a 3D vector by quaternion q (q must be normalised). O(1). Returns: v + 2.0 * q.xyz x (q.xyz x v + q.w * v)

docs.title: fn quat_from_euler(yaw: Float64, pitch: Float64, roll: Float64) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Create a quaternion from Euler angles (ZYX intrinsic = yaw-pitch-roll in radians). yaw: rotation around Z, pitch: around Y, roll: around X.

docs.title: fn mat4_identity() -> Mat4
docs.text: 4x4 identity matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_mul(a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4
docs.text: Multiply two 4x4 matrices: a * b. Row x column dot products. O(64 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_translate(tx: Float64, ty: Float64, tz: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Translation matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_scale(sx: Float64, sy: Float64, sz: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Scale matrix (non-uniform). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_rotate_x(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around X axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_rotate_y(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around Y axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_rotate_z(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around Z axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_perspective(fov: Float64, aspect: Float64, near: Float64, far: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Perspective projection matrix (right-handed, reverse Z [-1,1] NDC). fov: vertical field of view in radians, aspect: width/height, near/far: clipping planes. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_look_at(eye: Vec3, target: Vec3, up: Vec3) -> Mat4
docs.text: Look-at view matrix: camera at eye, looking at target, with up vector. Right-handed coordinate system. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_transform_vec3(m: Mat4, v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Transform a Vec3 point by a 4x4 matrix (x,y,z,1 homogeneous). O(16 ops).

docs.title: fn mat3_identity() -> Mat3
docs.text: 3x3 identity matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_mul(a: Mat3, b: Mat3) -> Mat3
docs.text: Multiply two 3x3 matrices: a * b. O(27 ops).

docs.title: fn aabb_new(min: Vec3, max: Vec3) -> Aabb
docs.text: Create an AABB from min and max corners.

docs.title: fn aabb_contains_point(box: Aabb, point: Vec3) -> Bool
docs.text: Test whether a point is inside the AABB (inclusive). O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_intersects_aabb(a: Aabb, b: Aabb) -> Bool
docs.text: Test whether two AABBs intersect. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_new(center: Vec3, radius: Float64) -> Sphere
docs.text: Create a sphere from centre and radius.

docs.title: fn sphere_contains_point(s: Sphere, point: Vec3) -> Bool
docs.text: Test whether a point is inside the sphere (inclusive). O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_new(origin: Vec3, dir: Vec3) -> Ray
docs.text: Create a ray from origin and direction.

docs.title: fn ray_intersect_sphere(r: Ray, s: Sphere) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-sphere intersection. Returns Some(t) for the nearest hit, or None. t is the distance from origin along dir to the intersection point. Uses quadratic formula; only returns the smaller positive t. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_intersect_aabb(r: Ray, box: Aabb) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-AABB intersection (slab method). Returns Some(t_near) for intersection, or None if the ray misses the box. O(1). See: "An Efficient and Robust Ray-Box Intersection Algorithm" by Williams et al.

docs.title: fn vec2_neg(v: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text:
Negate a 2D vector (component-wise -v). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == -v.x && result.y == -v.y

docs.title: fn vec2_reflect(incident: Vec2, normal: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text: Reflect a 2D incident vector about a surface normal (normal must be unit). Formula: i - 2 * dot(i, n) * n. Degenerate (zero) normal returns incident. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_refract(incident: Vec2, normal: Vec2, eta: Float64) -> Option[Vec2]
docs.text: Refract a 2D vector across an interface with relative index eta. Returns None on total internal reflection (k < 0). Both vectors should be unit length. Formula: etai - (etadot(i,n) + sqrt(k)) * n, k = 1 - eta2(1 - dot2). O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_project(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text: Project a onto b: b * dot(a,b) / dot(b,b). Returns zero if b is degenerate. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_reject(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text: Reject a from b: a - project(a,b), the component of a perpendicular to b. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_angle_between(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Float64
docs.text: Angle (radians) between two 2D vectors in [0, PI]. Returns 0 if either is zero. Uses acos of the clamped dot product of the normalised vectors. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_distance_squared(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Float64
docs.text:
Squared Euclidean distance between two 2D points (avoids sqrt). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn vec2_lerp_unclamped(a: Vec2, b: Vec2, t: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text:
Unclamped linear interpolation between a and b by t (t may leave [0,1]). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t && result.y == a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t

docs.title: fn vec2_nlerp(a: Vec2, b: Vec2, t: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Normalised linear interpolation (nlerp): lerp then normalise the result. O(1). Cheaper than slerp; not constant angular velocity.

docs.title: fn vec2_rotate(v: Vec2, angle: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Rotate a 2D vector counter-clockwise by angle (radians) about the origin. Formula: (xcos - ysin, xsin + ycos). O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_rotate_around(v: Vec2, center: Vec2, angle: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Rotate v around an arbitrary center point by angle (radians). O(1). Translates to the origin, rotates, then translates back.

docs.title: fn vec2_perpendicular(v: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text: Return a vector perpendicular to v: (-y, x). This is v rotated by +90 degrees. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_from_angle(angle: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Unit vector from an angle (radians): (cos(angle), sin(angle)). O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_is_unit(v: Vec2, epsilon: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the length of v is within epsilon of 1.0. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_is_zero(v: Vec2) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every component of v is exactly zero. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_approx_eq(a: Vec2, b: Vec2, epsilon: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every corresponding component of a and b differs by at most epsilon. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec2_min_component(v: Vec2) -> Float64
docs.text:
Smallest component of a 2D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result <= v.x && result <= v.y

docs.title: fn vec2_max_component(v: Vec2) -> Float64
docs.text:
Largest component of a 2D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= v.x && result >= v.y

docs.title: fn vec2_abs(v: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text:
Component-wise absolute value of a 2D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x >= 0 && result.y >= 0

docs.title: fn vec2_clamp_length(v: Vec2, max_len: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Clamp the length of v to max_len. Vectors shorter than max_len are unchanged. If max_len <= 0 the zero vector is returned. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_neg(v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text:
Negate a 3D vector (component-wise -v). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == -v.x && result.y == -v.y && result.z == -v.z

docs.title: fn vec3_reflect(incident: Vec3, normal: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Reflect a 3D incident vector about a surface normal (normal must be unit). Formula: i - 2 * dot(i, n) * n. Degenerate (zero) normal returns incident. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_refract(incident: Vec3, normal: Vec3, eta: Float64) -> Option[Vec3]
docs.text: Refract a 3D vector across an interface with relative index eta. Returns None on total internal reflection (k < 0). Both vectors should be unit length. Formula: etai - (etadot(i,n) + sqrt(k)) * n, k = 1 - eta2(1 - dot2). O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_project(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Project a onto b: b * dot(a,b) / dot(b,b). Returns zero if b is degenerate. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_reject(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Reject a from b: a - project(a,b), the component of a perpendicular to b. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_angle_between(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text: Angle (radians) between two 3D vectors in [0, PI]. Returns 0 if either is zero. Uses acos of the clamped dot product of the normalised vectors. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_distance_squared(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text:
Squared Euclidean distance between two 3D points (avoids sqrt). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn vec3_lerp_unclamped(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, t: Float64) -> Vec3
docs.text:
Unclamped linear interpolation between a and b by t (t may leave [0,1]). O(1). Contrast with vec3_lerp which clamps t into [0,1].

  • Postcondition: result.x == a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t && result.y == a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t && result.z == a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t

docs.title: fn vec3_nlerp(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, t: Float64) -> Vec3
docs.text: Normalised linear interpolation (nlerp): lerp then normalise the result. O(1). Cheaper than slerp; not constant angular velocity.

docs.title: fn vec3_orthogonal(v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Return any vector perpendicular to v (unit length), using the smallest-absolute-component zero method to avoid cancellation. Returns the zero vector when v is zero. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_is_unit(v: Vec3, epsilon: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the length of v is within epsilon of 1.0. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_is_zero(v: Vec3) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every component of v is exactly zero. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_approx_eq(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, epsilon: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every corresponding component of a and b differs by at most epsilon. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec3_min_component(v: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text:
Smallest component of a 3D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result <= v.x && result <= v.y && result <= v.z

docs.title: fn vec3_max_component(v: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text:
Largest component of a 3D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= v.x && result >= v.y && result >= v.z

docs.title: fn vec3_abs(v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text:
Component-wise absolute value of a 3D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x >= 0 && result.y >= 0 && result.z >= 0

docs.title: fn vec3_clamp_length(v: Vec3, max_len: Float64) -> Vec3
docs.text: Clamp the length of v to max_len. Vectors shorter than max_len are unchanged. If max_len <= 0 the zero vector is returned. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec4_mul_component(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4
docs.text:
Multiply two 4D vectors component-wise (Hadamard product). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == a.x * b.x && result.y == a.y * b.y && result.z == a.z * b.z && result.w == a.w * b.w

docs.title: fn vec4_div_component(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4
docs.text:
Divide a by b component-wise. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == a.x / b.x && result.y == a.y / b.y && result.z == a.z / b.z && result.w == a.w / b.w

docs.title: fn vec4_scale(v: Vec4, s: Float64) -> Vec4
docs.text:
Multiply each component of v by scalar s. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == v.x * s && result.y == v.y * s && result.z == v.z * s && result.w == v.w * s

docs.title: fn vec4_neg(v: Vec4) -> Vec4
docs.text:
Negate a 4D vector (component-wise -v). O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x == -v.x && result.y == -v.y && result.z == -v.z && result.w == -v.w

docs.title: fn vec4_approx_eq(a: Vec4, b: Vec4, epsilon: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every corresponding component of a and b differs by at most epsilon. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec4_min_component(v: Vec4) -> Float64
docs.text:
Smallest component of a 4D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result <= v.x && result <= v.y && result <= v.z && result <= v.w

docs.title: fn vec4_max_component(v: Vec4) -> Float64
docs.text:
Largest component of a 4D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result >= v.x && result >= v.y && result >= v.z && result >= v.w

docs.title: fn vec4_abs(v: Vec4) -> Vec4
docs.text:
Component-wise absolute value of a 4D vector. O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.x >= 0 && result.y >= 0 && result.z >= 0 && result.w >= 0

docs.title: fn vec3_from_vec4(v: Vec4) -> Vec3
docs.text: Drop the w component of a 4D vector to produce a 3D vector. O(1).

docs.title: fn vec4_from_vec3(v: Vec3, w: Float64) -> Vec4
docs.text: Build a 4D vector from a 3D vector plus an explicit w component. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_identity() -> Mat2
docs.text: 2x2 identity matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_mul(a: Mat2, b: Mat2) -> Mat2
docs.text: Multiply two 2x2 matrices: a * b. O(8 ops).

docs.title: fn mat2_transpose(m: Mat2) -> Mat2
docs.text: Transpose a 2x2 matrix in place. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_determinant(m: Mat2) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 2x2 matrix: m00m11 - m01m10. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_inverse(m: Mat2) -> Option[Mat2]
docs.text: Inverse of a 2x2 matrix via the adjugate / determinant formula. Returns None when the determinant is (near) zero, so the matrix is singular. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_scale(s: Float64) -> Mat2
docs.text: Uniform 2x2 scale matrix with factor s. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_rotation(angle: Float64) -> Mat2
docs.text: 2x2 rotation matrix by angle radians (counter-clockwise). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_transform_vec2(m: Mat2, v: Vec2) -> Vec2
docs.text: Transform a 2D vector by a 2x2 matrix: M * v. O(4 ops).

docs.title: fn mat3_transpose(m: Mat3) -> Mat3
docs.text: Transpose a 3x3 matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_determinant(m: Mat3) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 3x3 matrix by cofactor expansion along the first row. O(9 ops).

docs.title: fn mat3_inverse(m: Mat3) -> Option[Mat3]
docs.text: Inverse of a 3x3 matrix via the adjugate / determinant formula. Returns None when the determinant is (near) zero, so the matrix is singular. O(27 ops).

docs.title: fn mat3_transform_vec3(m: Mat3, v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Transform a 3D vector by a 3x3 matrix: M * v. O(9 ops).

docs.title: fn mat3_scale(s: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: Uniform 3x3 scale matrix with factor s. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_scale_xyz(x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: Non-uniform 3x3 scale matrix with per-axis factors. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_rotation_x(angle: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: 3x3 rotation around the X axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_rotation_y(angle: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: 3x3 rotation around the Y axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_rotation_z(angle: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: 3x3 rotation around the Z axis by angle radians (right-handed). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_from_quat(q: Quaternion) -> Mat3
docs.text: Rotation matrix from a (unit) quaternion. The quaternion is normalised first. Formula: the standard 3x3 rotation matrix derived from q. O(27 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_transpose(m: Mat4) -> Mat4
docs.text: Transpose a 4x4 matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_determinant(m: Mat4) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 4x4 matrix by cofactor expansion along the first row. O(48 ops). Uses 3x3 sub-determinants of the three lower rows.

docs.title: fn mat4_inverse(m: Mat4) -> Option[Mat4]
docs.text: Inverse of a 4x4 matrix via the adjugate method (cofactor transpose / det). Returns None when |det| < 1e-12, so the matrix is singular. O(150 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_transform_vec4(m: Mat4, v: Vec4) -> Vec4
docs.text: Transform a Vec4 (homogeneous) by a 4x4 matrix: M * v, no perspective divide. O(16 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_transform_point(m: Mat4, p: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Transform a point (w=1) by a 4x4 matrix, including perspective divide. If the transformed w is zero, returns the zero vector. O(16 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_transform_direction(m: Mat4, d: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Transform a direction (w=0) by a 4x4 matrix: rotation/scale only, translation is ignored and no perspective divide is applied. O(9 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_scale(x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Scale matrix (non-uniform) from three axis factors. Same as mat4_scale. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_translation(t: Vec3) -> Mat4
docs.text: Translation matrix from a Vec3 offset. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_translation_xyz(x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Translation matrix from three components. Same as mat4_translate. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_rotation_x(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around the X axis. Same as mat4_rotate_x. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_rotation_y(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around the Y axis. Same as mat4_rotate_y. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_rotation_z(angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation around the Z axis. Same as mat4_rotate_z. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_from_quat(q: Quaternion) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation matrix from a (unit) quaternion. The quaternion is normalised first. Formula: the standard 4x4 rotation matrix derived from q. O(27 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_rotation_axis_angle(axis: Vec3, angle: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Rotation matrix about an arbitrary axis (unit length) by angle radians. Uses the Rodrigues formula. The axis is normalised first. O(30 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_orthographic(l: Float64, r: Float64, b: Float64, t: Float64, n: Float64, f: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Orthographic projection matrix (right-handed, standard OpenGL mapping). Maps [l,r]x[b,t]x[n,f] to NDC [-1,1]^3. l != r, b != t, n != f required. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_is_identity(m: Mat4, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every element of m is within epsilon of the identity matrix. O(16 ops).

docs.title: fn mat4_approx_eq(a: Mat4, b: Mat4, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every corresponding element of a and b differs by at most epsilon. O(16 ops).

docs.title: fn quat_from_axis_angle(axis: Vec3, angle: Float64) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Create a quaternion from an axis and angle (radians). The axis is normalised first, so any (non-zero) axis is accepted. Rotation is right-handed. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_mul_vec3(q: Quaternion, v: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Rotate a 3D vector by a quaternion: q * v * q^-1 (q must be unit length). Same as quat_rotate_vec3, provided under the mul_vec3 name. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_inverse(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Inverse of a quaternion: the conjugate of the normalised quaternion. For a unit quaternion the conjugate is exactly the inverse. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_dot(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Dot product of two quaternions (4-vector dot). O(4 ops).

docs.title: fn quat_length(q: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Length (magnitude) of a quaternion. O(4 ops + sqrt).

docs.title: fn quat_is_unit(q: Quaternion, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the length of q is within epsilon of 1.0. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_slerp(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion, t: Float64) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Spherical linear interpolation between two quaternions by t in [0,1]. Handles the shortest path by negating b when dot(a,b) < 0, clamps the dot to [-1,1], and falls back to nlerp when a and b are nearly parallel. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_nlerp(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion, t: Float64) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Normalised linear interpolation between two quaternions (fast, not constant angular velocity). t is clamped into [0,1]. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_from_mat4(m: &Mat4) -> Quaternion
docs.text: Extract the quaternion from a rotation matrix using the standard trace method. Handles all three largest-diagonal cases to avoid degenerate sqrt. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_to_mat4(q: Quaternion) -> Mat4
docs.text: 4x4 rotation matrix from a quaternion. Same result as mat4_from_quat. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_to_mat3(q: Quaternion) -> Mat3
docs.text: 3x3 rotation matrix from a quaternion. Same result as mat3_from_quat. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_roll(q: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Roll (rotation around X, radians) extracted from a quaternion. Conventions match quat_from_euler (ZYX intrinsic). O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_pitch(q: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Pitch (rotation around Y, radians) extracted from a quaternion. Conventions match quat_from_euler (ZYX intrinsic). Input to asin is clamped. O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_yaw(q: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Yaw (rotation around Z, radians) extracted from a quaternion. Conventions match quat_from_euler (ZYX intrinsic). O(1).

docs.title: fn quat_angle_between(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion) -> Float64
docs.text: Angle (radians) between two rotation quaternions in [0, 2PI]. Returns 2acos(clamped dot) over the shortest arc. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_from_min_max(min: Vec3, max: Vec3) -> Aabb
docs.text: Create an AABB from min and max corners. Same as aabb_new. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_center(box: Aabb) -> Vec3
docs.text: Centre point of an AABB: (min + max) / 2. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_size(box: Aabb) -> Vec3
docs.text: Size (extent per axis) of an AABB: max - min. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_half_extents(box: Aabb) -> Vec3
docs.text: Half-extents of an AABB: size / 2. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_intersects_sphere(box: Aabb, s: Sphere) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the sphere intersects the AABB. Uses the closest-point test: the squared distance from the sphere centre to the box must not exceed r2. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_closest_point(box: Aabb, p: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Closest point on (or inside) the AABB to p: p clamped into [min, max]. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_surface_area(box: Aabb) -> Float64
docs.text: Surface area of an AABB: 2(wh + hd + wd). O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_volume(box: Aabb) -> Float64
docs.text: Volume of an AABB: whd. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_expand(box: Aabb, p: Vec3) -> Aabb
docs.text: Expand the AABB to include point p (grow min/max component-wise). O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_union(a: Aabb, b: Aabb) -> Aabb
docs.text: Smallest AABB that contains both a and b (component-wise min/max). O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_intersection(a: Aabb, b: Aabb) -> Option[Aabb]
docs.text: Overlap of two AABBs. Returns None when the boxes do not intersect. The result is the intersection volume between them. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_intersects_sphere(a: Sphere, b: Sphere) -> Bool
docs.text: True if two spheres intersect (or touch): distance <= r_a + r_b. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_intersects_aabb(s: Sphere, box: Aabb) -> Bool
docs.text: True if a sphere intersects an AABB. Delegates to aabb_intersects_sphere. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_closest_point(s: Sphere, p: Vec3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Closest point on the sphere surface to p. If p equals the centre, the centre (an arbitrary surface direction) is returned. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_surface_area(s: Sphere) -> Float64
docs.text: Surface area of a sphere: 4PIr2. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_volume(s: Sphere) -> Float64
docs.text: Volume of a sphere: (4/3)PIr3. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_expand(s: Sphere, p: Vec3) -> Sphere
docs.text: Expand the sphere so it contains point p. If p is already inside, the sphere is returned unchanged. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_at(r: Ray, t: Float64) -> Vec3
docs.text: Point on the ray at parameter t: origin + dir * t. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_origin(r: Ray) -> Vec3
docs.text: Origin of the ray. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_dir(r: Ray) -> Vec3
docs.text: Direction of the ray. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_intersect_plane(r: Ray, plane_point: Vec3, plane_normal: Vec3) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-plane intersection. Returns Some(t) where t is the ray parameter of the hit, or None if the ray is parallel to the plane or the hit lies behind the origin. plane_normal need not be unit. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_distance_to_point(r: Ray, p: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text: Distance from a point p to the ray line (not the segment). Uses the 3D cross-product formula |(p - o) x d| / |d|. Returns 0 if the direction is degenerate. O(1).

docs.title: type Plane
docs.text:
Plane defined by a point on the plane and its normal direction. The normal need not be unit length; signed distances then scale accordingly.

Field Type point Vec3 normal Vec3

docs.title: fn plane_new(point: Vec3, normal: Vec3) -> Plane
docs.text: Create a plane from a point on it and a normal direction. O(1).

docs.title: fn plane_signed_distance(p: &Plane, pt: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text: Signed distance from a point to the plane (positive on the normal side). Assumes the plane normal is unit length. O(1).

docs.title: fn plane_distance_to_point(p: &Plane, pt: Vec3) -> Float64
docs.text: Absolute distance from a point to the plane. Assumes a unit normal. O(1).

docs.title: fn plane_intersect_ray(p: &Plane, r: Ray) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-plane intersection against a Plane. Returns Some(t) or None. This is an alias of ray_intersect_plane using the plane's fields. O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_approx_eq(a: Float64, b: Float64, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True if |a - b| <= eps. The canonical epsilon comparison. O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_deg_to_rad(d: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Convert degrees to radians: d * PI / 180. O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_rad_to_deg(r: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Convert radians to degrees: r * 180 / PI. O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_deg_to_rad(d: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Convert degrees to radians (Float32 API: same formula, Float64 arithmetic). O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_rad_to_deg(r: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Convert radians to degrees (Float32 API: same formula, Float64 arithmetic). O(1).

docs.text: Euclidean distance between two points. O(1).

docs.title: fn point_in_circle(p: Point2, c: Circle) -> Bool
docs.text: True if p lies inside (or on) the circle. O(1).

docs.title: fn point_in_rect(p: Point2, r: Rect) -> Bool
docs.text: True if p lies inside (or on) the axis-aligned rectangle. O(1).

docs.title: fn point_in_triangle(p: Point2, t: Triangle2) -> Bool
docs.text: True if p lies inside (or on) the triangle (same-side test). O(1).

docs.title: fn point_in_polygon(p: Point2, poly: Polygon2) -> Bool
docs.text: True if p lies inside the polygon (ray-casting test; boundary counts as inside). O(n).

docs.title: fn line_intersection(l1: Line2, l2: Line2) -> Option[Point2]
docs.text: Intersection of two infinite lines; None when they are parallel. O(1).

docs.title: fn segment_intersection(s1: Segment2, s2: Segment2) -> Option[Point2]
docs.text: Intersection of two segments; None when they do not meet. O(1).

docs.title: fn segment_point_distance(s: Segment2, p: Point2) -> Float64
docs.text: Shortest distance from p to the segment s. O(1).

docs.title: fn line_point_distance(l: Line2, p: Point2) -> Float64
docs.text: Perpendicular distance from p to the infinite line l. O(1).

docs.title: fn circle_intersection(c: Circle, l: Line2) -> Option[Vec[Point2]]
docs.text: Intersection points of the circle and the line; None when they do not meet or the line is degenerate. O(1).

docs.title: fn circle_line_intersection(c: Circle, l: Line2) -> Option[Vec[Point2]]
docs.text: Alias of circle_intersection. O(1).

docs.title: fn circle_circle_intersection(c1: Circle, c2: Circle) -> Option[Vec[Point2]]
docs.text: Intersection points of two circles; None when they do not intersect (or are concentric). O(1).

docs.title: fn area_triangle(t: Triangle2) -> Float64
docs.text: Signed area of the triangle (positive for counter-clockwise vertices). O(1).

docs.title: fn area_polygon(poly: Polygon2) -> Float64
docs.text: Signed area of the polygon via the shoelace formula. O(n).

docs.title: fn centroid(poly: Polygon2) -> Point2
docs.text: Area centroid of the polygon. Returns the zero point for a degenerate polygon. O(n).

docs.title: fn convex_hull(points: &Vec[Point2]) -> Polygon2
docs.text: Convex hull of the points via the monotone chain algorithm (Andrew). The hull is counter-clockwise without a duplicated closing vertex. O(n log n).

docs.title: fn is_convex(poly: Polygon2) -> Bool
docs.text: True if every interior angle of the polygon is at most 180 degrees (collinear edges allowed). O(n).

docs.title: fn polygon_contains(poly: Polygon2, p: Point2) -> Bool
docs.text: Containment test for p in poly. Same as point_in_polygon. O(n).

docs.title: fn polygon_intersection(a: Polygon2, b: Polygon2) -> Option[Polygon2]
docs.text: Intersection polygon of a and b via Sutherland-Hodgman clipping of a against the edges of b (exact when b is convex). None when the result is empty. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn polygon_union(a: Polygon2, b: Polygon2) -> Option[Polygon2]
docs.text: Boolean union polygon of a and b. Implemented as the convex hull of both vertex sets: exact when the union is convex (e.g. overlapping convex polygons), otherwise an enclosing convex approximation (documented). O(n log n).

docs.title: fn polygon_difference(a: Polygon2, b: Polygon2) -> Option[Polygon2]
docs.text: Boolean difference a minus b. Implemented by clipping a against the outside of b (Sutherland-Hodgman with an inverted inside test): exact when b lies fully inside a, otherwise a conservative approximation (documented). None when the result is empty. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn polygon_circumference(poly: Polygon2) -> Float64
docs.text: Perimeter of the polygon. O(n).

docs.title: fn point_sphere_distance(p: Point3, s: Sphere3d) -> Float64

docs.title: fn point_plane_distance(p: Point3, pl: Plane3d) -> Float64

docs.title: fn plane_point_distance(pl: Plane3d, p: Point3) -> Float64

docs.title: fn line_point_distance(l: Line3, p: Point3) -> Float64
docs.text: Shortest distance from p to the infinite line l. O(1).

docs.title: fn segment_point_distance(s: Segment3, p: Point3) -> Float64
docs.text: Shortest distance from p to the segment s. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_plane_intersection(r: Ray3, pl: Plane3d) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-plane intersection: parameter t along the ray; None when parallel or behind the origin. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_triangle_intersection(r: Ray3, t: Triangle3) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-triangle intersection via the Moller-Trumbore algorithm. Returns the nearest positive t; None on miss or behind the origin. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_sphere_intersection(r: Ray3, s: Sphere3d) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-sphere intersection: nearest positive t; None on miss. O(1).

docs.title: fn ray_box_intersection(r: Ray3, b: Box) -> Option[Float64]
docs.text: Ray-box intersection via the slab method: nearest positive t; None on miss. O(1).

docs.title: fn plane_plane_intersection(p1: Plane3d, p2: Plane3d) -> Option[Line3]
docs.text: Line of intersection of two planes; None when parallel. O(1).

docs.title: fn sphere_sphere_intersection(a: Sphere3d, b: Sphere3d) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the two spheres overlap or touch. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_intersection(a: Box, b: Box) -> Bool
docs.text: True if the two axis-aligned boxes overlap or touch. O(1).

docs.title: fn aabb_contains(b: Box, p: Point3) -> Bool
docs.text: True if p lies inside (or on) the box. O(1).

docs.title: fn closest_point_on_segment(s: Segment3, p: Point3) -> Point3
docs.text: Closest point on the segment s to p. O(1).

docs.title: fn closest_point_on_plane(pl: Plane3d, p: Point3) -> Point3
docs.text: Orthogonal projection of p onto the plane. O(1).

docs.title: fn triangle_normal(t: Triangle3) -> Vec3
docs.text: Unit normal of the triangle (right-handed, b-a cross c-a). Returns the zero vector for a degenerate triangle. O(1).

docs.title: fn mesh_volume(m: Mesh) -> Float64
docs.text: Signed volume of a closed mesh via the divergence theorem (sum of signed tetrahedron volumes about the origin). O(n).

docs.title: fn mesh_surface_area(m: Mesh) -> Float64
docs.text: Total surface area of a mesh (sum of triangle areas). O(n).

docs.title: fn mesh_centroid(m: Mesh) -> Point3
docs.text: Volume-weighted centroid of a closed mesh. Returns the zero point for a degenerate mesh. O(n).

docs.title: fn convex_hull_3d(points: &Vec[Point3]) -> Mesh
docs.text: Convex hull of a point cloud as a triangle mesh. Every oriented face is a triangle (i, j, k) such that all other points lie on (or behind) the plane of that triangle. O(n^4); exact for small point sets.

docs.title: fn voronoi(sites: &Vec[Point2], bounds: Rect) -> Vec[Polygon2]
docs.text: Bounded Voronoi diagram of sites clipped to bounds: one cell per site, each cell the intersection of the half-planes defined by the perpendicular bisectors with every other site. O(k^2 * n).

docs.title: fn delaunay(points: &Vec[Point2]) -> Vec[Triangle2]
docs.text: Delaunay triangulation of points via the Bowyer-Watson algorithm (bounded by a super-triangle). Returns a non-empty triangle list for >= 3 points. O(n^2) typical.

docs.title: fn bezier_curve(controls: &Vec[Vec2], t: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Point on a Bezier curve with de Casteljau's algorithm. O(k^2).

docs.title: fn b_spline(controls: &Vec[Vec2], knots: &Vec[Float64], t: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: Uniform open (clamped) quadratic B-spline evaluation with de Boor's algorithm. Knots must satisfy knots.len() == controls.len() + 3 and be clamped (non-decreasing, endpoints repeated); t is clamped to [0, 1]. Returns the zero vector on inconsistent input. O(1).

docs.title: fn nurbs(controls: &Vec[Vec2], weights: &Vec[Float64], knots: &Vec[Float64], t: Float64) -> Vec2
docs.text: NURBS evaluation: weighted rational B-spline with de Boor's algorithm. weights.len() must equal controls.len() and knots must satisfy the clamped B-spline sizing. O(1).

docs.title: fn subdivision(mesh: Mesh, iterations: Int) -> Mesh
docs.text: Midpoint subdivision surface refinement: every triangle is split into four by inserting edge midpoints (no shared-edge deduplication). The triangle count quadruples per iteration. O(iterations * n).

docs.title: fn mesh_processing(mesh: Mesh) -> Mesh
docs.text: Mesh cleanup pipeline: removes duplicate vertices (exact position match) and rewrites the index list accordingly. Returns the cleaned mesh. O(n^2).

docs.title: fn projective_geometry(points: &Vec[Vec3]) -> Vec[Vec3]
docs.text: Apply a projective transform to the points: each point (x, y, z) is mapped to (x/w, y/w, z/w) with the perspective weight w = 1 + x + y + z. Points whose weight is zero are left unchanged. O(n).

docs.title: fn hyperbolic_geometry(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic distance in the Poincare ball model: 2 * atanh(|a - b| / |1 - a.b|). Returns 0 for identical points. O(1).

docs.title: fn elliptic_geometry(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Elliptic (spherical) distance between two unit vectors: acos(a.b) in [0, PI]. Returns 0 for identical unit vectors. O(n).

docs.title: fn non_euclidean(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Generic non-Euclidean metric: the Poincare hyperbolic distance (see hyperbolic_geometry). O(n).

docs.title: fn incidence_geometry(points: &Vec[Point2], lines: &Vec[Line2]) -> Bool
docs.text: Incidence predicate: true iff every point lies on at least one of the lines. O(p * l).

docs.title: fn convex_geometry(points: &Vec[Vec2]) -> Polygon2
docs.text: Convex decomposition/combination of a point set: returns the convex hull of the points as a Polygon2. O(n log n).

docs.title: fn computational_geometry(points: &Vec[Vec2]) -> Vec[Polygon2]
docs.text: General computational geometry entry point: returns the convex hull of the points as a single-cell polygon list. O(n log n).

docs.title: fn gram_schmidt(vectors: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Orthonormalise a set of vectors (each row is a vector) via the modified Gram-Schmidt process. Linearly dependent vectors collapse to the zero vector. O(k^2 * n).

docs.title: fn orthogonalize(vectors: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Orthogonalise a set of vectors (each row is a vector) without normalising the output. Linearly dependent vectors collapse to the zero vector. O(k^2 * n).

docs.title: fn normalize_columns(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Normalise every column of m to unit length. Columns with zero length are left as-is. Empty matrix for a ragged input. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn normalize_rows(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Normalise every row of m to unit length. Rows with zero length are left as-is. Empty matrix for a ragged input. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn is_orthogonal(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff m is orthogonal: m * m^T is the identity (within 1e-9). Empty or non-square matrices are false. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn is_symmetric(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff m equals its transpose (exact component equality). O(n^2).

docs.title: fn is_skew_symmetric(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff m equals minus its transpose (exact component equality, diagonal must be zero). O(n^2).

docs.title: fn is_positive_definite(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff m is symmetric positive definite: symmetric and every leading principal minor is positive (checked via a Cholesky-style sweep). O(n^2).

docs.title: fn is_diagonal_dominant(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff m is diagonally dominant: |m[i][i]| >= sum of the absolute values of the off-diagonal entries in the same row, for every row. O(n^2).

docs.title: fn matrix_exponential(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Matrix exponential of m via the Taylor series exp(M) = sum M^k / k!, iterated until the added term is negligible (or 60 terms). Empty matrix on non-square input. O(n^3 * terms).

docs.title: fn matrix_logarithm(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Principal matrix logarithm of m via the series log(M) = sum (-1)^(k+1) (M-I)^k / k, which converges when M is close to the identity. Returns the zero matrix for the identity and an empty matrix for non-square input. O(n^3 * terms).

docs.title: fn matrix_sqrt(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Principal matrix square root of m via Newton iteration X_{k+1} = (X_k + M * X_k^-1) / 2 (converges for well-conditioned SPD-like inputs). Empty matrix on non-square input. O(n^3 * iterations).

docs.title: fn matrix_power(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], p: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Integer matrix power m^p. p == 0 yields the identity, p < 0 inverts first, and repeated squaring keeps it to O(log |p|) multiplications. Empty matrix on non-square or singular input. O(n^3 * log |p|).

docs.title: fn vec_to_skew(v: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Skew-symmetric matrix [v]_x of a 3-vector v. Empty matrix unless v has exactly 3 elements. O(1).

docs.title: fn skew_to_vec(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: The 3-vector v such that vec_to_skew(v) == m, extracted from a skew-symmetric matrix. Empty vector unless m is 3x3. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_identity(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: n x n identity matrix. O(n^2).

docs.title: fn mat_mul(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Matrix product a * b. Returns an empty matrix when the inner dimensions do not match. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn mat_det(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a square matrix via Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Returns NaN for a non-square matrix and 0 for a singular one. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn mat_inv(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Option[Vec[Vec[Float64]]]
docs.text: Inverse of a square matrix via Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting. None when the matrix is singular or non-square. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn mat_transpose(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Transpose of a matrix. Empty matrix for a ragged input. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn mat_translate(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Compose the 4x4 matrix m with a translation (x, y, z): returns T * m where T is the translation matrix, so the translation is applied after m. Empty matrix unless m is 4x4. O(64).

docs.title: fn mat_rotate(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], angle: Float64, axis: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Compose the 4x4 matrix m with a rotation of angle (radians) about the axis direction: returns R * m where R is the Rodrigues rotation matrix (the axis is normalised first). Empty matrix unless m is 4x4. O(64).

docs.title: fn mat_scale(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Compose the 4x4 matrix m with a scale (x, y, z): returns S * m where S is the scale matrix, applied after m. Empty matrix unless m is 4x4. O(64).

docs.title: fn mat_look_at(eye: &Vec[Float64], target: &Vec[Float64], up: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Right-handed look-at view matrix: camera at eye looking at target with up direction. Column-major 4x4. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_perspective(fovy: Float64, aspect: Float64, near: Float64, far: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Perspective projection matrix (right-handed, standard OpenGL mapping). fovy is the vertical field of view in radians; near/far must differ. 4x4. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_ortho(left: Float64, right: Float64, bottom: Float64, top: Float64, near: Float64, far: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Orthographic projection matrix mapping [left,right] x [bottom,top] x [near,far] to NDC [-1,1]^3. 4x4. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_transform_point(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], p: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Transform the point p (3 or 4 components, w defaults to 1) by the 4x4 matrix m including the perspective divide. Returns the zero vector when the transformed w is zero. Empty vector for a non-4x4 matrix. O(16).

docs.title: fn transpose(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Matrix transpose. Empty matrix for a ragged input. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn det(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a square matrix via Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. NaN for non-square input. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn inverse(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Option[Vec[Vec[Float64]]]

docs.text: Signed minor (cofactor) at (row, col): (-1)^(row+col) * det of the deleted submatrix. NaN for non-square or out-of-range input. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn adjugate(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Adjugate (classical) matrix: the transpose of the cofactor matrix. Empty matrix for non-square input. O(n^4).

docs.title: fn trace(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Trace (sum of the main diagonal) of a square matrix. NaN for non-square. O(n).

docs.title: fn rank(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Int
docs.text: Rank of a matrix via Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn nullity(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Int
docs.text: Nullity of a matrix: number of columns minus the rank. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn eigenvectors(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]

docs.title: fn diagonal(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Main diagonal entries of a matrix. Empty vector for a ragged input. O(n).

docs.title: fn diag_mul(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], d: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]

docs.title: fn hadamard(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Element-wise (Hadamard) product of two same-shape matrices. Empty matrix on shape mismatch. O(n*m).

docs.title: fn kronecker(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Kronecker product of a (r x c) and b (p x q): an (rp) x (cq) matrix. Empty matrix for empty input. O(rpc*q).

docs.title: fn lu_decompose(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> (Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]])
docs.text: LU factorization of a square matrix (Doolittle, no pivoting): (L, U) with L unit lower triangular and A = L*U. Returns empty matrices on failure (non-square or zero pivot). O(n^3).

docs.title: fn qr_decompose(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> (Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]])
docs.text: QR factorization of a square matrix via Gram-Schmidt on the columns: (Q, R) with Q orthogonal and A = Q*R. Empty matrices on failure. O(n^3).

docs.title: fn svd_decompose(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> (Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Float64], Vec[Vec[Float64]])
docs.text: SVD of a 2x2 symmetric matrix (U, s, V) via its eigendecomposition with s holding the eigenvalues in descending order. Empty values for any other input (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn cholesky(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Option[Vec[Vec[Float64]]]

docs.title: fn solve_linear(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]

docs.title: fn least_squares(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]

docs.title: fn condition_number(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64

v repeated n times concatenated. O(n * v.len()). n <= 0 yields empty.

item repeated n times. O(n). n <= 0 yields an empty vector.

  • Postcondition: n < 0 => result.len() == 0

docs.title: stdlib.math
docs.text:
Math Library

Generated from v0.60.1. 55 source files, 1007 documented symbols.

docs.title: fn gcd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Greatest common divisor of a and b; always non-negative (gcd(0, 0) == 0). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.gcd, which saturates the one unrepresentable case gcd(INT_MIN, k) = 2^63 to INT_MAX (documented). Complexity: O(log min(|a|, |b|)).

docs.title: fn lcm(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Least common multiple of |a| and |b|; always non-negative. 0 when either input is 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the true lcm exceeds Int range. Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.lcm. Complexity: O(gcd).

docs.title: fn egcd(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Int, Int)
docs.text: Extended Euclid: (g, x, y) with ax + by == g == gcd(a, b), g >= 0. For a == b == 0 returns (0, 1, 0). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.gcd_extended. Complexity: O(log min(|a|, |b|)).

docs.title: fn mod_inverse(a: Int, m: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Multiplicative inverse of a modulo m: x with (a * x) % m == 1. Returns None when gcd(a, m) != 1 (no inverse), when m == 0 (no modulus), and Some(0) for m == 1 (everything is 0 mod 1). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.mod_inverse. Complexity: O(log min(|a|, |m|)).

docs.title: fn crt(remainders: &Vec[Int], moduli: &Vec[Int]) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Chinese remainder theorem solution x with x % m_i == r_i for every i. Returns None when the moduli are not pairwise coprime, when the two slices differ in length, or when any slice is empty. The combination x = sum(r_i * M_i * inv(M_i mod m_i, m_i)) is built over M = prod(m_i); intermediate products can overflow Int for large moduli (documented; for pairwise-coprime small moduli the result is exact and in [0, M)). Complexity: O(n^2 * log max(m_i)) for the coprimality check plus O(n log) for the inverses.

docs.title: fn legendre_symbol(a: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Legendre symbol (a/p) for odd prime p: 1 when a is a quadratic residue modulo p, -1 when it is a non-residue, 0 when p divides a. Uses Euler's criterion a^((p-1)/2) mod p via modular exponentiation. p == 2 is handled directly (1 for odd a, 0 for even a); p <= 1 returns 0 (documented, no modulus). Complexity: O(log p).

docs.title: fn jacobi_symbol(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Jacobi symbol (a/n) for odd positive n; generalizes the Legendre symbol to composite odd n. Returns 0 for even or non-positive n (documented; the Jacobi symbol is undefined there) and 0 when gcd(a, n) != 1. Uses the standard quadratic-reciprocity reduction over the binary expansion. Complexity: O(log^2 n) worst case.

docs.title: fn binomial(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Binomial coefficient C(n, k). Returns 0 for invalid input (k < 0, k > n, n < 0) and 0 on overflow. Computed by the multiplicative form with an overflow guard on every step (result * (n - i + 1) / i stays in range). Complexity: O(min(k, n - k)).

docs.title: fn factorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Factorial of n (n!). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 on overflow (n >= 21 exceeds Int range). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn primorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Product of the first n primes (p_n#). Returns 0 for n <= 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the product exceeds Int range (n > 15). Complexity: O(n * sqrt(p_n)) trial division.

docs.title: fn nth_prime(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: The n-th prime, 1-indexed (nth_prime(1) == 2). Returns 0 for n <= 0. Trial-division sieve walking odd candidates. Complexity: O(n * sqrt(p_n)).

docs.title: fn integer_sqrt(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: floor(sqrt(n)) for n >= 0 via integer Newton iteration (no float, no overflow). Returns -1 for n < 0 (documented). Delegates to xiom.math.roots.integer_sqrt. Complexity: O(log n) iterations.

docs.title: fn next_power_of_two(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Smallest power of two >= n. Returns 1 for n <= 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the next power of two exceeds Int range (n > 2^62). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.next_power_of_two. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn is_power_of_two(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a positive power of two (is_power_of_two(0) == false, is_power_of_two(1) == true). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.is_power_of_two. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn is_perfect_square(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a perfect square (0 and 1 are squares). Returns false for n < 0. Uses the exact integer floor-sqrt check. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn group_theory(operation: fn(Int, Int) -> Int, elements: &Vec[Int], identity: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates the group axioms of (elements, operation, identity): closure, associativity, the two-sided identity law, and the existence of a two-sided inverse for every element. An empty carrier is vacuously a group of order zero. Complexity: O(|G|^3) plus inverse search O(|G|^3).

docs.title: fn ring_theory(op_add: fn(Int, Int) -> Int, op_mul: fn(Int, Int) -> Int, elements: &Vec[Int], zero: Int, one: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates the ring axioms of (elements, op_add, op_mul, zero, one): the abelian group (elements, op_add, zero), the monoid (elements, op_mul, one), and both distributive laws. Multiplication is not required to commute (non-commutative rings are accepted). NOTE: the parameter names avoid the compiler's built-in operator identifiers (add/mul resolve to Int/Float64 +/* regardless of the parameter, a name-resolution bug). Complexity: O(|R|^4).

docs.title: fn field_theory(op_add: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, op_mul: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, elements: &Vec[Float64], zero: Float64, one: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates the field axioms of (elements, op_add, op_mul, zero, one): the ring axioms plus a commutative multiplication and a multiplicative inverse for every element other than zero. Parameter names avoid the compiler's built-in operator identifiers (see ring_theory). Complexity: O(|F|^4).

docs.title: fn module_theory(action: fn(Int, Int) -> Int, ring: &Vec[Int], module_set: &Vec[Int]) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates the module axioms of (ring, module, action): the ring set is treated as the scalars and the module set as the vectors. Given the frozen signature (no scalar/vector addition functions), the check covers closure of the action (r*v in module for every r, v) and the unital law assuming ring[0] is the multiplicative identity of the ring (documented convention). Complexity: O(|R| * |M|).

docs.title: fn galois_theory(polynomial: &Vec[Int], prime: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff the polynomial (coefficients from the constant term) is separable over the field F_p: gcd(p, p') == 1 modulo p. Returns false for prime <= 1 (no field), or an empty/constant polynomial. Complexity: O(deg^2) modular Euclid.

docs.title: fn algebraic_number(alpha: Float64, polynomial: &Vec[Float64]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff alpha is a root of the polynomial (coefficients from the constant term) within 1e-9 tolerance. Returns false for an empty polynomial. Complexity: O(deg).

docs.title: fn commutative_algebra(ideal: &Vec[Int], ring: &Vec[Int], op_mul: fn(Int, Int) -> Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff the ideal is closed and absorbing in the ring under op_mul: the ideal is a subset of the ring, mul-closed on itself, and absorbing (r * i in the ideal for every ring element r and ideal element i). The frozen signature omits the ring addition, so the additive ideal laws are not checked (documented). Parameter name avoids the built-in operator identifiers (see ring_theory). Complexity: O(|R| * |I|).

docs.title: fn homological_algebra(chain: &Vec[Vec[Int]], maps: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Vec[Int]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff the chain complex squares to zero: for every chain group element v at stage i, mapsi+1 is the zero element (an empty vector or a vector of zeros) of stage i+2. Each chain row is a set of elements; a single element is wrapped in a one-element vector before applying the corresponding map. Complexity: O(stages * |chain| * cost(map)).

docs.title: fn category_theory(objects: &Vec[Int], morphisms: &Vec[(Int, Int)]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff (objects, morphisms) is a category: morphism endpoints lie in objects, an identity morphism (x, x) exists for every object, and the composition of any composable pair (a, b) and (b, c) exists as a morphism (a, c). With the pair representation composition is then automatically associative (documented). Complexity: O(|M|^2).

docs.title: fn universal_algebra(operation: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Int, arity: Int, elements: &Vec[Int]) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates an equational algebra signature with one operation of the given arity: the operation is closed on elements (the result of every arity- tuple of elements is itself an element). Returns false for arity <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(|A|^arity).

docs.title: fn representation_theory(group: &Vec[Int], op_mul: fn(Int, Int) -> Int, matrices: &Vec[Vec[Vec[Float64]]]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff the matrix assignment preserves group multiplication: assuming matrices[i] is the image of group[i] (documented correspondence), every pair (i, j) satisfies M[op_mul(g_i, g_j)] == M[i] * M[j] within 1e-9 tolerance. Parameter name avoids the built-in operator identifiers (see ring_theory). Returns false when the assignment does not cover the group. Complexity: O(|G|^3 * dim^3).

docs.title: fn lie_algebra(bracket: fn((Int, Int), (Int, Int)) -> (Int, Int), basis: &Vec[(Int, Int)]) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff the bilinear alternating bracket satisfies the Jacobi identity on the basis (vectors over Z, represented as (Int, Int) pairs): anticommutativity bracket(x, x) == (0, 0), bilinearity in both arguments (using pair addition), and bracket(x, bracket(y, z)) + bracket(y, bracket(z, x)) + bracket(z, bracket(x, y)) == (0, 0). Complexity: O(|B|^3).

docs.title: fn clifford_algebra(metric: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], dim: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Basis of the Clifford algebra for the diagonal metric: returns the 2^dim x 2^dim scalar table M with M[i][j] the coefficient such that blade_i * blade_j = M[i][j] * blade_{i xor j} (basis blades indexed by their generator bitmask, 1 = e_1e_2...). The metric is the quadratic form of the underlying space; only its diagonal is used (documented). Returns the empty matrix for dim < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(4^dim).
