docs.text: Wrap radians into (-pi, pi]. normalize_angle(-pi) == pi, normalize_angle(3*pi) == pi. Infinities pass through unchanged. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn normalize_angle_deg(deg: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Wrap degrees into (-180, 180]. normalize_angle_deg(-180) == 180, normalize_angle_deg(540) == 180. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn angle_diff(a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Signed angular difference a - b (radians), wrapped into (-pi, pi]. angle_diff(pi/2, 0) == pi/2. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn angle_lerp(a: Float64, b: Float64, t: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Shortest-path linear interpolation between angles a and b at parameter t: a + normalize_angle(b - a) * t. t in [0, 1] interpolates; angle_lerp(0, pi, 0.5) == pi/2. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn interpolation(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], point: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Interpolated value at point through the data (x, y): a natural cubic spline (the default smooth interpolant). Delegates to math.numerical.interp_cubic. Returns NaN for empty, mismatched, or fewer-than-2-points input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn extrapolation(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], point: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Extrapolated value at point outside the sample range [x[0], x[n-1]]: the linear extension of the two nearest end segments. Points inside the range are interpolated (cubic spline). Returns NaN for empty, mismatched, or fewer-than-2-points input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn polynomial_approx(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Least-squares polynomial fit of degree degree through (x, y): solves the (A^T A) c = A^T y normal equations over the Vandermonde basis. Returns the coefficient vector [c0, c1, ..., c_degree] with c0 the constant term; the empty vector for empty/mismatched input or degree < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n * d^2 + d^3).

docs.title: fn rational_approx(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], m: Int, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Rational approximation (num degree m, den degree n) of the data (x, y) by linearized least squares: y ~= (p0 + p1 x + ... + pm x^m) / (1 + q1 x + ... + qn x^n). Returns [p0..pm, q1..qn] (the leading denominator coefficient is fixed at 1); the empty vector for empty/mismatched input or m, n < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(k * (m+n)^2 + (m+n)^3).

docs.title: fn trigonometric_approx(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], harmonics: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Fourier series coefficients of the sampled data (x, y) with harmonics sine/cosine terms (the sample points are treated as uniformly spaced over one period). Returns [a0, a1..aH, b1..bH] where a0 is the DC term and a_k/b_k the cosine/sine amplitudes; the empty vector for empty/mismatched input or harmonics < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(k * H).

docs.title: fn exponential_approx(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Fitted exponential model y ~= a * e^(b x) of the data (x, y) by least squares on the linearized problem ln y = ln a + b x. Returns [a, b]. Non-positive y values are skipped; the empty vector is returned when no valid samples remain or the inputs mismatch (documented). Complexity: O(k).

docs.title: fn chebyshev_approx(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Chebyshev series coefficients of f on [a, b] up to degree: the Chebyshev-Gauss quadrature c_k = (2/N) sum_i f(c) T_k over the N mapped Chebyshev nodes (c_0 averaged). Returns [c0, c1, ..., c_degree]. The empty vector for degree < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(N * degree).

docs.title: fn least_squares(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Normal-equation least-squares solution of A x = b: solves (A^T A) x = A^T b by Gaussian elimination. Returns the empty vector for empty or mismatched input (documented). Complexity: O(m * n^2 + n^3). Least-squares solution of A x = b via the normal equations (A^T A x = A^T b). Returns the empty vector for empty/mismatched input, a singular normal matrix, or when the input matrix is read through a &Vec[Vec[Float64]] parameter (TODO(compiler): BUG 26 #1 -- by-ref nested float Vec element reads return garbage data pointers; len fields are correct). The matrix case is unimplementable until the compiler fix lands; the early-return paths are verified.

docs.title: fn minimax(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimax polynomial coefficients of degree degree for f on [a, b]. Computed by the Remez exchange algorithm (see remez); the returned vector holds power-basis coefficients from the constant term. Complexity: O(iters * degree^3).

docs.title: fn pade_approx(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, m: Int, n: Int, x0: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Pade approximant of order (m, n) of f at x0: builds the Taylor coefficients c0..c_{m+n} by central finite differences, then solves the Pade equations for the denominator q1..qn (q0 = 1) and folds the numerators p0..pm. Returns [p0..pm, q1..qn]; the empty vector for m, n < 0 (documented). NOTE: finite-difference Taylor coefficients limit accuracy (h = 1e-3); the approximation is most reliable for modest orders. Complexity: O((m+n) * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn remez(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Remez exchange algorithm producing the degree-degree minimax polynomial of f on [a, b]. Iterates reference points (initialised at the Chebyshev nodes) by solving the alternation linear system and exchanging with the largest deviation on a dense grid. Returns power-basis coefficients from the constant term; the empty vector for degree < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(iters * degree^3).

docs.title: fn spline_approx(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Cubic spline segment coefficients through the data (x, y): for n points the result holds n - 1 rows, each [a, b, c, d] describing p(x) = a + bt + ct^2 + d*t^3 with t = x - x_i (natural spline). The empty matrix for fewer than 2 points or mismatched input (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn best_approx(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, basis: &Vec[fn(Float64) -> Float64], a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Best least-squares coefficients of f in the given basis functions over [a, b]: samples f and the basis on a 64-point uniform grid and solves the normal equations. Returns the coefficient vector; the empty vector for an empty basis (documented). Complexity: O(64 * m^2 + m^3). Least-squares fit of f over [a, b] in the given function basis, via the normal equations sampled at 64 points. Returns the empty vector for an empty basis or when the basis is read through a &Vec[fn] parameter (TODO(compiler): BUG 26 #2 -- Vec[fn] element reads return garbage).

docs.title: fn gcd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Greatest common divisor of a and b; always non-negative. gcd(0, 0) == 0. The one unrepresentable case gcd(INT_MIN, k) = 2^63 saturates to INT_MAX (documented). Complexity: O(log min(|a|,|b|)).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn lcm(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Least common multiple of |a| and |b|; always non-negative. 0 when either input is 0, and 0 (documented overflow) when the true lcm exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(gcd).

docs.title: fn is_power_of_two(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a positive power of two. is_power_of_two(0) == false, is_power_of_two(1) == true. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn next_power_of_two(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Smallest power of two >= n. Returns 1 for n <= 0. When the next power of two would exceed Int range (n > 2^62) returns 0 (documented overflow). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn prev_power_of_two(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Largest power of two <= n. Returns 0 for n <= 0 (no positive power fits). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn gcd_extended(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Int, Int)
docs.text: Extended Euclid: returns (g, x, y) with ax + by == g == gcd(a, b). g is non-negative. For a == b == 0 returns (0, 1, 0). Complexity: O(log).

docs.title: fn mod_inverse(a: Int, m: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Multiplicative inverse of a mod m: x with (a * x) % m == 1. Returns None when gcd(a, m) != 1 (no inverse exists), when m == 0 (no modulus), and Some(0) for m == 1 (everything is 0 mod 1). Complexity: O(log min(a, m)).

docs.title: fn pow_mod(base: Int, exp: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: base^exp mod m via exponentiation by squaring. Result in [0, m). exp < 0 returns 0 (documented; only non-negative exponents are supported), m == 1 returns 0, m == 0 returns 0 (documented, division by zero guard). Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn is_odd(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is odd (sign-aware: -3 is odd).

docs.title: fn is_even(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is even (sign-aware: -4 is even).

docs.title: fn div_ceil(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Integer division rounded toward positive infinity (ceiling). ceil(-7, 2) == -3. Division by zero returns 0; INT_MIN / -1 returns INT_MIN (unrepresentable +2^63). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn div_floor(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Integer division rounded toward negative infinity (floor). floor(-7, 2) == -4. Division by zero returns 0; INT_MIN / -1 returns INT_MIN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn div_trunc(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Integer division truncated toward zero (native semantics). trunc(-7, 2) == -3. Division by zero returns 0; INT_MIN / -1 returns INT_MIN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mod_floor(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Modulus with result matching the divisor sign. mod_floor(-7, 2) == 1, mod_floor(7, -2) == -1. Division by zero returns 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mod_trunc(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Modulus with result matching the dividend sign (native semantics). mod_trunc(-7, 2) == -1, mod_trunc(7, -2) == 1. Division by zero returns 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn derivative(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: First derivative of f at x with step h (central difference). Delegates to xiom.math.differential.derivative. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn derivative_2nd(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Second derivative of f at x with step h. Delegates to xiom.math.differential.derivative2. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn derivative_3rd(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Third derivative of f at x with step h. Delegates to xiom.math.differential.derivative3. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn integrate(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Default high-accuracy definite integral of f over [a, b]. Delegates to xiom.math.integral.definite_integral. Complexity: depends on the integrand.

docs.title: fn integrate_trapezoid(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite trapezoidal rule with n subintervals. Delegates to xiom.math.integral.integrate_trapezoid. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_simpson(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite Simpson's rule with n subintervals (odd n reduced to n - 1). Delegates to xiom.math.integral.integrate_simpson. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_romberg(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Romberg integration of f over [a, b] to tolerance tol: builds the trapezoid Richardson table with up to 12 refinements and returns the best diagonal estimate. Returns 0.0 for tol <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(2^refinements). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the Romberg Richardson-table loops emit AVX-512 and crash with 0xC000001D (BUG 20) on Zen 2. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when the loops are not vectorized.

docs.title: fn integrate_gauss(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: n-point Gauss quadrature over [a, b] (Gauss-Legendre, n in 1..8, otherwise the 8-point rule). Delegates to xiom.math.integral.integrate_gauss_legendre. Complexity: O(n). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the cross-module delegation to the Gauss-Legendre recursion crashes at startup with 0xC000001D (BUG 20 AVX-512 codegen) even though the direct call works. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when cross-module Float64 delegation is safe.

docs.title: fn limit(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Two-sided limit of f as the argument approaches x, estimated by Richardson extrapolation of the symmetric averages at h = 1e-4 and h = 1e-5. A discontinuous or singular integrand yields an undefined (NaN or infinite) result. Complexity: O(1). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - crashes at startup with 0xC000001D (BUG 20 AVX-512 codegen on Zen 2). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when the extrapolation arithmetic is not vectorized.

docs.title: fn limit_left(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: One-sided limit of f from below (x approached from the left), estimated by linear Richardson extrapolation of f(x - h) at h = 1e-4 and h = 1e-5. Complexity: O(1). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same crash as limit (0xC000001D).

docs.title: fn limit_right(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: One-sided limit of f from above (x approached from the right), estimated by linear Richardson extrapolation of f(x + h) at h = 1e-4 and h = 1e-5. Complexity: O(1). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same crash as limit (0xC000001D).

docs.title: fn is_continuous(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff f is continuous at x within tol: the two-sided limit estimate and the value f(x) must both be defined and agree within tol. Returns false when either is NaN or infinite. Complexity: O(1). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - depends on limit, which crashes with 0xC000001D (see limit). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn gradient(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Gradient vector of the scalar field f at x (central partial differences, h = 1e-6). Delegates to xiom.math.differential.gradient. Complexity: O(n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the central partial-difference loops build and read Vec[Float64] perturbations, which crash with 0xC0000005 (BUG 12 family Vec[Float64] element reads) and 0xC000001D (BUG 20 loops). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when Vec[Float64] element reads and float loops are codegen-correct.

docs.title: fn partial_derivative(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64], i: Int, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Partial derivative of f with respect to x[i] at x with step h. Delegates to xiom.math.differential.partial_derivative. Complexity: O(f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn jacobian(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Jacobian matrix of the function vector fs at x. Delegates to xiom.math.differential.jacobian. Complexity: O(|fs| * n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn hessian(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Hessian matrix of second partials of the scalar field f at x: entry (i, j) is the mixed central difference with h = 1e-5. Complexity: O(n^2 * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn laplacian(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Laplacian of the scalar field f at x: sum of the second partials via the central difference, h = 1e-5. Complexity: O(n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn curl(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Curl of a 3D vector field f at x: (dFz/dy - dFy/dz, dFx/dz - dFz/dx, dFy/dx - dFx/dy) via central differences with h = 1e-5. Returns the empty vector when x has fewer than 3 components (documented). Complexity: O(f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn divergence(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Divergence of the vector field f at x: sum of dF_i/dx_i via central differences with h = 1e-5. Complexity: O(n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn logistic_map(r: Float64, x0: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Logistic map x_{k+1} = r x (1 - x) iterated n steps from x0. Returns the orbit (x0, x1, ..., x_{n-1}); empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn lorenz_system(sigma: Float64, rho: Float64, beta: Float64, x0: &Vec[Float64], steps: Int, dt: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Lorenz system dx/dt = sigma(y-x), dy/dt = x(rho-z) - y, dz/dt = xy - beta z integrated by explicit Euler. Returns steps + 1 rows of 3 components; empty for steps <= 0. Complexity: O(steps).

docs.title: fn rossler_system(a: Float64, b: Float64, c: Float64, x0: &Vec[Float64], steps: Int, dt: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Rossler system dx/dt = -y - z, dy/dt = x + a y, dz/dt = b + z(x - c) integrated by explicit Euler. Returns steps + 1 rows of 3 components; empty for steps <= 0. Complexity: O(steps).

docs.title: fn henon_map(a: Float64, b: Float64, x0: Float64, y0: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Henon map x' = 1 - a x^2 + y, y' = b x iterated n steps. Returns the orbit as (x, y) pairs; empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bifurcation_diagram(r_min: Float64, r_max: Float64, steps: Int, transients: Int) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Bifurcation-diagram points of the logistic map: for steps parameter values uniformly spread over [r_min, r_max], discard transients iterations then capture 10 orbit points as (r, x) pairs. Empty for degenerate input. Complexity: O(steps * (transients + 10)).

docs.title: fn lyapunov_exponent(orbit: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Estimated largest Lyapunov exponent of a 1-D time series from the mean log expansion ratio |x_{k+1} - x_k| / |x_k - x_{k-1}|. NaN for fewer than 3 points or a zero difference (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn strange_attractor(dynamics: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Trajectory of a chaotic attractor under the discrete dynamics map x <- dynamics(x), n steps. Returns n + 1 states; empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n * cost(dynamics)).

docs.title: fn fractal_dimension(points: &Vec[(Float64, Float64)]) -> Float64
docs.text: Box-counting fractal dimension of a 2-D point set: for four box sizes the occupied-box counts are fit by least squares on log-log scales. NaN for fewer than 2 points. Complexity: O(4 * n).

docs.title: fn mandelbrot_set(c_re: Float64, c_im: Float64, max_iter: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Escape iterations of c under z <- z^2 + c from z = 0; max_iter means the point is inside the set. Complexity: O(max_iter).

docs.title: fn julia_set(c_re: Float64, c_im: Float64, z_re: Float64, z_im: Float64, max_iter: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Escape iterations of z0 under z <- z^2 + c for fixed parameter c; max_iter means the point is inside the Julia set. Complexity: O(max_iter).

docs.title: fn burning_ship(c_re: Float64, c_im: Float64, max_iter: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Burning-ship fractal escape count: z <- (|re z| + i |im z|)^2 + c. Complexity: O(max_iter).

docs.title: fn newton_fractal(coeffs: &Vec[Float64], z: Float64, max_iter: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Index of the root that a point converges to under Newton iteration on the polynomial a x^2 + b x + c (given as coeffs [a, b, c]). Returns 0 or 1 for a non-degenerate quadratic (documented restriction to degree <= 2). Complexity: O(iters).

docs.title: fn tent_map(mu: Float64, x0: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Tent map x_{k+1} = mu * min(x, 1 - x) iterated n steps from x0. Returns the orbit; empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn permutations(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of k-permutations of n distinct items: n!/(n-k)!. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.falling_factorial (returns 0 for invalid input and on overflow). Complexity: O(k).

docs.title: fn combinations(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of k-combinations of n distinct items: C(n, k). Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.binomial. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k)).

docs.title: fn permutations_with_repetition(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of ordered k-selections from n items with repetition: n^k. Returns 0 for n < 0 or k < 0 (documented), 1 for k == 0, and 0 (documented overflow) when n^k exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(k).

docs.title: fn combinations_with_repetition(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of unordered k-selections from n items with repetition: C(n + k - 1, k). Returns 0 for n < 0 or k < 0 and on overflow (documented). Complexity: O(min(k, n-1)).

docs.title: fn derangements(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of derangements of n items (fixed-point-free permutations). Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.subfactorial. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bell_numbers(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bell number B(n): partitions of an n-set. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.bell. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn catalan_numbers(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Catalan number C_n. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.catalan. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn eulerian_numbers(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Eulerian number A(n, k): permutations of n items with exactly k ascents. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.eulerian. Complexity: O(n*k).

docs.title: fn stirling_numbers_1(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Signed Stirling numbers of the first kind s(n, k). Derived from the unsigned numbers: s(n,k) = (-1)^(n-k) * |s(n,k)|. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.stirling_first. Complexity: O(n*k).

docs.title: fn stirling_numbers_2(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k): partitions of an n-set into k blocks. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.stirling_second. Complexity: O(n*k).

docs.title: fn lah_numbers(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Lah numbers L(n, k). Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.lah. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k) + (n-k)).

docs.title: fn narayana_numbers(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Narayana numbers N(n, k). Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.narayana. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k)).

docs.title: fn fibonacci(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Fibonacci number F(n), 0-indexed: F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when F(n) exceeds Int range (n > 92). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fibonacci_start(a: Int, b: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Term n of the Fibonacci-like sequence beginning with a and b (term 0 is a, term 1 is b, each later term is the sum of the previous two). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the term exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn lucas(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Lucas number L(n): L(0) = 2, L(1) = 1, L(n) = L(n-1) + L(n-2). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when L(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn tribonacci(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Tribonacci number T(n): T(0) = T(1) = 0, T(2) = 1, T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when T(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn tetranacci(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Tetranacci number T(n): T(0) = T(1) = T(2) = 0, T(3) = 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous four. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when T(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn partitions(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of integer partitions p(n). Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.partition_count. Complexity: O(n * sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn integer_partitions(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All integer partitions of n as lists. Delegates to xiom.math.factorial.integer_partitions. Complexity: O(p(n) * n).

docs.title: fn compositions(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of compositions of n into exactly k positive parts: C(n-1, k-1). Returns 0 for n < 0, k <= 0, and k > n; n == 0, k == 0 yields 1 (the empty composition) and n == 0 with k > 0 yields 0. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k)).

docs.title: fn compositions_all(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Total number of compositions of n: 2^(n-1) for n >= 1, 1 for n == 0. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when 2^(n-1) exceeds Int range (n > 63). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn surjections(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of onto (surjective) functions from an n-set to a k-set: k! * S(n, k). Returns 0 for n < 0, k < 0, k > n, and 0 (documented overflow) when the count exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n*k + k).

docs.title: fn involutions(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of involutions on n elements (self-inverse permutations). Uses the recurrence I(n) = I(n-1) + (n-1)*I(n-2), I(0) = I(1) = 1. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when I(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn derangements_enum(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All fixed-point-free permutations of 1..n as lists. Returns the empty list for n < 0; n == 0 yields a single empty permutation. Complexity: O(!n * n).

docs.title: fn permutations_enum(elems: &Vec[Int]) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All permutations of elems as lists (n! results). Returns an empty list for an empty input. Complexity: O(n! * n).

docs.title: fn combinations_enum(elems: &Vec[Int], k: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All k-combinations of elems as lists (C(n, k) results). Returns an empty list for k < 0 or k > n. Complexity: O(C(n, k) * k).

docs.title: fn subsets_enum(elems: &Vec[Int], k: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All k-element subsets of elems as lists. Alias of combinations_enum. Complexity: O(C(n, k) * k).

docs.title: fn powerset_enum(elems: &Vec[Int]) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All subsets of elems as lists (2^n results). Returns an empty list when n > 20 (documented guard against an impractical 2^n result set). Complexity: O(2^n * n).

docs.title: type Complex
docs.text:
Complex number in Cartesian form: re + im * i.

Field Type re Float64 im Float64

docs.title: fn complex_new(re: Float64, im: Float64) -> Complex
docs.text: Create a complex number from real and imaginary parts. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_from_polar(r: Float64, theta: Float64) -> Complex
docs.text: Create a complex number from polar form (magnitude r, phase theta). O(1). z = r * (cos(theta) + i * sin(theta))

docs.title: fn complex_add(a: Complex, b: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Add two complex numbers: (a+bi) + (c+di) = (a+c) + (b+d)i. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_sub(a: Complex, b: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Subtract b from a: (a+bi) - (c+di) = (a-c) + (b-d)i. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_mul(a: Complex, b: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Multiply two complex numbers: (a+bi)(c+di) = (ac-bd) + (ad+bc)i. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_div(a: Complex, b: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Divide a by b: (a+bi)/(c+di) = (ac+bd)/(c2+d2) + i*(bc-ad)/(c2+d2). O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_scale(z: Complex, s: Float64) -> Complex
docs.text: Multiply a complex number by a real scalar. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_conj(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Conjugate: conj(a+bi) = a - bi. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_abs(z: Complex) -> Float64
docs.text: Absolute value (magnitude, modulus): |z| = sqrt(re2 + im2). O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_arg(z: Complex) -> Float64
docs.text: Argument (phase, angle): atan2(im, re) in radians (-pi, pi]. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_equals(a: Complex, b: Complex, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: Check if the complex number is approximately equal to another within epsilon. Uses absolute tolerance comparison. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_is_zero(z: Complex, eps: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: Check if the complex number is approximately zero within epsilon. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_exp(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex exponential: exp(a+bi) = e^a * (cos(b) + isin(b)). O(1). Euler's formula: e^(ib) = cos(b) + i*sin(b).

docs.title: fn complex_log(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex natural logarithm (principal branch). ln(z) = ln(|z|) + i * arg(z), where arg(z) in (-pi, pi]. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_pow(z: Complex, w: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex power: z^w = exp(w * ln(z)). Uses the principal branch of the logarithm. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_sqrt(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex square root (principal branch). Formula: sqrt(z) = sqrt(r) * (cos(theta/2) + i*sin(theta/2)) where r=|z|, theta=arg(z). Also handles negative re branch properly. O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_sin(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex sine: sin(a+bi) = sin(a)cosh(b) + icos(a)*sinh(b). O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_cos(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex cosine: cos(a+bi) = cos(a)cosh(b) - isin(a)*sinh(b). O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_tan(z: Complex) -> Complex
docs.text: Complex tangent: tan(z) = sin(z) / cos(z). Uses tan(a+bi) = (sin(2a) + i*sinh(2b)) / (cos(2a) + cosh(2b)). O(1).

docs.title: fn complex_to_string(z: Complex) -> Str
docs.text: Convert a complex number to a human-readable string "a + bi". Uses built-in to_string and manual decimal string building. O(n) in digits.

docs.title: fn infinity() -> Float64
docs.text: Positive infinity. Constructor fn (no literal syntax; BUG 3 -- see header).

docs.title: fn neg_infinity() -> Float64
docs.text: Negative infinity. Constructor fn (no literal syntax; BUG 3 -- see header).

docs.title: fn nan() -> Float64
docs.text: NAN (not-a-number) -- constructor fn (no NaN literal syntax exists; a const initializer can't hold the 0.0 / 0.0 expression -- const-fold handles literals only). IEEE semantics verified: nan() != nan() is true and math.is_nan(nan()) is true since BUG 19's fcmp-one/Str+Float64-concat defects were fixed (2026-08-11, 9c3a2f9e/88f924ea).

docs.title: fn pid_controller(kp: Float64, ki: Float64, kd: Float64, error: Float64, dt: Float64, integral: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: PID output and updated integral: the derivative term requires a previous error sample, which the frozen signature does not carry, so the output is the proportional + integral action kpe + kiI_new. Returns (output, integral_new) with integral_new = integral + error*dt. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn transfer_function(num: &Vec[Float64], den: &Vec[Float64], s: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Rational transfer function evaluated at s: num(s) / den(s) by Horner's scheme. NaN when the denominator vanishes. Complexity: O(degree).

docs.title: fn state_space(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], c: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], d: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> (Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]])
docs.text: Canonical state-space realization. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn observability(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], c: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the pair (A, C) is observable. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn controllability(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the pair (A, B) is controllable. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn stability_routh_hurwitz(den: &Vec[Float64]) -> Bool
docs.text: Routh-Hurwitz stability test on the denominator polynomial (coefficients highest power first). Returns false for an empty or non-positive leading coefficient. Routh table rows hold at most 4 entries (degree <= 8). Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn nyquist_plot(tf: fn(Float64) -> Float64, freqs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Nyquist curve points for a transfer function: the function is evaluated at each frequency and returned as (real, imag) with imag = 0 (a real-valued tf(omega) cannot carry phase in this signature; documented). Complexity: O(freqs * cost(tf)).

docs.title: fn bode_plot(tf: fn(Float64) -> Float64, freqs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Bode plot points: (frequency, magnitude) with the magnitude supplied by tf(omega). Complexity: O(freqs * cost(tf)).

docs.title: fn root_locus(num: &Vec[Float64], den: &Vec[Float64], gains: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Closed-loop pole locations (real, imag) over a list of gains for the loop transfer num/den: the closed-loop characteristic polynomial den + K num is solved for each gain (exact for degree <= 2; empty otherwise, documented). Complexity: O(gains * degree).

docs.title: fn pole_placement(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], poles: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: State-feedback gain K that places the poles. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn lqr(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], q: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], r: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> (Vec[Vec[Float64]], Vec[Vec[Float64]])
docs.text: LQR gain and value matrix. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn lqg(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], c: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], q: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], r: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: LQG controller combining LQR with a Kalman filter. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the matrices are Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn kalman_filter(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], c: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], y: &Vec[Float64], x_hat: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: One Kalman filtering step updating the state estimate. The measurement y and the prior estimate x_hat are used directly; the system matrices are not readable in this compiler build, so the update degenerates to a documented identity step (estimate unchanged). TODO(compiler): matrix inputs (A, B, C) unreadable (BUG 23 #1 residual).

docs.title: fn h_infinity(p: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: H-infinity optimal controller synthesis from a plant. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the plant is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn robust_control(nominal: fn(Float64) -> Float64, uncertainty: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: Small-gain robust stability check: the loop is robustly stable when max_omega |nominal(i omega)| * uncertainty < 1 over a log-spaced sweep of omega in [0.01, 100]. Complexity: O(50 * cost(nominal)).

docs.title: enum FloatClass
docs.text:
IEEE-754 bit decomposition and float classification (concrete Float64). frexp uses the [0.5, 1) fraction convention; ilogb/exponent use the [1, 2) mantissa convention (ilogb(8.0) == 3). NaN cannot be produced by this compiler (BUG 19); classify still detects a NaN input if one ever arrives. nextafter/nexttoward delegate to the exact arithmetic walk in math.primitives (exact for all finite normal/subnormal values). NOTE: requires/ensures clauses are runtime-enforced in this compiler and crash on violation, so all domain handling is guarded inside the bodies.

  • NaN
  • Infinity
  • Normal
  • Subnormal
  • Zero

docs.title: fn frexp(x: Float64) -> (Float64, Int)
docs.text: Split x into (fraction, exponent) with x == fraction * 2^exponent and fraction in [0.5, 1). frexp(8.0) == (0.5, 4), frexp(0.0) == (0.0, 0). Exact. Complexity: O(1074) worst case.

docs.title: fn ldexp(x: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: x * 2^n with a single rounding. For n beyond the representable exponent range the result is +-inf (n > 1100) or 0.0 (n < -1100); subnormal results flush correctly. Exact for all finite representable outcomes. Complexity: O(1074 + 1024).

docs.title: fn ilogb(x: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Binary exponent of x: the e with |x| == m * 2^e and 1 <= m < 2. ilogb(8.0) == 3, ilogb(0.5) == -1. For x == 0 returns INT_MIN (C FP_ILOGB0), for +-inf returns INT_MAX (C FP_ILOGB... convention). Complexity: O(1074) worst case.

docs.title: fn logb(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Binary exponent of x as a float: logb(8.0) == 3.0. For x == 0 returns -inf, for +-inf returns +inf (C semantics). Complexity: O(1074) worst case.

docs.title: fn scalbn(x: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: x * 2^n (FLT_RADIX == 2). Same semantics as ldexp. Complexity: O(ldexp).

docs.title: fn scalbln(x: Float64, n: Int64) -> Float64
docs.text: x * 2^n with a long (Int64) exponent. Same semantics as ldexp. Complexity: O(ldexp).

docs.title: fn significand(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Normalized fraction of x in [0.5, 1), sign preserved (frexp fraction). significand(8.0) == 0.5, significand(0.0) == 0.0; +-inf pass through. Complexity: O(1074) worst case.

docs.title: fn exponent(x: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Binary exponent of x. Alias of ilogb: exponent(8.0) == 3, exponent(0) == INT_MIN, exponent(+-inf) == INT_MAX. Complexity: O(ilogb).

docs.title: fn frexp_pure(x: Float64) -> (Float64, Int)
docs.text: frexp without libm. Identical semantics to frexp (the algorithm is exact integer scaling; no libm involved). Complexity: O(1074) worst case.

docs.title: fn ldexp_pure(x: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: ldexp without libm. x * 2^n via exact frexp decomposition and power-of-two scaling (all intermediate steps are exact or correctly flushed). For n > 1100 returns +-inf, for n < -1100 returns 0.0. Complexity: O(1074).

docs.title: fn is_normal(x: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff x is a normal (non-subnormal, non-zero, finite) Float64: 2^-1022 <= |x| < +inf. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn is_subnormal(x: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff x is a subnormal Float64: 0 < |x| < 2^-1022. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn classify(x: Float64) -> FloatClass
docs.text: Classify x into the FloatClass taxonomy: NaN, Infinity, Normal, Subnormal, Zero. NaN classification is unreachable from code compiled by this compiler (BUG 19 cannot produce NaN), but is detected if one arrives. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn nextafter(x: Float64, y: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Next representable Float64 from x toward y. Exact for all finite normal and subnormal values; delegates to math.primitives.nextafter (the same arithmetic ulp walk). nextafter(max, +inf) == +inf. TODO(compiler): an exact implementation normally uses a float<->int bitcast; the arithmetic form is exact for finite values (see primitives).

docs.title: fn nexttoward(x: Float64, y: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Next representable Float64 from x toward y. Float64 has no distinct long double, so this is the same operation as nextafter.

docs.title: fn derivative(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: First derivative of f at x by the central difference (f(x+h) - f(x-h))/2h. Returns 0.0 for h == 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn derivative2(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Second derivative of f at x by the central difference (f(x+h) - 2f(x) + f(x-h))/h^2. Returns 0.0 for h == 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn derivative3(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Third derivative of f at x by the four-point central difference (f(x+2h) - 2f(x+h) + 2f(x-h) - f(x-2h))/2h^3. Returns 0.0 for h == 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn finite_difference(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Central finite-difference approximation of the first derivative. Alias of derivative. Returns 0.0 for h == 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn richardson(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Richardson-extrapolated first derivative of f at x: repeatedly halves h and combines D(h) and D(h/2) as (4*D(h/2) - D(h))/3 until consecutive estimates agree within tol. Returns 0.0 for tol <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(halvings). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the halving iteration loop emits AVX-512 and crashes with 0xC000001D (BUG 20) on Zen 2. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when the loop is not vectorized.

docs.title: fn gradient(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Gradient vector of the scalar field f at x: each component is the central partial difference (f(x + h e_i) - f(x - h e_i))/2h with h = 1e-6. Complexity: O(n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the central partial-difference loops build and read Vec[Float64] perturbations, which crash with 0xC0000005 (BUG 12 family Vec[Float64] element reads) and 0xC000001D (BUG 20 loops). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when Vec[Float64] element reads and float loops are codegen-correct.

docs.title: fn jacobian(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Jacobian matrix of the function vector fs at x: entry (i, j) is the central partial difference of fs[i] with respect to x[j] (step h = 1e-6). Complexity: O(|fs| * n * f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn partial_derivative(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x: &Vec[Float64], i: Int, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Partial derivative of f with respect to x[i] at x by the central difference. Returns 0.0 for h == 0 and for i out of [0, len(x)) (documented). Complexity: O(f). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - same Vec[Float64]/loop crash as gradient (0xC0000005 / 0xC000001D). Keep the frozen signature.

docs.title: fn solve_ode_euler(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, y0: Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Explicit Euler steps of y' = f(t, y) from t0 to t1 in n steps. Returns n + 1 values (y(t0), ..., y(t1)); empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn solve_ode_rk4(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, y0: Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration of y' = f(t, y) in n steps. Returns n + 1 values; empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn solve_ode_rk45(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, y0: Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Adaptive Dormand-Prince (RK45) integration of y' = f(t, y) to tolerance tol. Returns the accepted trajectory (including the initial value) with step-size doubling/halving; at most 100000 internal steps. NaN for tol <= 0. Complexity: O(steps * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn solve_ode_adaptive(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, y0: Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Generic adaptive step-size integrator of y' = f(t, y) to tolerance tol. Uses the Dormand-Prince pair (same trajectory semantics as solve_ode_rk45). Complexity: O(steps * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn solve_ode_bdf(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, y0: Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Backward differentiation formula of order 1 (implicit backward Euler): y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1}) solved by fixed-point iteration (8 iterations per step). Returns n + 1 values; empty for n <= 0. Complexity: O(n * iters * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn solve_pde_fd(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, nx: Int, nt: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Explicit finite-difference (FTCS) solution of the 1-D heat equation u_t = u_xx + f(t, x) on x in [0, 1], u(x, 0) = sin(pi x), zero boundary conditions. Returns nt + 1 rows of nx + 1 spatial samples. Empty for degenerate input. Complexity: O(nt * nx).

docs.title: fn solve_pde_fem(f: fn(Float64, Float64) -> Float64, t0: Float64, t1: Float64, nx: Int, nt: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Linear finite-element (Galerkin, hat functions, lumped mass) solution of u_t = u_xx + f(t, x) on x in [0, 1] with zero boundaries and initial u = sin(pi x). Returns nt + 1 rows of nx + 1 samples. Empty for degenerate input. Complexity: O(nt * nx).

docs.title: fn exp(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: e^x. Returns +inf for x > 700 (overflow) and 0.0 for x < -745 (underflow) via libm. Complexity: O(1), libm exp.

docs.title: fn exp2(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: 2^x. Complexity: O(1), libm pow.

docs.title: fn exp10(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: 10^x. Complexity: O(1), libm pow.

docs.title: fn expm1(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: e^x - 1, accurate for small x. Uses the Taylor series x + x^2/2! + ... for |x| <= 1e-4 (where exp(x) - 1.0 suffers catastrophic cancellation) and libm exp - 1.0 otherwise. Returns -1.0 for x < -700 and +inf for x > 700. Complexity: O(20) series terms / O(1) libm.

docs.title: fn ln(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Natural logarithm of x. Requires x > 0. For x <= 0 returns NaN (IEEE semantics; BUG 19 fixed -- NaN ops now work).

docs.title: fn log2(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Base-2 logarithm of x. Requires x > 0. For x <= 0 returns NaN (see ln). Complexity: O(1), libm log2.

docs.title: fn log10(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Base-10 logarithm of x. Requires x > 0. For x <= 0 returns NaN (see ln). Complexity: O(1), libm log10.

docs.title: fn log1p(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: ln(1 + x), accurate for small x. Requires x > -1. Uses the alternating series x - x^2/2 + x^3/3 - ... for |x| <= 1e-4 and libm ln(1+x) otherwise. log1p(-1.0) == -inf (ln 0), log1p(x < -1) returns NaN (IEEE semantics).

docs.title: fn ln_1_plus(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: ln(1 + x), alias of log1p. See log1p for semantics and domain handling.

docs.title: fn pow(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: base^exp. Uses libm pow; negative bases require an integral exponent (libm semantics). For a negative base with a non-integral exponent returns NaN (IEEE semantics). Complexity: O(1), libm pow.

docs.title: fn pow_int(base: Float64, exp: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: base raised to an integer power via binary exponentiation (square-and- multiply). pow_int(2, 10) == 1024, pow_int(2, -2) == 0.25. 0^0 == 1.0; 0^negative == +inf; base^INT_MIN is handled by magnitude (|base| < 1 -> 0, == 1 -> 1, > 1 -> +inf). Complexity: O(log |exp|) multiplications.

docs.title: fn pow_float(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: base^exp for a float exponent. See pow for semantics and domain handling. Complexity: O(1), libm pow.

docs.title: fn sqrt_power(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
sqrt(base)^exp. Requires base >= 0. For base < 0 returns NaN (IEEE). Complexity: O(1), libm.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0 || result != result

docs.title: fn exp_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: e^x via the pure range-reduced Taylor series (math.exp_pure), no libm. Returns +inf for x > 700 and 0.0 for x < -700. Complexity: O(25 + log).

docs.title: fn ln_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Natural logarithm via the pure atanh series (math.ln_pure), no libm. Requires x > 0; for x <= 0 returns NaN (IEEE semantics).

docs.title: fn log2_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Base-2 logarithm via the pure series (math.log2_pure), no libm. Requires x > 0; for x <= 0 returns NaN (IEEE semantics).

docs.title: fn log10_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Base-10 logarithm via the pure series (math.log10_pure), no libm. Requires x > 0; for x <= 0 returns NaN (IEEE semantics).

docs.title: fn pow_pure(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: base^exp via the pure exp/ln series (math.pow_pure), no libm. Negative bases are handled before delegation because math.pow_pure declares requires: base >= 0.0 || exp integral (runtime-enforced in this compiler); a negative base with a non-integral exponent returns NaN (IEEE semantics). Complexity: O(ln + exp).

docs.title: fn factorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: n! for n >= 0. Returns 0 for n < 0 (documented) and 0 (documented overflow) when the true value exceeds Int range (n > 20). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn double_factorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Double factorial n!! = product of n, n-2, n-4, ... down to 1 (odd n) or 2 (even n). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n/2).

docs.title: fn subfactorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Derangement count !n: the number of fixed-point-free permutations of n items. Uses the recurrence D(0)=1, D(1)=0, D(n) = (n-1)(D(n-1)+D(n-2)). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when D(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn multifactorial(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: k-th multifactorial of n: product n, n-k, n-2k, ... down to the smallest positive term. Returns 0 for n < 0 or k <= 0 (documented) and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n/k).

docs.title: fn binomial(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Binomial coefficient C(n, k). Returns 0 for invalid input (n < 0, k < 0, k > n) and 0 (documented overflow) when C(n, k) exceeds Int range. Uses the multiplicative form with a per-step overflow guard. Complexity: O(min(k, n - k)).

docs.title: fn binomial_coeff(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Alias of binomial. Complexity: O(min(k, n - k)).

docs.title: fn multinomial(n: Int, ks: &Vec[Int]) -> Int
docs.text: Multinomial coefficient n!/(k1! k2! ... km!) where the ki sum to n. Returns 0 when the entries are negative or do not sum to n, and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Computed as a chain of binomial coefficients. Complexity: O(m * min(k_i, ...)).

docs.title: fn falling_factorial(x: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Falling factorial x * (x-1) * ... * (x-k+1). Returns 0 for k < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the magnitude exceeds Int range. k == 0 gives 1. Complexity: O(k).

docs.title: fn rising_factorial(x: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Rising factorial x * (x+1) * ... * (x+k-1). Returns 0 for k < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the magnitude exceeds Int range. k == 0 gives 1. Complexity: O(k).

docs.title: fn stirling_first(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Unsigned Stirling number of the first kind s(n, k): permutations of n items with exactly k cycles. Row DP over s(n,k) = s(n-1,k-1) + (n-1)s(n-1,k) with s(0,0) = 1. Returns 0 for invalid input (n < 0, k < 0, k > n) and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(nk).

docs.title: fn stirling_second(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Stirling number of the second kind S(n, k): partitions of an n-element set into k nonempty blocks. Row DP over S(n,k) = kS(n-1,k) + S(n-1,k-1) with S(0,0) = 1. Returns 0 for invalid input and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(nk).

docs.title: fn bell(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bell number B(n): the number of partitions of an n-element set. Computed via the Aitken / Bell triangle, whose rightmost entry of row k is B(k+1) (row 0 is [1] and B(0) = B(1) = 1), so the value is the last entry of row n - 1. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when B(n) exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn catalan(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Catalan number C_n = C(2n, n)/(n+1). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range (n > 33). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn eulerian(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Eulerian number A(n, k): permutations of n items with exactly k ascents. Row DP over A(n,k) = (n-k)A(n-1,k-1) + (k+1)A(n-1,k) with A(0,0) = 1 and A(n,n) = 0. Returns 0 for invalid input and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n*k).

docs.title: fn narayana(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Narayana number N(n, k) = C(n, k) * C(n, k-1) / n. Returns 0 for invalid input (n <= 0, k <= 0, k > n) and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k)).

docs.title: fn lah(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Lah number L(n, k) = C(n, k) * C(n-1, k-1) * (n-k)!. Returns 0 for invalid input (n <= 0, k <= 0, k > n) and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(min(k, n-k) + (n-k)).

docs.title: fn motzkin(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Motzkin number M_n (lattice paths / non-crossing partitions). Uses the closed recurrence M(n) = ((2n+1)M(n-1) + (3n-3)M(n-2))/(n+2), M(0) = M(1) = 1. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when M_n exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn schroeder(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Large Schroder number S_n. Uses S(n) = S(n-1) + sum_{k=0..n-1} S(k)*S(n-1-k), S(0) = 1. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when S_n exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn partition_count(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of integer partitions p(n). Uses the Euler pentagonal-number recurrence p(n) = sum_{k != 0} (-1)^(k+1) p(n - k(3k-1)/2). Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when p(n) exceeds Int range (n > 255). Complexity: O(n * sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn integer_partitions(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: All integer partitions of n as lists (each partition non-increasing, starting from the largest part; the result order is unspecified). Returns an empty list for n < 0; n == 0 yields a single empty partition. Complexity: O(p(n) * n).

docs.title: fn derangements(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of derangements of n items (fixed-point-free permutations). Alias of subfactorial. Returns 0 for n < 0 and 0 (documented overflow). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bell_triangle(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: Bell triangle rows up to n: rows 0..n inclusive. Row 0 is [1]; each later row starts with the previous row's last entry and continues with the sum of the entry to its left and the one above-left, so the rightmost entry of row k is B(k+1) and the leftmost is B(k). Returns an empty list for n < 0. Cells that would overflow Int are stored as 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn pv(rate: Float64, nper: Float64, pmt: Float64, fv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Present value of an annuity and lump sum: PV = -(FV + pmt((1+r)^n-1)/r) / (1+r)^n. r == 0 uses PV = -(FV + pmtn). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fv(rate: Float64, nper: Float64, pmt: Float64, pv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Future value of an annuity and lump sum: FV = PV (1+r)^n + pmt((1+r)^n-1) / r. r == 0 uses FV = PV + pmtn. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn npv(rate: Float64, cashflows: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Net present value of a cashflow series discounted from t = 0 (the first element is the undiscounted cashflow at time zero). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn irr(cashflows: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Internal rate of return: the rate r with npv(r, cashflows) == 0, found by bisection over [-0.99, 10] (200 iterations). NaN when no sign change exists. Complexity: O(iters * n).

docs.title: fn mirr(cashflows: &Vec[Float64], finance_rate: Float64, reinvest_rate: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Modified internal rate of return: MIRR = ((FV_positive / PV_negative)^(1/n) - 1) where positive cashflows compound at reinvest_rate and negative ones discount at finance_rate. NaN when no negative cashflow exists. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn pmt(rate: Float64, nper: Float64, pv: Float64, fv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Periodic payment of an annuity: pmt = (fv - pv (1+r)^n) r / ((1+r)^n - 1); r == 0 uses (fv - pv)/n. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn ipmt(rate: Float64, per: Int, nper: Float64, pv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Interest portion of the payment in period per (1-based) for a loan of pv amortized at rate over nper periods (fv = 0). Complexity: O(per).

docs.title: fn ppmt(rate: Float64, per: Int, nper: Float64, pv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Principal portion of the payment in period per. Complexity: O(per).

docs.title: fn nper(rate: Float64, pmt: Float64, pv: Float64, fv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Number of periods to reach fv from pv paying pmt per period: n = ln((pmt - fv r) / (pmt + pv r)) / ln(1 + r). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn rate(nper: Float64, pmt: Float64, pv: Float64, fv: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Interest rate implied by an annuity: bisection on the fv identity over [-0.999, 10] (200 iterations). NaN when no root exists. Complexity: O(200).

docs.title: fn annuity(rate: Float64, nper: Float64, pmt: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Present value of a level annuity paying pmt for nper periods at rate. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn perpetuity(pmt: Float64, rate: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Present value of a level perpetuity pmt / rate. NaN for rate <= 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bond_price(face: Float64, coupon: Float64, ytm: Float64, n: Int, freq: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Price of a coupon bond with face, annual coupon rate, yield to maturity, n years and freq coupons per year. Complexity: O(n * freq).

docs.title: fn bond_yield(face: Float64, coupon: Float64, price: Float64, n: Int, freq: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Yield to maturity of a coupon bond, found by bisection on the price equation over [-0.999, 10] (200 iterations). NaN when no root exists. Complexity: O(200 * n * freq).

docs.title: fn duration(face: Float64, coupon: Float64, ytm: Float64, n: Int, freq: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Macaulay duration of a coupon bond (years). Complexity: O(n * freq).

docs.title: fn convexity(face: Float64, coupon: Float64, ytm: Float64, n: Int, freq: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Convexity of a coupon bond (years squared). Complexity: O(n * freq).

docs.title: fn option_call(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Black-Scholes price of a European call. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_put(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Black-Scholes price of a European put. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_call_delta(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Delta of a European call: N(d1). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_put_delta(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Delta of a European put: N(d1) - 1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_gamma(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Gamma of a European option: phi(d1) / (S sigma sqrt(T)). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_theta(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Theta of a European call (per year): -(S phi(d1) sigma)/(2 sqrt(T)) - r K e^{-rT} N(d2). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_vega(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Vega of a European option: S phi(d1) sqrt(T) / 100 (per 1% volatility). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn option_rho(s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64, sigma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Rho of a European call: K T e^{-rT} N(d2) / 100. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn implied_volatility(market: Float64, s: Float64, k: Float64, t: Float64, r: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Black-Scholes implied volatility for a European call price, by Newton iteration (100 iterations from sigma = 0.2). NaN when no solution is found (e.g. an arbitrage-violating price). Complexity: O(100).

docs.title: fn cagr(begin_value: Float64, end_value: Float64, years: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Compound annual growth rate (end/begin)^(1/years) - 1. NaN for years <= 0 or non-positive begin. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn sharpe_ratio(returns: &Vec[Float64], rf: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Sharpe ratio (mean(returns) - rf) / sample_stddev(returns). NaN for fewer than 2 returns. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn sortino_ratio(returns: &Vec[Float64], rf: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Sortino ratio (mean(returns) - rf) / downside_deviation(returns, rf), where the downside deviation is the sqrt of the mean of squared returns below rf. NaN for fewer than 2 returns. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn calmar_ratio(returns: &Vec[Float64], max_drawdown: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Calmar ratio annualized mean return / |max drawdown|. NaN for a zero drawdown or fewer than 2 returns. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn value_at_risk(returns: &Vec[Float64], alpha: Float64, method: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Value at risk at confidence alpha: method 0 = historical quantile, method 1 = parametric (normal) quantile. Returns a positive loss. Complexity: O(n log n) historical / O(n) parametric.

docs.title: fn cvar(returns: &Vec[Float64], alpha: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Conditional value at risk: mean of the returns below the alpha-VaR level. NaN for fewer than 1 tail observation. Complexity: O(n log n).

docs.title: fn drawdown(returns: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Drawdown series of the returns (cumulative product minus 1, then peak-to-trough). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn beta(asset_returns: &Vec[Float64], market_returns: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Systematic risk of an asset versus the market: covariance / market variance. NaN for fewer than 2 observations or zero market variance. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn alpha(asset_returns: &Vec[Float64], market_returns: &Vec[Float64], rf: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Jensen's alpha: mean(asset) - (rf + beta * (mean(market) - rf)). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn treynor_ratio(returns: &Vec[Float64], beta: Float64, rf: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Treynor ratio (mean(returns) - rf) / beta. NaN for beta <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_set(universe: &Vec[Int], membership: fn(Int) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Membership degrees of the universe elements under the membership fn. Returns an empty vector for an empty universe. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn membership(set: &Vec[Float64], element: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Membership degree of element in a fuzzy set; elements outside the set's range yield 0.0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_logic(a: Float64, b: Float64, op: Str) -> Float64
docs.text: Triangular norm/conorm or negation of two truth values, selected by op: "and" -> min, "or" -> max, "not" -> 1 - a, "prod" -> ab, "sum" -> a + b - ab (probabilistic or). Unknown op returns NaN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_intersection(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Pointwise minimum (intersection) of two fuzzy sets; empty on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_union(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Pointwise maximum (union) of two fuzzy sets; empty on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_complement(a: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Pointwise complement 1 - a of a fuzzy set. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_relation(r: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates that every membership degree of the fuzzy relation matrix lies in [0, 1]. docs.title: fn fuzzy_composition(r: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], s: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Max-min composition of two fuzzy relations. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn defuzzification(set: &Vec[Float64], universe: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Centroid (center-of-gravity) defuzzification of a fuzzy set over the universe values: sum(u_i m_i) / sum(m_i). NaN when the total membership is zero or the lengths differ. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_inference(rules: &Vec[Str], facts: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Aggregated conclusion degrees from fuzzy rules ("a:b:s" = antecedent, consequent, strength): out[j] = max over rules with consequent j of min(facts[a], s). NaN facts propagate as NaN conclusions. Complexity: O(rules).

docs.title: fn mamdani(rules: &Vec[Str], inputs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Mamdani-style inference: min implication with max aggregation over the same "a:b:s" rule convention (alias of fuzzy_inference). Complexity: O(rules).

docs.title: fn sugeno(rules: &Vec[Str], inputs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Sugeno-style weighted crisp output: rules are decimal strengths s_i and the result is sum(s_i * inputs_i) / sum(s_i). NaN when the weight sum is zero or the rule format is invalid. Complexity: O(rules).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_control(setpoint: Float64, measurement: Float64, kp: Float64, ki: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Fuzzy logic controller output (position form): kp * error + ki * error with error = setpoint - measurement (integral term approximated proportionally; documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_decision(alternatives: &Vec[Float64], weights: &Vec[Float64]) -> Int
docs.text: Index of the best fuzzy-weighted alternative: argmax of alternatives_i * weights_i. Returns -1 for empty or mismatched input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn nash_equilibrium(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[(Float64, Float64)]
docs.text: Mixed Nash equilibria of a two-player bimatrix game. docs.title: fn minimax(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Minimax value of a zero-sum game. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see nash_equilibrium (payoff matrix reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn alpha_beta(game: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Float64, depth: Int, alpha: Float64, beta: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Minimax search with alpha-beta pruning over a game tree given by game(move_sequence) -> terminal value. Searches to fixed depth; at a terminal or depth-0 node the game value is returned. Complexity: O(branch^depth) with pruning.

docs.title: fn dominant_strategy(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Index of a strictly dominant strategy, if any. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see nash_equilibrium (payoff matrix reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn pareto_optimal(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Indices of Pareto-optimal strategy profiles. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see nash_equilibrium (payoff matrix reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn cooperative_game(v: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Float64, n: Int) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: Grand-coalition value v(all players) and a feasible imputation: the tuple is (grand_coalition_value, equal-share imputation value). Complexity: O(1) plus the cost of v on the grand coalition.

docs.title: fn shapley_value(v: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Shapley value of each of the n players: the average marginal contribution over all player permutations (exact for n <= 6 via permutations_enum, approximate for larger n by iterating cyclic shifts). Complexity: O(n! * n) exact / O(n^2) approximate.

docs.title: fn game_core(v: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Float64, n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Imputations in the core of a cooperative game. For n == 2 the core is the set of allocations (x1, x2) with x1 + x2 = v({0,1}) and x_i >= v({i}); the function returns a sample of its extreme points. For other n the function returns a documented greedy sample. Complexity: O(2^n * v) for small n.

docs.title: fn auction(bids: &Vec[Float64], reserve: Float64) -> (Float64, Int)
docs.text: Winning price and winner index of a first-price auction with a reserve: the highest bid at or above the reserve wins at its own bid. Returns (price, winner_index) or (0, -1) when no bid clears the reserve. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn mechanism_design(type_space: &Vec[Float64], values: fn(Int) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Dominant-strategy incentive-compatible allocation: bidder i receives a share of the type-space value proportional to values(i). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn evolutionary_game(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], population: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Next-generation population shares under replicator dynamics: x_i' = x_i (f_i - mean) where f_i is the i-th strategy's expected payoff.
