docs.title: fn replicator_dynamics(payoffs: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], population: &Vec[Float64], steps: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Iterated replicator dynamics over steps generations. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see evolutionary_game (payoff matrix reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn prisoner_dilemma(defect: Float64, cooperate: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: Payoffs of the one-shot prisoner's dilemma: the tuple is (mutual_cooperation, mutual_defection) payoff. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: type WeightedGraph
docs.text:
A graph: n vertices (implicitly 0..n-1), an edge list of (u, v) pairs, a parallel weight list (scaled by 1e5), and a directedness flag.

Field Type n Int edges Vec[(Int, Int)] weights Vec[Int] directed Bool

docs.title: fn graph_new() -> WeightedGraph
docs.text: Create an empty graph. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn graph_add_vertex(g: &mut WeightedGraph, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Add vertex v (grows n to v + 1; vertices are implicit ids). Returns true. Complexity: O(v - n).

docs.title: fn graph_add_edge(g: &mut WeightedGraph, u: Int, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Add an unweighted edge (u, v) (weight 1.0). Adds the vertices first; an undirected graph also stores the reverse edge. Returns false for negative ids. Complexity: O(1) amortized.

docs.title: fn graph_add_weighted_edge(g: &mut WeightedGraph, u: Int, v: Int, w: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: Add a weighted edge (u, v) with weight w (rounded to 1e-5 resolution). Complexity: O(1) amortized.

docs.title: fn graph_remove_vertex(g: &mut WeightedGraph, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Remove vertex v and all incident edges. Returns false when v is absent. Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_remove_edge(g: &mut WeightedGraph, u: Int, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Remove the edge (u, v); an undirected graph removes the reverse too. Returns false when no such edge exists. Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_has_vertex(g: &WeightedGraph, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether v is present. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn graph_has_edge(g: &WeightedGraph, u: Int, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the edge (u, v) is present (either direction for undirected). Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_degree(g: &WeightedGraph, v: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Degree of vertex v (undirected degree counts once per incident edge). Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_vertices(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: All vertices as ids [0, n - 1]. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn graph_edges(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[(Int, Int)]
docs.text: All edges as (u, v) pairs (duplicated pairs for undirected graphs, one per stored direction). Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_adjacent(g: &WeightedGraph, u: Int, v: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether u and v are neighbors. Complexity: O(edges).

docs.title: fn graph_dfs(g: &WeightedGraph, start: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Depth-first vertex order from start. Returns the empty vector for a start outside the graph. Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_bfs(g: &WeightedGraph, start: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Breadth-first vertex order from start. Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_dijkstra(g: &WeightedGraph, source: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Shortest-path distances from source via Dijkstra's algorithm (edge-list scanning; O(V^2 + E) worst case). Unreachable vertices get _INF. Complexity: O(V^2 + E).

docs.title: fn graph_bellman_ford(g: &WeightedGraph, source: Int) -> Option[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Shortest-path distances from source via Bellman-Ford; None when a negative cycle is reachable. Complexity: O(V * E).

docs.title: fn graph_floyd_warshall(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: All-pairs shortest-path distances via repeated Bellman-Ford-style edge relaxation from every source. The result is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] distance matrix (callers can only rely on its shape; element reads of module-returned nested float Vecs are unreliable in this compiler build). Complexity: O(V^2 * E).

docs.title: fn graph_astar(g: &WeightedGraph, start: Int, goal: Int, h: fn(Int, Int) -> Float64) -> Option[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: A* path from start to goal using the heuristic h(vertex, goal); returns the vertex sequence (inclusive) or None when no path exists. Complexity: O(V^2 + E) (linear scan open set).

docs.title: fn graph_prim(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Option[Vec[(Int, Int)]]
docs.text: Minimum spanning tree edges by Prim's algorithm (edge-list scanning); None for a disconnected or empty graph. Complexity: O(V^2 + E).

docs.title: fn graph_kruskal(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Option[Vec[(Int, Int)]]
docs.text: Minimum spanning tree edges by Kruskal's algorithm (union-find with min-weight edge selection; compares scaled-integer weights directly). None for a disconnected graph. Complexity: O(V * E).

docs.title: fn graph_tarjan_scc(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: Strongly connected components by Tarjan's algorithm (iterative). Each component is one inner vector. Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_kosaraju_scc(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: Strongly connected components by Kosaraju's algorithm (two DFS passes). Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_topological_sort(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Option[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: Linear ordering of a directed acyclic graph (Kahn's algorithm); None when the graph has a cycle. Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_is_connected(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the graph is connected (a single BFS reaches every vertex). Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_is_cyclic(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the graph contains a cycle (DFS with colors; undirected uses the parent check). Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_is_bipartite(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the vertices split into two independent sets (BFS 2-coloring). Complexity: O(V + E).

docs.title: fn graph_isomorphic(g1: &WeightedGraph, g2: &WeightedGraph) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether g1 and g2 are isomorphic. Checks vertex count, edge count, and degree sequence; for n <= 6 an exact permutation test is performed. Complexity: O(n! * n^2) for small n, O(n^2) otherwise.

docs.title: fn graph_color(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Greedy vertex coloring (smallest available color per vertex in id order). Returns one color per vertex (0-based). Complexity: O(V * E).

docs.title: fn graph_max_flow(g: &WeightedGraph, s: Int, t: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Maximum flow from s to t by Edmonds-Karp (BFS augmenting paths) over the edge list with parallel residual-capacity tracking. Complexity: O(V * E^2).

docs.title: fn graph_min_cut(g: &WeightedGraph, s: Int, t: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Minimum s-t cut: the vertices reachable from s in the residual graph after the maximum flow (the S side of the min cut). Complexity: O(V * E^2).

docs.title: fn graph_hamiltonian_path(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Option[Vec[Int]]
docs.text: Hamiltonian path if one exists (exhaustive DFS; practical for n <= 12). Complexity: O(n!).

docs.title: fn graph_tsp(g: &WeightedGraph) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Traveling-salesperson tour by the nearest-neighbor heuristic: visits every vertex once starting from vertex 0 and returns to the start. Returns the tour as a vertex sequence (length n + 1). Complexity: O(n^2 + n * E).

docs.title: fn sinh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic sine of x. sinh(0.0) == 0.0; |x| > ~710 overflows to +-inf. Complexity: O(1), libm exp.

docs.title: fn cosh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic cosine of x. cosh(0.0) == 1.0; |x| > ~710 overflows to +inf. Complexity: O(1), libm exp.

docs.title: fn tanh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic tangent of x. tanh(0.0) == 0.0; saturates to +-1.0 for |x| > 20. Uses (exp(2x)-1)/(exp(2x)+1) for stability. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn csch(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic cosecant, 1/sinh(x). csch(0.0) == +inf (native 1.0/0.0). Complexity: O(1), libm exp.

docs.title: fn sech(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic secant, 1/cosh(x). Always finite (cosh > 0). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn coth(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic cotangent, 1/tanh(x). coth(0.0) == +inf (native 1.0/0.0). Complexity: O(1), libm exp.

docs.title: fn asinh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Inverse hyperbolic sine: ln(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)). Odd function. For |x| > 1e150 uses ln(|x|) + ln 2 (avoids x^2 overflow and cancellation). asinh(1.0) == 0.881373587019543. Complexity: O(1), libm ln/sqrt.

docs.title: fn acosh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Inverse hyperbolic cosine: ln(x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)). Requires x >= 1. For x < 1 returns NaN (IEEE semantics). For x > 1e150 uses ln(x) + ln 2 (avoids overflow). acosh(1.0) == 0.0, acosh(cosh(1.0)) == 1.0. Complexity: O(1), libm ln/sqrt.

docs.title: fn atanh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Inverse hyperbolic tangent: 0.5 * ln((1+x)/(1-x)). Requires |x| < 1. For |x| > 1 returns NaN (IEEE semantics); atanh(1.0) == +inf and atanh(-1.0) == -inf (native, ln 0/inf). atanh(0.0) == 0.0. Complexity: O(1), libm ln.

docs.title: fn sinh_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic sine via the pure exp series (math.exponential.exp_pure), no libm. sinh_pure(0.0) == 0.0. Complexity: O(exp_pure).

docs.title: fn cosh_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic cosine via the pure exp series, no libm. cosh_pure(0.0) == 1.0. Complexity: O(exp_pure).

docs.title: fn tanh_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic tangent via pure sinh/cosh series, no libm. Saturates to +-1.0 for |x| > 20. tanh_pure(0.0) == 0.0. Complexity: O(exp_pure).

docs.title: fn entropy(probs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Shannon entropy H(p) = -sum p_i log2 p_i (bits). NaN for a negative probability. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn joint_entropy(p_joint: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Entropy of a joint distribution over pairs: H(X, Y) = -sum p_ij log2 p_ij. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the joint distribution is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn conditional_entropy(p_joint: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Conditional entropy H(X|Y) = -sum_ij p_ij log2(p_ij / p_j) (bits). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see joint_entropy (matrix element reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn mutual_information(p_joint: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Mutual information I(X; Y) = sum_ij p_ij log2(p_ij / (p_i p_j)) (bits). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see joint_entropy (matrix element reads return garbage in this compiler build).

docs.title: fn kl_divergence(p: &Vec[Float64], q: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Kullback-Leibler divergence D(p || q) = sum p_i log2(p_i / q_i) (bits). NaN for a zero q_i with positive p_i. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn js_divergence(p: &Vec[Float64], q: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Jensen-Shannon divergence JSD(p || q) = 0.5 D(p || m) + 0.5 D(q || m) with m = (p + q)/2 (bits; values in [0, 1]). NaN on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn cross_entropy(p: &Vec[Float64], q: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Cross entropy H(p, q) = -sum p_i log2 q_i (bits). NaN for a zero q_i with positive p_i. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn perplexity(probs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Perplexity = 2^H (exponential of the entropy in bits). NaN for negative probabilities. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn self_information(p: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Self information -log2(p) of a single event (bits). p <= 0 returns +inf. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn entropy_rate(p_transition: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], stationary: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Entropy rate of a stationary Markov source: sum_j s_j H(row j of the transition matrix). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the transition matrix is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn channel_capacity(p_transition: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Channel capacity by the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the channel matrix is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build (verified by minimal probe); the resulting q values become NaN and violate math.ln's positivity requirement. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn data_compression_bound(dist: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Lower bound on the average code length for a distribution: its entropy (bits). NaN for negative probabilities. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn huffman_coding(probs: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[(Int, Str)]
docs.text: Prefix-free Huffman code for a probability distribution. The result holds (symbol index, codeword) pairs with codewords of "0"/"1"; NaN inputs or an empty distribution yield an empty result. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn arithmetic_coding(probs: &Vec[Float64], seq: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64
docs.text: Arithmetic coding of the symbol sequence seq under the distribution probs: returns the midpoint of the final code interval in [0, 1). Invalid symbols (outside the distribution) contribute nothing (documented). Complexity: O(len(seq) * n).

docs.title: fn integrate_riemann(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Riemann sum over n subintervals using left endpoints. Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_trapezoid(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite trapezoidal rule over n subintervals. Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_midpoint(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite midpoint rule over n subintervals. Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_simpson(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite Simpson's rule over n subintervals. An odd n is reduced to n - 1 (documented). Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn integrate_adaptive(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Adaptive Simpson quadrature refining [a, b] until the local error estimate falls under tol (depth-capped to 40 refinements per interval). Returns 0.0 for tol <= 0 (documented). Complexity: depends on the integrand's smoothness; O(refinements). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the recursive refinement threading a fn-typed param together with Float64 parameters makes any program that links it crash at startup with 0xC000001D (BUG 20 AVX-512 codegen on Zen 2), even before main. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when the vectorizer cannot touch this shape.

docs.title: fn integrate_gauss_legendre(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: n-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature over [a, b]. Supported point counts are 1..8 (standard node/weight tables); other counts fall back to the 8-point rule (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn definite_integral(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Default high-accuracy definite integral over [a, b]. Returns 0.0 when a == b. NOTE: the adaptive-Simpson implementation crashes at startup with 0xC000001D in this build (BUG 20 AVX-512 codegen on Zen 2; see integrate_adaptive), so this currently falls back to the composite trapezoidal rule with 1000 subintervals (~1e-6 accuracy for smooth integrands). Complexity: O(1000).

docs.title: fn asin(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arcsine of x in radians, result in [-pi/2, pi/2]. For x outside [-1, 1] returns NaN (documented domain error). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn acos(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arccosine of x in radians, result in [0, pi]. For x outside [-1, 1] returns NaN (documented domain error). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn atan(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arctangent of x in radians, result in (-pi/2, pi/2). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn atan2(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Four-quadrant arctangent of y/x in radians. When both y and x are zero returns NaN (documented; the angle is undefined there). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn atan2_pure(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Four-quadrant arctangent of y/x computed purely by series (xiom.math's pure atan, no libm). When both y and x are zero returns NaN (documented). Complexity: O(series terms).

docs.title: fn asin_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arcsine of x via the identity asin(x) = atan(x/sqrt(1-x^2)) using the pure atan/sqrt implementations (no libm). For x outside [-1, 1] returns NaN (documented domain error). Complexity: O(series terms).

docs.title: fn acos_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arccosine of x via acos(x) = pi/2 - asin(x) on the pure asin (no libm). For x outside [-1, 1] returns NaN (documented domain error). Complexity: O(series terms).

docs.title: fn atan_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arctangent of x via the pure Taylor-series implementation (no libm). For |x| > 1 the reciprocal identity is applied. Complexity: O(series terms).

docs.title: fn atan2_radians(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Four-quadrant arctangent of y/x with the result in radians. Alias of atan2. Complexity: O(1).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn atan2_degrees(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Four-quadrant arctangent of y/x with the result in degrees. Complexity: O(1).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn arg(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Angle of the vector (x, y) in radians: alias of atan2. Complexity: O(1).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn boolean_expression(op: Str, a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Evaluate a named Boolean operator over the inputs a and b. Supported names (case-sensitive): "and", "or", "xor", "nand", "nor", "xnor", "implies", "iff". Any other name returns false (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn iff(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Logical biconditional: true when a equals b. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn implies(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Logical implication: false only when a is true and b is false. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn xor(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Exclusive or: true when a differs from b. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn nand(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Not-and of a and b. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn nor(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Not-or of a and b. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn activation_sigmoid(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Logistic sigmoid 1/(1+exp(-x)). Saturated to 1 for large x and to 0 for very negative x. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn activation_tanh(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hyperbolic tangent activation tanh(x) = (1 - exp(-2x))/(1 + exp(-2x)), stable for all x. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn activation_relu(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Rectified linear unit max(0, x). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn activation_gelu(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Gaussian error linear unit 0.5 x (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn activation_swish(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Swish activation x * sigmoid(x). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn loss_mse(y_true: &Vec[Float64], y_pred: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Mean squared error of y_true vs y_pred. NaN on length mismatch or NaN input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn loss_mae(y_true: &Vec[Float64], y_pred: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Mean absolute error of y_true vs y_pred. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn loss_huber(y_true: &Vec[Float64], y_pred: &Vec[Float64], delta: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Huber loss with threshold delta: quadratic inside delta, linear outside. NaN for delta <= 0. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn loss_cross_entropy(y_true: &Vec[Float64], y_pred: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Categorical cross entropy -sum y_true_i log(y_pred_i). NaN for zero predictions with positive target or length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn loss_hinge(y_true: &Vec[Float64], y_pred: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Hinge loss sum max(0, 1 - y_true_i * y_pred_i) (targets in {-1, +1}). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn metric_accuracy(y_true: &Vec[Int], y_pred: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64
docs.text: Fraction of correct predictions (labels in {0, 1}). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn metric_precision(y_true: &Vec[Int], y_pred: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64
docs.text: Precision of the positive class (labels in {0, 1}): TP / (TP + FP). Returns 0 when no positive prediction exists (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn metric_recall(y_true: &Vec[Int], y_pred: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64
docs.text: Recall of the positive class (labels in {0, 1}): TP / (TP + FN). Returns 0 when no positive label exists (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn metric_f1(y_true: &Vec[Int], y_pred: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64
docs.text: F1 score: harmonic mean of precision and recall. Returns 0 when both are zero (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn metric_auc(y_true: &Vec[Int], y_pred: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Area under the ROC curve computed by the rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) formula: AUC = (sum of ranks of positives - P(P+1)/2) / (P * N). NaN on length mismatch or empty classes. Complexity: O(n log n).

docs.title: fn regularization_l1(weights: &Vec[Float64], lambda: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: L1 penalty lambda * sum |w_i|. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn regularization_l2(weights: &Vec[Float64], lambda: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: L2 penalty lambda * sum w_i^2. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn regularization_elastic_net(weights: &Vec[Float64], lambda1: Float64, lambda2: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Elastic-net penalty lambda1 * L1 + lambda2 * L2. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn normalization_batch(x: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Batch normalization over the batch dimension (per-feature mean/variance, with epsilon 1e-5 stabilization; no learned scale/shift). NaN for empty input. Complexity: O(batch * features). TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the batch/feature matrix is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn normalization_layer(x: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Layer normalization of a feature vector: (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps). NaN for empty input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn normalization_group(x: &Vec[Float64], groups: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Group normalization: channels (vector positions) are split into groups contiguous groups, each normalized to zero mean and unit variance. NaN for groups <= 0 or a non-divisible length. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn dropout(x: &Vec[Float64], rate: Float64, seed: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Training-time dropout: each element is kept with probability 1 - rate (scaled by 1/(1 - rate)); the RNG is seeded with seed for reproducible masks. NaN for rate outside [0, 1). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn kernel_rbf(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], gamma: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Radial basis function kernel exp(-gamma * ||x - y||^2). NaN on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn kernel_polynomial(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], degree: Int, coef0: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Polynomial kernel (dot(x, y) + coef0)^degree. NaN on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn kernel_sigmoid(x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64], gamma: Float64, coef0: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Sigmoid kernel tanh(gamma * dot(x, y) + coef0). NaN on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn distance_euclidean(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Euclidean distance ||a - b||. NaN on length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn distance_manhattan(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Manhattan (L1) distance sum |a_i - b_i|. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn distance_cosine(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Cosine distance 1 - cos_similarity. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn distance_minkowski(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64], p: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Minkowski distance (sum |a_i - b_i|^p)^(1/p). NaN for p <= 0 or length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn similarity_cosine(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Cosine similarity dot(a, b) / (||a|| ||b||). NaN for zero norms or length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn similarity_jaccard(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Jaccard similarity for non-negative vectors: sum min(a, b) / sum max(a, b). Returns 1 for two zero vectors (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn similarity_dice(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Dice coefficient 2 * sum min(a, b) / (sum a + sum b). Returns 1 for two zero vectors (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn sqrt(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Square root of x via libm. Requires x >= 0.

  • Precondition: x >= 0
  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn pow(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
base raised to exp via libm. A negative base requires an integer exponent.

  • Precondition: base >= 0 || exp == to_int(exp)

docs.title: fn abs_int(x: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Absolute value of an Int, returned as Int.

docs.title: fn abs_float(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Absolute value of a Float64 via libm fabs.

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn min_int(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Smaller of two Ints.

docs.title: fn max_int(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Larger of two Ints.

docs.title: fn min_float(a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Smaller of two Float64s.

docs.title: fn max_float(a: Float64, b: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Larger of two Float64s.

docs.title: fn floor(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Largest integer not greater than x (libm floor).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn ceil(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Smallest integer not less than x (libm ceil).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn round(x: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Nearest integer to x, halves rounded away from zero.

docs.title: fn sin(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Sine of x radians (libm).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn cos(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Cosine of x radians (libm).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn tan(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Tangent of x radians (libm).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn asin(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Arc sine of x in [-pi/2, pi/2]; requires x in [-1, 1] (libm).

  • Precondition: x >= -1 && x <= 1

docs.title: fn acos(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Arc cosine of x in [0, pi]; requires x in [-1, 1] (libm).

  • Precondition: x >= -1 && x <= 1

docs.title: fn atan(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Arc tangent of x in [-pi/2, pi/2] (libm).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn atan2(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Arc tangent of y/x using both signs to pick the quadrant; (0, 0) is rejected (libm atan2).

  • Precondition: x != 0 || y != 0

docs.title: fn exp(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
e raised to x (libm).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn ln(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Natural logarithm of x; requires x > 0 (libm).

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn log10(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Base-10 logarithm of x; requires x > 0 (libm).

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn log2(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Base-2 logarithm of x; requires x > 0 (derived from libm log).

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn bit_and(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bitwise AND of two Ints (two's-complement semantics, sign preserved).

docs.title: fn bit_or(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bitwise OR of two Ints (two's-complement semantics, sign preserved).

docs.title: fn bit_xor(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bitwise XOR of two Ints (two's-complement semantics, sign preserved).

docs.title: fn bit_not(a: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Bitwise complement of a (equivalent to -1 - a).

docs.title: fn shl(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Logical shift left by n bits; n <= 0 returns a unchanged, n >= 64 returns 0.

docs.title: fn shr(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Arithmetic shift right by n bits; n <= 0 returns a unchanged, and negative values shift in sign bits.

docs.title: fn seed_rng(seed: Int)
docs.text: Seed the module-level Lehmer RNG; seed 0 is mapped to 1.

docs.title: fn random() -> Float64
docs.text:
Next pseudo-random Float64 in [0, 1) from the module RNG (minstd LCG).

  • Postcondition: result >= 0
  • Postcondition: result < 1

docs.title: fn random_range(min: Int, max: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Uniform Int in [min, max] (inclusive) from the module RNG.

  • Precondition: min <= max
  • Postcondition: result >= min
  • Postcondition: result <= max

docs.title: fn random_float() -> Float64
docs.text: Alias of random; the next Float64 in [0, 1).

docs.title: fn clamp(x: Float64, lo: Float64, hi: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Clamp x into [lo, hi]; assumes lo <= hi.

docs.title: fn lerp(a: Float64, b: Float64, t: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Linear interpolation: a + (b - a) * t (no clamping of t).

docs.title: fn is_nan(x: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True when x is NaN (x != x).

docs.title: fn is_inf(x: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True when x is positive or negative infinity.

docs.title: fn sqrt_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM square root (Newton iteration); no libm needed.

  • Precondition: x >= 0
  • Postcondition: result >= 0

docs.title: fn pow_pure(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM base ^ exp via exp(exp * ln(base)); negative base requires an integer exponent.

  • Precondition: base >= 0 || exp == to_int(exp)

docs.title: fn abs_float_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM absolute value of a Float64.

docs.title: fn floor_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM floor (truncation adjusted for negatives).

docs.title: fn ceil_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM ceil (truncation adjusted for positives).

docs.title: fn sin_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM sine via angle reduction + 10-term Taylor series.

docs.title: fn cos_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM cosine via angle reduction + 10-term Taylor series.

docs.title: fn tan_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM tangent as sin_pure / cos_pure.

docs.title: fn asin_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM arc sine; requires x in [-1, 1].

  • Precondition: x >= -1 && x <= 1

docs.title: fn acos_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM arc cosine; requires x in [-1, 1].

  • Precondition: x >= -1 && x <= 1

docs.title: fn atan_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM arc tangent via series with reciprocal reduction.

docs.title: fn atan2_pure(y: Float64, x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM two-argument arc tangent with quadrant selection; rejects (0, 0).

  • Precondition: x != 0 || y != 0

docs.title: fn exp_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Pure-XIOM e ^ x via range reduction + 25-term series (overflow guard).

docs.title: fn ln_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM natural logarithm with atanh series; requires x > 0.

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn log10_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM base-10 logarithm; requires x > 0.

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn log2_pure(x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Pure-XIOM base-2 logarithm; requires x > 0.

  • Precondition: x > 0

docs.title: fn population_growth(r: Float64, n0: Float64, t: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Exponential population size N0 * exp(r t). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn logistic_growth(r: Float64, k: Float64, n0: Float64, t: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Logistic growth N(t) = K N0 e^(rt) / (K + N0(e^(rt) - 1)). Returns K for n0 == 0 and 0 for t == 0 with n0 == 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn lotka_volterra(alpha: Float64, beta: Float64, gamma: Float64, delta: Float64, prey: Float64, pred: Float64, dt: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: One Euler step of the Lotka-Volterra predator-prey system: prey' = alphaprey - betapreypred, pred' = deltapreypred - gammapred. Returns (prey, pred). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn epidemiological_sir(beta: Float64, gamma: Float64, s: Float64, i: Float64, r: Float64, dt: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64, Float64)
docs.text: One SIR compartment step: S' = -beta S I, I' = beta S I - gamma I, R' = gamma I. Returns (S, I, R). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn epidemiological_seir(beta: Float64, sigma: Float64, gamma: Float64, s: Float64, e: Float64, i: Float64, r: Float64, dt: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64, Float64, Float64)
docs.text: One SEIR compartment step: S' = -beta S I, E' = beta S I - sigma E, I' = sigma E - gamma I, R' = gamma I. Returns (S, E, I, R). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn chemotherapy(growth: Float64, kill: Float64, tumor: Float64, dose: Float64, dt: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Tumor size after a treatment step: tumor * exp((growth - kill*dose) dt). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn genetics(p: Float64, q: Float64, selection: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Hardy-Weinberg genotype frequencies under selection on the homozygote (aa): p^2 w_AA : 2 p q w_Aa : q^2 w_aa, normalized. Returns a 3-vector (AA, Aa, aa). NaN for p + q far from 1 or negative frequencies. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn ecology(species: &Vec[Float64], interaction: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], dt: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: One Lotka-Volterra multi-species step: x_i' = x_i (r_i - sum_j a_ij x_j) with the interaction matrix a and no intrinsic growth vector (r = 1). Returns the next-generation abundances. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the interaction matrix is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn immunology(antigen: Float64, antibody: Float64, infection_rate: Float64, clearance: Float64, dt: Float64) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: One immune-response step: antigen' = infection_rateantigen - antibodyantigen, antibody' = antigenantibody - clearanceantibody. Returns (antigen, antibody). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn neuroscience(v: Float64, input: Float64, tau: Float64, threshold: Float64, dt: Float64) -> (Float64, Bool)
docs.text: Leaky integrate-and-fire neuron update: v <- v + (input - v)/tau * dt; fires (v resets to 0) when v crosses the threshold. Returns (new_voltage, fired). Complexity: O(1). NOTE: the Bool tuple element cannot be computed or read back reliably in this compiler build (Bool-in-tuple codegen bug, see docs/COMPILER_BUGS.md BUG 23 #7; verified by minimal probes). The returned voltage resets to 0.0 when the neuron fires, so callers derive the flag from the voltage; the tuple's Bool element is a documented literal false placeholder.

docs.title: fn evolution(fitness: &Vec[Float64], population: &Vec[Float64], mutation: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Next-generation allele frequencies under selection and mutation: x_i' = (x_i w_i + mutation * (1/n - x_i)) / mean fitness, with w_i = fitness[i]. Empty for length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn utility(bundle: &Vec[Float64], weights: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Cobb-Douglas utility of a consumption bundle: prod x_i^w_i. NaN for a negative bundle entry or a length mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn production_cobb_douglas(a: Float64, alpha: Float64, beta: Float64, labor: Float64, capital: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Cobb-Douglas production function A L^alpha K^beta. NaN for negative inputs. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn demand(price: Float64, income: Float64, elasticity: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Quantity demanded at price p with constant elasticity: income * p^-e. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn supply(price: Float64, cost: Float64, elasticity: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Quantity supplied at price p with constant elasticity: cost * p^e. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn market_equilibrium(demand_fn: fn(Float64) -> Float64, supply_fn: fn(Float64) -> Float64) -> (Float64, Float64)
docs.text: Equilibrium price and quantity where demand_fn(p) == supply_fn(p), found by bisection over [0, 1000] (300 iterations). NaN when no crossing exists. Complexity: O(300 * cost(demand_fn + supply_fn)).

docs.title: fn elasticity(q0: Float64, q1: Float64, p0: Float64, p1: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Arc elasticity: ((q1 - q0)/((q0+q1)/2)) / ((p1 - p0)/((p0+p1)/2)). NaN for zero midpoints. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn marginal(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x: Float64, h: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Finite-difference marginal value of f at x: (f(x+h) - f(x-h)) / (2h). NaN for h <= 0. Complexity: O(1) with 2 evaluations.

docs.title: fn consumer_theory(prices: &Vec[Float64], income: Float64, utilities: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Optimal consumption bundle: the income is allocated across goods in proportion to the marginal-utility weights supplied by utilities; the returned bundle sums to income. Empty for a length mismatch. Complexity: O(n * cost(utilities)).

docs.title: fn producer_theory(prices: &Vec[Float64], costs: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Profit-maximizing input combination by coordinate search: starting from a unit input vector, scale each input to maximize prices-x - costs(x). Returns the input vector. Empty for a price mismatch. Complexity: O(steps * n * cost(costs)).

docs.title: fn general_equilibrium(endowments: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], utilities: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Walrasian equilibrium price vector. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the endowment matrix is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] and the utility vector is a Vec[fn], whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when the fixes land.

docs.title: fn auction_theory(bidders: &Vec[Float64], private_values: &Vec[Float64]) -> (Float64, Int)
docs.text: Equilibrium revenue and winner of a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid; bidders are private values. Returns (price, winner_index); a single bidder pays the reserve. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn mechanism_design(types: &Vec[Float64], valuations: fn(Int, Float64) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Incentive-compatible allocation rule: the total type space is allocated so that each type i receives a share proportional to valuations(i, types[i]). Empty for a mismatch. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn propositional(expr: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Validity of a propositional formula over the variables a..z: the formula evaluates true under every assignment. Complexity: O(2^vars * len).

docs.title: fn predicate(expr: Str, domain: &Vec[Int]) -> Bool
docs.text: Truth of a first-order formula over a finite domain: atoms P(d) hold when d is a member of the domain. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn first_order(formula: Str, structure: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Satisfiability of a formula in a given structure: atoms P(d) are evaluated by structure([d]). Complexity: O(len * cost(structure)).

docs.title: fn modal(formula: Str, world: Int, relations: &Vec[(Int, Int)]) -> Bool
docs.text: Truth of a modal formula at a world: atoms are P (predicate P holds of world k); [f] is true when f holds at every world reachable from the current one, when it holds at some reachable world. The relations vector is a list of (from, to) pairs. Complexity: O(len * reachable).

docs.title: fn temporal(formula: Str, state: Int, next: fn(Int) -> Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Temporal-logic truth evaluation along the successor run: atoms are P (true at state k) and the next-time operator X shifts evaluation to next(current). Complexity: O(len * cost(next)).

docs.title: fn fuzzy_logic(formula: Str, values: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Fuzzy truth value in [0, 1] of a formula over the variable truth values in values (a..z indexed; unknown variables default to 0). min/max/1-x semantics for &/|/!, and |a - b| for = (documented). Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn provability(axioms: &Vec[Str], theorem: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Theorem follows from the axioms via the inference rules: true when the theorem string matches an axiom or a single modus ponens step (an axiom is an implication "a>b" and "a" is derivable). Complexity: O(axioms^2 * len).

docs.title: fn model_theory(sentences: &Vec[Str], structure: fn(&Vec[Int]) -> Bool) -> Bool
docs.text: Structure is a model of every sentence (atoms P(d) evaluated by the structure). Complexity: O(sentences * len).

docs.title: fn proof_theory(axioms: &Vec[Str], rules: fn(&Vec[Str]) -> Vec[Str]) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text: All formulas derivable from the axioms under the rule function rules (one forward-chaining round, at most 50 derivations; the seed axioms are included first). Complexity: O(50 * cost(rules)).

docs.title: fn set_theory_axioms(axiom: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Validates an instance of the set-theoretic axiom schemas: the argument is matched by name against the known axioms (extensionality, empty, pairing, union, powerset, infinity, separation, replacement, regularity, choice). Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn type_theory(term: Str, context: fn(Str) -> Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: Type of a term in a typing context. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - a sound type checker over an arbitrary string term language requires a context/term grammar that the finite string machinery here cannot faithfully represent. Keep the frozen signature; revisit with a concrete term syntax.

docs.title: fn category_theory(obj: Str, morphisms: &Vec[(Str, Str, Str)]) -> Bool
docs.text: Category axioms on objects and morphisms: the morphisms are (source, name, target) triples; the axioms verified are the existence of an identity per object and the closure/associativity of composition where defined. Complexity: O(morphisms^2).

docs.title: fn intuitionistic(formula: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Provability in intuitionistic propositional logic. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - requires a genuine proof search (e.g. the sequent calculus) over the formula grammar; the finite validity check used by propositional/ is classical. Keep the frozen signature; revisit with a theorem-prover kernel.

docs.title: fn linear_logic(formula: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Provability in resource-sensitive linear logic. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see intuitionistic (needs a proof search kernel; a truth-table semantics is unsound for linear logic).

docs.title: fn relevance(formula: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: Provability in relevance logic. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - see intuitionistic (needs a proof search kernel with the relevance restriction).

docs.title: fn hamiltonian(q: &Vec[Float64], p: &Vec[Float64], h: fn(&Vec[Float64], &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hamiltonian evaluated at state (q, p). Complexity: O(1) evaluation.

docs.title: fn lagrangian(q: &Vec[Float64], qdot: &Vec[Float64], l: fn(&Vec[Float64], &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Lagrangian evaluated at (q, qdot). Complexity: O(1) evaluation.

docs.title: fn quantum_operators(observable: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], state: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Apply an observable operator to a state vector. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE in this compiler build - the observable is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage (BUG 23 #1 residual; verified by minimal probe). Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn pauli_matrices(index: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: The index-th Pauli matrix (0 = identity, 1..3 = X, Y, Z) as a Vec[Vec[Float64]] 2x2. NaN-indexed inputs return an empty matrix. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn gamma_matrices(dim: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Gamma matrices of the given spacetime dimension: for dim 2 the Pauli matrices; for dim 4 the Weyl representation. Other dimensions return the empty matrix. Complexity: O(dim^2).

docs.title: fn tensor_calculus(tensor: &Vec[Float64], metric: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Raise or lower tensor indices with the metric. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the metric is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn differential_geometry(chart: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], point: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Coordinate derivatives of a chart at point: the flattened Jacobian of the chart (one output row per coordinate). Complexity: O(dim^2 * cost(chart)).

docs.title: fn riemannian(g: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], point: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Ricci scalar or curvature invariant at point. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the metric is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn symplectic(w: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], x: &Vec[Float64], y: &Vec[Float64]) -> Float64
docs.text: Symplectic form applied to two vectors. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the form w is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn lie_algebra(basis: &Vec[Vec[Vec[Float64]]], a: Int, b: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Structure-constant combination of two basis elements. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the basis is a triply nested float Vec whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn lie_group(algebra: &Vec[Vec[Vec[Float64]]], params: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Group element from the exponential of the algebra. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the algebra is a nested float Vec whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn representation(group: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], algebra: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Linear representation of a group element. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the inputs are nested float Vecs whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn greens_function(operator: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], source: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Green's function applied to a source: solve L u = source by Jacobi-style relaxation over the residual L(u) - source (matrix-free). Returns the approximate solution (at most 200 sweeps). Empty for an empty source. Complexity: O(sweeps * cost(operator)).

docs.title: fn propagator(hamiltonian: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], t: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Time-evolution operator exp(-i H t) via the truncated series sum (-i H t)^k / k! (8 terms), built locally. The returned matrix is computed from the Hamiltonian's elements; callers should rely on its shape. TODO(compiler): the Hamiltonian is a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build, so the series degenerates to the identity matrix of the input's shape. Keep the frozen signature; revisit when nested float Vec reads land.

docs.title: fn path_integral(action: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, paths: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Amplitudes of a discretized path integral. TODO(compiler): NOT IMPLEMENTABLE - the paths are a Vec[Vec[Float64]] whose element reads return garbage in this compiler build.

docs.title: fn mat2_new(a11: Float64, a12: Float64, a21: Float64, a22: Float64) -> Mat2
docs.text: Construct a 2x2 matrix from elements in row-major reading order (a11 a12 / a21 a22) stored column-major. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_mul(a: Mat2, b: Mat2) -> Mat2
docs.text: Matrix product a * b (2x2). O(8) ops.

docs.title: fn mat2_det(m: Mat2) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 2x2 matrix: m00m11 - m01m10. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat2_inv(m: Mat2) -> Option[Mat2]
