docs.title: fn mat3_new(a11: Float64, a12: Float64, a13: Float64, a21: Float64, a22: Float64, a23: Float64, a31: Float64, a32: Float64, a33: Float64) -> Mat3
docs.text: Construct a 3x3 matrix from elements in row-major reading order (three rows) stored column-major. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat3_mul(a: Mat3, b: Mat3) -> Mat3
docs.text: Matrix product a * b (3x3). O(27) ops.

docs.title: fn mat3_det(m: Mat3) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 3x3 matrix by cofactor expansion. O(9) ops.

docs.title: fn mat3_inv(m: Mat3) -> Option[Mat3]
docs.text: Inverse of a 3x3 matrix via the adjugate formula. Returns None when the determinant is near zero (|det| < 1e-12, documented singularity cutoff). O(27) ops.

docs.title: fn mat3_transpose(m: Mat3) -> Mat3
docs.text: Transpose of a 3x3 matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_new(a11: Float64, a12: Float64, a13: Float64, a14: Float64, a21: Float64, a22: Float64, a23: Float64, a24: Float64, a31: Float64, a32: Float64, a33: Float64, a34: Float64, a41: Float64, a42: Float64, a43: Float64, a44: Float64) -> Mat4
docs.text: Construct a 4x4 matrix from elements in row-major reading order (four rows) stored column-major. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat4_mul(a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4
docs.text: Matrix product a * b (4x4). O(64) ops.

docs.title: fn mat4_det(m: Mat4) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a 4x4 matrix by cofactor expansion along the first row (3x3 sub-determinants of the lower rows). O(48) ops.

docs.title: fn mat4_inv(m: Mat4) -> Option[Mat4]
docs.text: Inverse of a 4x4 matrix via the adjugate (cofactor-transpose / det). Returns None when |det| < 1e-12 (documented singularity cutoff). O(150).

docs.title: fn mat4_transpose(m: Mat4) -> Mat4
docs.text: Transpose of a 4x4 matrix. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_identity(n: Int) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: n x n identity matrix. Returns an empty matrix for n <= 0 (documented). O(n^2).

docs.title: fn mat_mul(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Dynamic matrix product a * b. Returns an empty matrix when the inner dimensions disagree (a.cols != b.rows), or when either input is empty (documented; no silent garbage). O(rows * cols * inner).

docs.title: fn mat_det(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Float64
docs.text: Determinant of a dynamic square matrix via Laplace cofactor expansion. Returns NaN (0.0/0.0) for non-square or empty input (documented). O(n!).

docs.title: fn mat_inv(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]]) -> Option[Vec[Vec[Float64]]]
docs.text: Inverse of a dynamic square matrix via Gauss-Jordan elimination. Returns None for non-square, empty, or (numerically) singular input (documented; pivot tolerance 1e-12). O(n^3).

docs.title: fn mat_translate(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: m * T where T is the 4x4 translation matrix by (x, y, z). When m is not 4x4 the input is returned unchanged (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_rotate(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], angle: Float64, axis: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: m * R where R is the 4x4 rotation by angle radians about axis (axis is normalised internally). A zero axis returns m unchanged (documented); a non-4x4 m is returned unchanged. O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_scale(m: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], x: Float64, y: Float64, z: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: m * S where S is the 4x4 scale matrix by (x, y, z). A non-4x4 m is returned unchanged (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_look_at(eye: &Vec[Float64], target: &Vec[Float64], up: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Right-handed look-at view matrix: camera at eye looking at target with up vector. eye/target/up are length-3 dynamic vectors; vectors of any other length return an empty matrix (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_perspective(fovy: Float64, aspect: Float64, near: Float64, far: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Perspective projection matrix (right-handed, standard OpenGL mapping to NDC [-1, 1]^3). Returns an empty matrix for fovy <= 0, aspect <= 0, or near == far (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn mat_ortho(left: Float64, right: Float64, bottom: Float64, top: Float64, near: Float64, far: Float64) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]]
docs.text: Orthographic projection matrix mapping [l, r] x [b, t] x [n, f] to NDC [-1, 1]^3. Returns an empty matrix when any two facing planes coincide (documented). O(1).

docs.title: fn mod_add(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: (a + b) mod m with the result in [0, m). Returns 0 for m <= 0 (no modulus, documented) and 0 for m == 1 (everything is 0 mod 1). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mod_sub(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: (a - b) mod m with the result in [0, m). Returns 0 for m <= 0 (no modulus, documented) and 0 for m == 1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn mod_mul(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: (a * b) mod m with the result in [0, m). Uses overflow-free double-and-add. Returns 0 for m <= 0 (no modulus, documented) and 0 for m == 1. Complexity: O(log min(a, b)).

docs.title: fn mod_pow(base: Int, exp: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: base^exp mod m with the result in [0, m). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.pow_mod. Returns 0 for m <= 0, m == 1, and exp < 0 (documented; only non-negative exponents are supported). Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn mod_inverse(a: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Multiplicative inverse of a mod m: x with (a*x) % m == 1. Returns 0 when no inverse exists (gcd(a, m) != 1), when m == 0 (no modulus) and for m == 1 (documented). Delegates to xiom.math.arithmetic.mod_inverse. Complexity: O(log min(|a|, |m|)).

docs.title: fn mod_sqrt(a: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: A square root of a mod prime p (x with x^2 == a mod p), choosing the root in [0, (p-1)/2]. Returns 0 when no root exists, when p <= 1 (no modulus) and when p is composite (documented: p must be prime). Delegates to tonelli_shanks. Complexity: O(log^3 p).

docs.title: fn mod_cbrt(a: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: A cube root of a mod m: x with x^3 == a mod m. For prime m with gcd(3, m-1) == 1 the root is a^((2m-1)/3) mod m; for m == 1 (mod 3) a small scan is used. Returns 0 when no root exists, for m <= 0 (no modulus) and when m == 1. Complexity: O(log m) for the closed form, O(m) scan otherwise.

docs.title: fn mod_div(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: (a / b) mod m: a * b^(-1) mod m. Returns 0 when b has no inverse mod m (gcd(b, m) != 1), when m <= 0 (no modulus) and for m == 1 (documented). Complexity: O(log min(|b|, |m|)).

docs.title: fn mod_lcm(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Least common multiple of a and b reduced mod m. Returns 0 when m <= 0 (no modulus), for m == 1 and when either input is 0. Uses the overflow-free modular multiply so the true lcm may exceed Int range. Complexity: O(log).

docs.title: fn crt(remainders: &Vec[Int], moduli: &Vec[Int]) -> Int
docs.text: Chinese remainder theorem solution x with x % m_i == r_i for every pair. Returns 0 when the slices differ in length, when either slice is empty, when any modulus is non-positive, when the moduli are not pairwise coprime, and when the product of the moduli overflows Int (documented). The result lies in [0, M) with M = prod(m_i). Complexity: O(n^2 * log max(m_i)).

docs.title: fn crt_solve(congruences: &Vec[(Int, Int)]) -> Int
docs.text: Solve a system of congruences given as (remainder, modulus) pairs using the iterative merging method. Returns 0 when the list is empty, when any modulus is non-positive, when the system is inconsistent, and on overflow (documented). Complexity: O(n * log max(m_i)).

docs.title: fn linear_congruence(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Solve a*x == b (mod m): returns the least non-negative solution. Returns 0 when m <= 0 (no modulus), when m == 1, when gcd(a, m) does not divide b (no solution) and on overflow (documented). Complexity: O(log min(|a|, |m|)).

docs.title: fn quadratic_residue(a: Int, p: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff a is a quadratic residue mod prime p, i.e. x^2 == a (mod p) has a solution. a == 0 (mod p) counts as a residue (x = 0). Returns false for p <= 1 (no modulus). Uses Euler's criterion. Complexity: O(log p).

docs.title: fn tonelli_shanks(n: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Square root of n mod odd prime p via the Tonelli-Shanks algorithm, choosing the root in [0, (p-1)/2]. Returns 0 when n is a non-residue mod p, for p <= 2 (p == 2 is handled directly) and when p is composite (documented: p must be prime). Complexity: O(log^3 p).

docs.title: fn cipolla(n: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Square root of n mod odd prime p via Cipolla's algorithm, choosing the root in [0, (p-1)/2]. Returns 0 when n is a non-residue mod p, for p <= 2 (p == 2 is handled directly) and when p is composite (documented: p must be prime). Complexity: O(log^2 p).

docs.title: fn cornacchia(d: Int, b: Int, m: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Cornacchia's algorithm: find integers x, y >= 0 with x^2 + d*y^2 = m. The parameter b is a square root of -d modulo m (the caller must supply one; for prime m this is sqrt(-d) mod m, e.g. via tonelli_shanks). Returns (0, 0) when d <= 0, when no representation exists, and on overflow (documented). Complexity: O(log^2 m).

docs.title: fn hilbert_symbol(a: Int, b: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Local Hilbert symbol (a, b)_p over Q_p, returning 1 or -1. Uses the standard factorization: for odd p, (a,b)_p = (-1)^(alpha*beta) * (u/p)^beta * (v/p)^alpha with a = p^alpha * u, b = p^beta * v; for p == 2 the explicit epsilon/omega formula is used. Returns 0 when a or b is 0 (the symbol is degenerate there, documented). Complexity: O(log_p |a| + log_p |b| + log p).

docs.title: fn pow_mod_fast(base: Int, exp: Int, m: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Fast modular exponentiation base^exp mod m. Alias of xiom.math.arithmetic.pow_mod; returns 0 for m <= 0, m == 1 and exp < 0 (documented). Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn binary_to_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Binary string to Int. Err("invalid") for empty, non-'0'/'1', or overflow input. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn int_to_binary(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal Int to a binary string. n == 0 yields "0"; negatives get a '-' prefix. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn octal_to_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Octal string to Int. Err on invalid input. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn int_to_octal(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal Int to an octal string. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn hex_to_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Hexadecimal string to Int. Err on invalid input. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn int_to_hex(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal Int to a hexadecimal string (upper-case digits). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn base_n_to_int(s: Str, base: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Parse a string in an arbitrary base (2..36) to Int. Err on invalid input, an out-of-range base, or overflow. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn int_to_base_n(n: Int, base: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal Int to a string in an arbitrary base (2..36). Returns "" for an out-of-range base. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn roman_to_int(s: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
docs.text: Roman numeral string to Int. Err for empty or invalid input; subtractive notation (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM) is supported. Complexity: O(len).

docs.title: fn int_to_roman(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Int to a Roman numeral string (1..3999); "" outside that range. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn chinese_numerals(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Int to a Chinese numeral string (supports 0..99999999; larger values return the 亿-form with the remainder documented). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn japanese_numerals(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Int to a Japanese numeral string (〇一...九 + 十百千万; 0..99999999). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn egyptian_fractions(numer: Int, denom: Int) -> Vec[(Int, Int)]
docs.text: Greedy Egyptian fraction expansion of numer/denom as (1, unit) pairs. Empty for a non-positive numerator or denominator. Complexity: O(denom).

docs.title: fn babylonian_numerals(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Babylonian-style base-60 notation: the sexagesimal places of n joined by ';' (a documented approximation of cuneiform numerals). n == 0 yields "0". Complexity: O(log_60 n).

docs.title: fn greek_numerals(n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Int to a Greek alphabetic numeral string (1..999 using the standard archaic digits; "" outside the range). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn continued_fraction(x: Float64, terms: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Continued-fraction coefficients of x (at most terms of them). Complexity: O(terms).

docs.title: fn fraction_new(numer: Int, denom: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Reduced fraction (numer / gcd, denom / gcd) with the sign on the numerator. Returns (0, 1) for denom == 0. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn fraction_add(a: (Int, Int), b: (Int, Int)) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Sum of two reduced fractions (reduced again). Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn surd_simplify(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: Simplify sqrt(a)/sqrt(b) to (coefficient, radicand): the largest square factor of ab is pulled out of the radical. Returns (1, 1) for b == 0. Complexity: O(sqrt(ab)).

docs.title: fn octonion_add(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Componentwise sum of two octonions (8 components). Empty for a length mismatch. Complexity: O(8).

docs.title: fn sedenion_add(a: &Vec[Float64], b: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Componentwise sum of two sedenions (16 components). Empty for a length mismatch. Complexity: O(16).

docs.title: fn is_prime(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Deterministic primality test for 64-bit n (Miller-Rabin over the fixed base set {2, 325, 9375, 28178, 450775, 9780504, 1795265022}, which is proven for every n < 2^64). Returns false for n < 2. Complexity: O(log^3 n).

docs.title: fn is_prime_deterministic(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Strict deterministic primality test: Miller-Rabin with the fixed base set proven correct for all 64-bit integers. Returns false for n < 2. Complexity: O(log^3 n).

docs.title: fn next_prime(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Smallest prime strictly greater than n. Returns 0 for n < 0 (no positive prime is representable in range for the largest inputs) and 0 when no such prime fits in Int (n >= INT_MAX - 1). Complexity: O(gap * sqrt(p)).

docs.title: fn prev_prime(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Largest prime strictly less than n. Returns 0 for n <= 2 (no such prime) and 0 (documented) when the search leaves the representable range. Complexity: O(gap * sqrt(p)).

docs.title: fn factor(n: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Prime factorization of n with multiplicity. Returns the empty list for n <= 1; negative n is factored by absolute value. Complexity: O(sqrt(|n|)).

docs.title: fn pollard_rho(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: A non-trivial factor of n via Pollard's rho (Floyd cycle detection with f(x) = x^2 + c mod n). Returns n itself when n is prime or when no split is found within the retry budget (documented; a repeated call with a different internal constant is the standard recovery). Returns 1 for n <= 1. Complexity: O(sqrt(p)) expected for the smallest prime factor p.

docs.title: fn p_1_factor(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: A non-trivial factor of n via Pollard's p-1 method (a = 2^B! mod n for an increasing stage bound B). Returns n itself when n is prime or when no factor is found within the stage bound (documented). Returns 1 for n <= 1. Complexity: O(B * log B * mulmod).

docs.title: fn is_pseudoprime(n: Int, base: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n passes the Fermat test for base a, i.e. a^(n-1) == 1 (mod n). Returns false for n <= 1, true for n == 2, and false when a is a multiple of n (the residue is 0, not 1). Primes always pass; composite pseudoprimes to base a also return true. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn miller_rabin(n: Int, bases: &Vec[Int]) -> Bool
docs.text: Miller-Rabin strong pseudoprime test against the supplied bases. Returns false for n <= 1, even n (n > 2) and for any base witnessing compositeness; a value that passes every base is reported true (likely prime, exactly prime for n < 2^64 when the base set is the deterministic one). Complexity: O(|bases| * log^3 n).

docs.title: fn fermat_test(n: Int, a: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Fermat compositeness test with base a: true iff a^(n-1) == 1 (mod n). Alias of is_pseudoprime. Complexity: O(log n).

docs.title: fn lucas_lehmer(p: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: Lucas-Lehmer primality test for the Mersenne number M_p = 2^p - 1. Returns false for p < 2 and when M_p does not fit in Int (p > 62). Complexity: O(p * mulmod).

docs.title: fn mersenne_prime_p(p: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff 2^p - 1 is prime. Alias of lucas_lehmer. Returns false for p < 2 and when M_p exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(p * mulmod).

docs.title: fn euler_phi(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Euler totient phi(n): count of integers k in [1, n] coprime to n. Returns 0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn mobius(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Mobius function mu(n): 0 if n has a squared prime factor, otherwise (-1)^k with k the number of distinct prime factors. Returns 0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn jordan_totient(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Jordan totient J_k(n): count of k-tuples (x_1..x_k) in [1, n]^k that are jointly coprime to n. Returns 0 for n <= 0, 1 for n == 1, 0 for k < 0 (documented) and 0 for k == 0 with n > 1 (J_0(n) = 0). Returns 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(sqrt(n) * log k).

docs.title: fn carmichael(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Carmichael lambda function: the smallest m with a^m == 1 (mod n) for every a coprime to n. Computed as the lcm of lambda(p^a) over the prime powers dividing n: lambda(2) = 1, lambda(4) = 2, lambda(2^a) = 2^(a-2) for a >= 3, lambda(p^a) = p^(a-1)(p-1) for odd p. Returns 0 for n <= 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(sqrt(n) * lcm).

docs.title: fn prime_pi(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: pi(n): the number of primes <= n. Returns 0 for n < 2. Uses a simple sieve of Eratosthenes over [0, n]. Complexity: O(n log log n).

docs.title: fn nth_prime(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: The n-th prime, 1-indexed (nth_prime(1) == 2). Returns 0 for n <= 0 and 0 (documented) when the search leaves the representable Int range. Complexity: O(n * sqrt(p_n)).

docs.title: fn primorial(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Product of the first n primes (p_n#). Returns 0 for n <= 0 and 0 (documented overflow) when the product exceeds Int range (n > 15). Complexity: O(n * sqrt(p_n)).

docs.title: fn is_composite(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is composite (n > 1 and not prime). Returns false for n <= 1. Complexity: O(log^3 n) via the Miller-Rabin primality test.

docs.title: fn is_semiprime(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a product of exactly two primes (with multiplicity), so squares of primes count. Returns false for n < 4. Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn is_power(n: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a perfect power a^k for integers a and k >= 2. Returns false for n <= 1. Uses the prime-exponent gcd criterion: n is a perfect power iff the gcd of the exponents in its prime factorization exceeds 1. Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn is_power_of(n: Int, base: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff n is a power of base: n == base^k for some integer k >= 1. Special cases: base 0 (only n == 0), base 1 (only n == 1), base -1 (n == 1 or n == -1). Returns false when the power series overflows Int before reaching n. Complexity: O(log_base |n|).

docs.title: fn radical(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Radical of n: the product of the distinct prime factors of n. Returns n for n <= 1 (rad(1) = 1, rad(0) = 0) and 0 (documented overflow) when the product exceeds Int range. Negative n is handled by absolute value. Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn smooth(n: Int, bound: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff every prime factor of n is <= bound. Returns true for n <= 1 (no prime factors) and false for bound <= 1. Negative n is handled by absolute value. Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn rough(n: Int, bound: Int) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff every prime factor of n is > bound. Returns true for n <= 1 (no prime factors). Negative n is handled by absolute value. Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn legendre_symbol(a: Int, p: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Legendre symbol (a/p) for odd prime p: 1 for a quadratic residue, -1 for a non-residue, 0 when p divides a. Uses Euler's criterion a^((p-1)/2) mod p. p == 2 is handled directly (1 for odd a, 0 for even a); p <= 1 returns 0 (documented, no modulus). Complexity: O(log p).

docs.title: fn jacobi_symbol(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Jacobi symbol (a/n) for odd positive n; generalizes the Legendre symbol to composite odd n. Returns 0 for even or non-positive n (documented; the Jacobi symbol is undefined there) and 0 when gcd(a, n) != 1. Uses the quadratic-reciprocity reduction over the binary expansion of a. Complexity: O(log^2 n) worst case.

docs.title: fn kronecker_symbol(a: Int, n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Kronecker symbol (a/n), the full extension of the Jacobi symbol to all integer n. Returns 1 for n == 1, (a/-1) by the sign of a, and uses the 2-adic rules for even n. n == 0 gives 1 iff a == 1 or a == -1, else 0. Complexity: O(log^2 |n|).

docs.title: fn divisor_sum(n: Int, k: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Sum of the k-th powers of the positive divisors of n, sigma_k(n). Returns 0 for n <= 0 and 0 for k < 0 (documented). Computed from the prime factorization: sigma_k(n) = prod (p^(k(e+1)) - 1)/(p^k - 1); k == 0 is the divisor count. Returns 0 (documented overflow) when the value exceeds Int range. Complexity: O(sqrt(n) * log k).

docs.title: fn divisor_count(n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Number of positive divisors of n. Returns 0 for n <= 0. Alias of divisor_sum(n, 0). Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn proper_divisors(n: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: All positive divisors of n excluding n itself (unsorted). Returns the empty list for n <= 1 (1 has no proper divisors). Complexity: O(sqrt(n)).

docs.title: fn bisection(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f in [a, b] via bisection on a sign change. When f(a) and f(b) share a sign the interval is sampled (64 points) for a sub-bracket; if none is found NaN (0.0/0.0) is returned (documented). Convergence to interval width tol, at most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(log((b-a)/tol)).

docs.title: fn newton(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, fprime: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x0: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f via Newton's method from x0: x <- x - f(x)/f'(x). Returns x0 when the derivative vanishes (documented), at most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f + f')).

docs.title: fn secant(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x0: Float64, x1: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f via the secant method from x0, x1. Returns x1 when f(x1) == f(x0) (documented, division by zero guard), at most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn falsi(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f in [a, b] via regula falsi (false position) with the Illinois anti-stalling adjustment. Returns NaN when no sign change exists in [a, b] (documented), at most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn brent(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f in [a, b] via Brent's method (inverse quadratic interpolation with bisection fallback). The most robust of the bracketing methods; returns NaN when no sign change exists in [a, b] (documented). At most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn fixed_point(g: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x0: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Fixed point of g by iteration x <- g(x) from x0. Convergence when |g(x) - x| < tol; at most 1000 iterations. Complexity: O(1000 * cost(g)).

docs.title: fn steffensen(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x0: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Root of f via Steffensen's accelerated iteration, which achieves quadratic convergence without derivatives: x <- x - f(x)^2 / (f(x + f(x)) - f(x)). Returns x when the denominator vanishes (documented), at most 200 iterations. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn newton_multi(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], jac: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Root of the nonlinear system fs(x) = 0 via Newton's method with the Jacobian supplied by jac. Solves J * d = -f by Gaussian elimination each iteration; converges to norm(d) < tol (at most 100 iterations). Returns the last iterate. Complexity: O(iters * n^3).

docs.title: fn newton_raphson_multi(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], jac: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Multi-variable Newton-Raphson root of the system fs(x) = 0. Alias of newton_multi. Complexity: O(iters * n^3).

docs.title: fn gauss_seidel(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Solve Ax = b by Gauss-Seidel iteration from x0. Requires a non-zero diagonal; returns the last iterate (at most 1000 iterations, convergence on the sup-norm of the increment). The empty vector is returned for empty input. Complexity: O(iters * n^2).

docs.title: fn jacobi_iterative(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Solve Ax = b by Jacobi iteration from x0 (updates use the previous iterate). Requires a non-zero diagonal; returns the last iterate. Complexity: O(iters * n^2).

docs.title: fn conjugate_gradient(a: &Vec[Vec[Float64]], b: &Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Solve SPD Ax = b by the conjugate gradient method from x0. Requires a symmetric positive-definite system; returns the last iterate (at most n + 200 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n^2).

docs.title: fn gradient_descent(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], lr: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f(x) by gradient descent with learning rate lr from x0. Returns the last iterate (at most 10000 steps, stop when |lr * grad| < tol). Complexity: O(steps * cost(grad)).

docs.title: fn broyden(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Solve the nonlinear system fs(x) = 0 by Broyden's quasi-Newton method (secant update of the inverse-Jacobian estimate, no derivatives needed). Returns the last iterate (at most 100 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n^2).

docs.title: fn anderson(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], m: Int, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Anderson-accelerated fixed-point iteration for the system fs(x) = 0 (fixed-point map x - fs(x)), keeping a history of the last m residuals. Returns the last iterate (at most 1000 outer iterations). Complexity: O(iters * m * n).

docs.title: fn solver_system(fs: &Vec[fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: General nonlinear system solver from x0. Broyden requires no Jacobian, so it is the natural default; delegates to broyden. Complexity: O(iters*n^2).

docs.title: fn interp_linear(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Piecewise linear interpolation of the points (xs, ys) at x. x outside [xs[0], xs[n-1]] is clamped to the nearest endpoint (documented). Returns NaN for empty or mismatched input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn interp_polynomial(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Polynomial interpolation through the points (xs, ys) evaluated at x (Lagrange form). Returns NaN for empty, mismatched, or repeated-x input (division by zero guard). Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn interp_spline(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Default spline interpolation at x: a natural cubic spline through the points (xs, ys). Same semantics as interp_cubic. Returns NaN for empty, mismatched, or fewer-than-2-points input. Complexity: O(n) per call after an O(n) setup.

docs.title: fn interp_cubic(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Natural cubic spline interpolation at x through the points (xs, ys) (zero second derivatives at the ends). Returns NaN for empty, mismatched, or fewer-than-2-points input. Complexity: O(n) setup + O(n) evaluation.

docs.title: fn interp_hermite(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], dys: &Vec[Float64], x: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Hermite cubic interpolation at x using derivative values dys. Returns NaN for empty, mismatched input, or fewer than 2 points. x outside the data range is clamped to the nearest endpoint (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn spline_linear(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Build linear spline coefficients: for n points the returned vector holds 2 * (n - 1) values, one (slope, intercept) pair per segment (documented layout). Returns the empty vector for fewer than 2 points or mismatched input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn spline_cubic(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Build natural cubic spline coefficients: for n points the returned vector holds 4 * (n - 1) values, one (a, b, c, d) tuple per segment with p(x) = a + b(x - x_i) + c(x - x_i)^2 + d*(x - x_i)^3 (documented layout). Returns the empty vector for fewer than 2 points or mismatched input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn spline_b_spline(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Build B-spline control points of degree degree interpolating the data points ys (uniform knots). For degree 3 the interior control points come from the standard tridiagonal system c_(i-1) + 4 c_i + c_(i+1) = 6 y_i; for degree 1 the data points are returned as control points; other degrees fall back to the degree-3 fit (documented). Returns the empty vector for fewer than 2 points. Complexity: O(n) Thomas solve.

docs.title: fn spline_nurbs(xs: &Vec[Float64], ys: &Vec[Float64], weights: &Vec[Float64], degree: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Build NURBS control points from ys with the per-point weights: returns the homogeneous (weighted) control points w_i * y_i, one per data point (documented layout; an evaluator divides through by the weights). Returns the empty vector when weights do not match ys or the data is empty. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn quadrature_trapezoid(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite trapezoidal rule for the integral of f over [a, b] with n subintervals. Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn quadrature_simpson(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Composite Simpson's rule for the integral of f over [a, b] with n subintervals (n is clamped up to an even count; returns 0.0 for n <= 0). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn quadrature_gauss(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: n-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature over [a, b]. Nodes/weights are computed on the fly by Newton iteration on the Legendre polynomial (valid for any n >= 1); returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Exact for polynomials of degree <= 2n - 1. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn quadrature_adaptive(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Adaptive quadrature to absolute tolerance tol via recursive Simpson refinement (a global error bookkeeping loop, at most 32 levels deep). Returns NaN for tol <= 0 (documented). Complexity: O(refinements * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn quadrature_monte_carlo(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, n: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Monte Carlo quadrature of f over [a, b] with n samples using the seeded xiom RNG (math.random). Returns 0.0 for n <= 0 (documented). Error ~ O(sigma / sqrt(n)). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn optimize_golden(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Minimize the univariate f over [a, b] by golden-section search to width tol. Returns the minimizing x (at most 200 iterations). Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn optimize_ternary(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Minimize the univariate f over [a, b] by ternary search to width tol. Returns the minimizing x (at most 200 iterations). Complexity: O(200 * cost(f)).

docs.title: fn optimize_bfgs(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by the BFGS quasi-Newton method from x0 (approximate inverse Hessian updated by the secant formula; line search = fixed step 1). Returns the last iterate (at most 200 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n^2).

docs.title: fn optimize_lbfgs(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], m: Int, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by limited-memory BFGS from x0 keeping the last m update pairs. Falls back to steepest descent when the history is empty. Returns the last iterate (at most 200 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * m * n).

docs.title: fn optimize_simplex(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by the Nelder-Mead downhill simplex method from x0. Returns the best vertex (at most 500 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n).

docs.title: fn optimize_powell(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by Powell's conjugate direction method from x0 (cyclic one-dimensional golden-section line searches along a direction set). Returns the best point (at most 100 outer iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n * golden).

docs.title: fn optimize_cg(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by nonlinear conjugate gradient (Polak-Ribiere) from x0 with an exact-ish line search. Returns the last iterate (at most 500 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * cost(grad)).

docs.title: fn optimize_gradient(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], lr: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by gradient descent with learning rate lr from x0. Alias of gradient_descent. Complexity: O(steps * cost(grad)).

docs.title: fn optimize_newton(f: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, grad: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], hess: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Vec[Float64]], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize f by Newton's method with the Hessian from x0: solve H d = -g and step. Returns the last iterate (at most 100 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n^3).

docs.title: fn optimize_least_squares(residuals: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Vec[Float64], x0: &Vec[Float64], tol: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Minimize the sum of squared residuals by Gauss-Newton from x0 (requires the residual Jacobian; a one-sided finite-difference Jacobian is used when not available through the residual function alone). Returns the last iterate (at most 100 iterations). Complexity: O(iters * n^3).

docs.title: fn bisection_root(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Bracketing root finder via bisection. Alias of bisection. Complexity: O(log((b-a)/tol)).

docs.title: fn newton_root(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, fprime: fn(Float64) -> Float64, x0: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Derivative-based Newton root finder. Alias of newton. Complexity: O(200 * cost(f + f')).

docs.title: fn solver_single(f: fn(Float64) -> Float64, a: Float64, b: Float64, tol: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: General single-equation root solver over [a, b]. Uses Brent's method (robust bracketing with quadratic convergence). Alias of brent.

docs.title: fn dynamic_programming(states: &Vec[Int], actions: fn(Int) -> Vec[Int], reward: fn(Int, Int) -> Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Optimal value of each state by discounted value iteration: V[s] = max over next states ns in actions(s) of (reward(s, ns) + gamma V[ns]) with gamma = 0.99, converged when the largest update is below 1e-6 (at most 200 passes). Empty for an empty state set. Complexity: O(iters * A).

docs.title: fn inventory(demand: &Vec[Float64], holding_cost: Float64, order_cost: Float64) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Optimal order quantities over time by an (s, S)-style periodic-review heuristic: target S = 1.5 * mean demand, reorder point s = mean demand; orders top inventory back up to S. Returns one order quantity per period. Empty for an empty demand series. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn scheduling(jobs: &Vec[(Int, Int, Int)], machines: Int) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text: Job-to-machine assignment minimizing the makespan by list scheduling: jobs (id, duration, priority) are placed on the least-loaded machine in priority order. Returns a Vec[Int] with one machine index per job (in the input order). Empty for no jobs or machines <= 0. Complexity: O(jobs * machines).

docs.title: fn facility_location(demand: &Vec[Float64], candidates: &Vec[(Float64, Float64)], k: Int) -> Vec[Int]

docs.title: fn revenue_management(seats: Int, fare_classes: &Vec[(Float64, Float64)]) -> Vec[Float64]

docs.title: fn stochastic_optimization(objective: fn(&Vec[Float64]) -> Float64, bounds: &Vec[(Float64, Float64)], iters: Int) -> Vec[Float64]
docs.text: Stochastic search optimum within bounds by uniform random sampling: the objective is minimized over the box [bounds[i].0, bounds[i].1]^dims with iters samples; returns the best point. Empty for degenerate input. Complexity: O(iters * dims * cost(objective)).
