docs.title: fn float_mantissa(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: The significand of f as an integer (implicit leading bit included for normal values; no implicit bit for subnormals). Zero, NaN, and infinities map to 0 (documented). Exact: computed by scaling |f| by exact powers of two until it lies in [1, 2), then multiplying by 2^52 (or 2^(e+1074) for subnormals). Complexity: O(|exponent|) -- at most ~1074 iterations.

docs.title: fn float_exponent(f: Float64) -> Int
docs.text: Unbiased binary exponent of |f|: the unique e with 2^e <= |f| < 2^(e+1). Zero, NaN, and infinities map to 0 (documented; IEEE's stored exponent of zero would be -1023, but 0 is the conventional frexp-style result). Exact via repeated halving/doubling. Complexity: O(|e|) -- at most ~1074 iterations.

docs.title: fn float_is_subnormal(f: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff f is a subnormal value: 0 < |f| < 2^-1022 (the minimum normal). Zero, NaN, and infinities are not subnormal. Exact via comparison. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn float_is_nan(f: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff f is NaN (f != f is the IEEE identity). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn float_is_infinite(f: Float64) -> Bool
docs.text: True iff f is +inf or -inf (checked against 1.0/0.0 and -1.0/0.0). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn float_next_up(f: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Smallest Float64 strictly greater than f. FALLBACK (TODO(compiler): needs bitcast intrinsic): returns f unchanged until intrinsic lands (exact next-up needs float_bits). Do not rely on the value.

docs.title: fn float_next_down(f: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Largest Float64 strictly less than f. FALLBACK (TODO(compiler): needs bitcast intrinsic): returns f unchanged until intrinsic lands. Do not rely on the value.

docs.title: fn float_ulp(f: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Unit in the last place of f: the distance to the next representable value. FALLBACK (TODO(compiler): needs bitcast intrinsic): returns 0.0 until one lands. Do not rely on the value.

docs.title: fn float_classify(f: Float64) -> Str
docs.text: Classification string: "nan", "inf", "-inf", "subnormal", "zero", or "normal" (checked in that order). The "nan" branch uses f != f (IEEE). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: type Fraction
docs.text:
A rational number num/den with den > 0, always in lowest terms.

Field Type num Int den Int

docs.title: fn fraction_new(num: Int, den: Int) -> Fraction
docs.text:
Constructs a reduced fraction from num/den, normalizing the sign to the denominator. den == 0 returns the zero fraction 0/1 (documented fallback for the requires-clause violation). Result satisfies the module invariant. Complexity: O(log max(|num|,|den|)).

  • Precondition: den != 0
  • Postcondition: result.den > 0

docs.title: fn fraction_from_float(f: Float64) -> Fraction
docs.text: Best rational approximation of f via continued-fraction convergents. The first convergent that would overflow i64 (or the first exact one) is returned. Zero, NaN, and infinities map to 0/1 (documented). |f| must be < 2^63 for the floor cast; larger magnitudes return the current convergent. Complexity: O(log |f|) iterations.

docs.title: fn fraction_add(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a + b. Pre-reduces by gcd(a.den, b.den) to limit overflow; the result is re-reduced. Cross-products may still overflow i64 for very large denominators (documented). Complexity: O(log max(a.den, b.den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_sub(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a - b. Complexity: O(log max(a.den, b.den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_mul(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a * b. Cross-cancels via gcd before multiplying, minimizing overflow. Complexity: O(log max(|num|, den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_div(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Option[Fraction]
docs.text: a / b as a / (b^-1). None when b is zero (no silent division by zero). Complexity: O(log max(|num|, den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_reduce(f: Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: Reduces f to lowest terms with a positive denominator. Identity when f already satisfies the module invariant. Complexity: O(log max(|num|,|den|)).

docs.title: fn fraction_to_float(f: Fraction) -> Float64
docs.text: Converts to Float64 (numerator / denominator division). A zero denominator (invariant violation) returns 0.0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_to_str(f: Fraction) -> Str
docs.text: Renders as "num/den". Complexity: O(1) string building.

docs.title: fn fraction_is_zero(f: Fraction) -> Bool
docs.text: Returns true iff the numerator is zero. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_compare(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Int
docs.text: Three-way comparison via gcd-reduced cross-multiplication: -1, 0, or 1. Valid because denominators are positive. Cross-products can overflow i64 for large fractions (documented). Complexity: O(log max(den)).

docs.title: fn u64_mul_sat(a: UInt64, b: UInt64) -> UInt64
docs.text: Saturating u64 multiplication: clamps at 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_from_i64(v: Int) -> Int128
docs.text: Constructs an Int128 from a signed 64-bit value (sign-extended). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_from_parts(hi: Int, lo: UInt64) -> Int128
docs.text: Constructs an Int128 directly from a high signed limb and a low unsigned limb (value = hi * 2^64 + lo). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_add(a: Int128, b: Int128) -> Int128
docs.text: 128-bit addition (wraps on overflow). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_sub(a: Int128, b: Int128) -> Int128
docs.text: 128-bit subtraction (wraps on underflow). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_neg(a: Int128) -> Int128
docs.text: Two's-complement negation. Handles INT128_MIN correctly (wraps back to itself, as required by two's-complement arithmetic). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_abs(a: Int128) -> Int128
docs.text: Absolute value (returns the negated value for INT128_MIN, documenting the two's-complement wrap). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_mul_wide(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int128
docs.text: Full 128-bit product of two 64-bit signed values. i64_mul_wide(2^32, 2^32) == { hi: 1, lo: 0 } == 2^64. Exact. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_mul(a: Int128, b: Int128) -> Int128
docs.text: 128 x 128 multiplication (result is modulo 2^128; low 128 bits are exact regardless of signedness). Complexity: O(1) -- native i128 mul.

docs.title: fn i128_compare(a: Int128, b: Int128) -> Int
docs.text: Three-way comparison (-1/0/1). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_is_zero(a: Int128) -> Bool
docs.text: Returns true iff the value is exactly zero. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_is_negative(a: Int128) -> Bool
docs.text: Returns true iff the value is negative (top bit set). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_to_i64(a: Int128) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Converts to i64; None if the value does not fit in a signed 64-bit range. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_to_str(a: Int128) -> Str
docs.text:
Decimal string representation, handling the sign. Exact for the full Int128 range, including INT128_MIN. Complexity: O(128 * digits) ~ O(1) bounded by 39 digits.

NOTE (2026-08-08): uses 64-bit limb arithmetic, NOT native i128 div/rem -- the sdiv/srem i128 libcalls (__divti3/__modti3) inside a multi-iteration loop with memory ops miscompile at clang -O2 (verified repeatedly). The limb algorithm is exact (e2e-proven pre-D1) and works at every opt level.

docs.title: fn i128_from_str(s: Str) -> Result[Int128, Str]
docs.text: Parses a decimal string (optional +/- prefix) into an Int128. Returns Err on invalid characters, empty input, or overflow beyond the 128-bit range. Complexity: O(digits * 128) ~ O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_shl(a: Int128, n: Int) -> Int128
docs.text: Arithmetic shift left by n bits (wraps at 128 bits). n >= 128 yields zero. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i128_shr(a: Int128, n: Int) -> Int128
docs.text: Arithmetic shift right by n bits (sign-extending). For n >= 128 the result is the sign (all ones for negatives, zero otherwise). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_mul_div(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Int
docs.text: a*b/c evaluated with a 128-bit intermediate, then clamped (saturated) to the i64 range. c == 0 returns 0 (documented). Exact for all i64 inputs. Complexity: O(1) -- native i128 mul + div.

docs.title: fn u8_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: u8 from i64: Some(v) iff 0 <= v <= 255. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn u8_from_i32(v: Int32) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: u8 from i32 (promoted through i64 arithmetic). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn u16_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: u16 from i64: Some(v) iff 0 <= v <= 65535. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn u32_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: u32 from i64: Some(v) iff 0 <= v <= 4294967295. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn u64_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[UInt64]
docs.text: u64 from i64: Some(v) iff v >= 0. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i8_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: i8 from i64: Some(v) iff -128 <= v <= 127. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i16_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: i16 from i64: Some(v) iff -32768 <= v <= 32767. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i32_from_i64(v: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: i32 from i64: Some(v) iff -2147483648 <= v <= 2147483647. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_u64(v: UInt64) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: i64 from u64: Some(v) iff v has the top bit clear. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_i32(v: Int32) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from i32: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_i16(v: Int16) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from i16: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_i8(v: Int8) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from i8: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_u8(v: UInt8) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from u8: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_u16(v: UInt16) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from u16: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_from_u32(v: UInt32) -> Int
docs.text: i64 from u32: always fits. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_from_int(v: Int) -> Float64
docs.text: Float64 from i64 (lossless only for |v| < 2^53; rounds beyond). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_from_i32(v: Int32) -> Float64
docs.text: Float64 from i32: always exact. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_from_u64(v: UInt64) -> Float64
docs.text: Float64 from u64: exact split into two 32-bit halves avoids relying on unsigned-to-float conversions for values above i64::MAX. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_from_int(v: Int) -> Float32
docs.text: Float32 from i64 (rounds for |v| > 2^24). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_from_f64(v: Float64) -> Float32
docs.text: Float32 from Float64 (round-to-nearest; inf/NaN propagate). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_from_f32(v: Float32) -> Float64
docs.text: Float64 from Float32: always exact. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_from_f64_trunc(v: Float64) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Truncating conversion Float64 -> Int. None on NaN or out-of-i64-range. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_from_f64_round(v: Float64) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Rounding conversion Float64 -> Int (round-half-away-from-zero). None on NaN or out-of-range. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i32_from_f64_trunc(v: Float64) -> Option[Int32]
docs.text: Truncating conversion Float64 -> Int32. None on NaN, out-of-i64-range, or outside the Int32 range. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i32_from_f64_round(v: Float64) -> Option[Int32]
docs.text: Rounding conversion Float64 -> Int32 (round-half-away-from-zero). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn u64_from_f64_trunc(v: Float64) -> Option[UInt64]
docs.text: Truncating conversion Float64 -> UInt64. None on NaN, negatives, or values >= 2^64. Handles the high half without unsigned-to-int casts. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_from_f32_trunc(v: Float32) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Truncating conversion Float32 -> Int. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_from_f32_round(v: Float32) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Rounding conversion Float32 -> Int (round-half-away-from-zero). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn int_from_str_radix_checked(s: Str, radix: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Bounds-checked integer parse in the given radix (2..36). Reuses parse_int_radix; None on invalid input or overflow. Complexity: O(len(s)).

docs.title: fn i64_abs(v: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Absolute value of an i64. NOTE: |INT_MIN| wraps to INT_MIN (two's-complement); use i64_neg_checked for overflow-safe negation. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i32_abs(v: Int32) -> Int32
docs.text: Absolute value of an i32. |INT32_MIN| wraps to INT32_MIN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i16_abs(v: Int16) -> Int16
docs.text: Absolute value of an i16. |INT16_MIN| wraps to INT16_MIN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i8_abs(v: Int8) -> Int8
docs.text: Absolute value of an i8. |INT8_MIN| wraps to INT8_MIN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_abs(x: Float64) -> Float64

docs.title: fn f32_abs(x: Float32) -> Float32
docs.text: Absolute value of a Float32. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_clamp(v: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int

docs.title: fn i32_clamp(v: Int32, lo: Int32, hi: Int32) -> Int32

docs.title: fn u64_clamp(v: UInt64, lo: UInt64, hi: UInt64) -> UInt64

docs.title: fn f64_clamp(x: Float64, lo: Float64, hi: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Clamps a Float64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_clamp(x: Float32, lo: Float32, hi: Float32) -> Float32
docs.text: Clamps a Float32. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_signum(v: Int) -> Int
docs.text: -1/0/1 for negative/zero/positive i64. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i32_signum(v: Int32) -> Int
docs.text: -1/0/1 for i32. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_signum(v: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: -1.0/0.0/1.0 for a Float64. NaN returns NaN (IEEE signum semantics). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_signum(v: Float32) -> Float32
docs.text: -1.0/0.0/1.0 for a Float32. NaN returns NaN. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_pow(base: Int, exp: Int) -> Int
docs.text: base^exp for i64 via square-and-multiply. Overflows WRAP (documented); use i64_pow_checked for overflow detection. Negative exponent returns 0. Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn u64_pow(base: UInt64, exp: Int) -> UInt64
docs.text: base^exp for u64. Overflows WRAP (documented). Negative exponent returns 0. Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn i32_pow(base: Int32, exp: Int) -> Int32
docs.text: base^exp for i32 (wraps at 32 bits; documented). Negative exponent returns 0. Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn f64_pow(base: Float64, exp: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text:
Float64 power, delegating to xiom.math.pow. Negative bases require an integer exponent; otherwise returns NaN. Exponent outside the i64 range returns NaN (documented edge). Complexity: O(log exp) via libm.

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn f32_pow(base: Float32, exp: Float32) -> Float32
docs.text: Float32 power (promoted through f64_pow). Complexity: O(log exp).

docs.title: fn i64_min_of3(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Minimum of three i64 values. Concrete (generic min3 needs Ord dispatch). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_max_of3(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Maximum of three i64 values. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_new(num: Int, den: Int) -> Fraction
docs.text: Builds a reduced fraction from num/den, normalizing the sign to the denominator. den == 0 returns the zero fraction (documented). Complexity: O(log max(|num|, |den|)) for gcd.

docs.title: fn fraction_from_int(v: Int) -> Fraction
docs.text: Builds the fraction v/1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_zero() -> Fraction
docs.text: The zero fraction 0/1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_one() -> Fraction
docs.text: The one fraction 1/1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_add(a: &Fraction, b: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a + b. Pre-reduces by gcd(a.den, b.den) to limit overflow; the final result is re-reduced. Cross-products may still overflow i64 for very large denominators (documented). Complexity: O(log max(den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_sub(a: &Fraction, b: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a - b. Complexity: O(log max(den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_mul(a: &Fraction, b: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a * b. Cross-cancels via gcd before multiplying, minimizing overflow. Complexity: O(log max(|num|, den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_div(a: &Fraction, b: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: a / b (flip b and multiply). Dividing by the zero fraction yields zero (documented). Complexity: O(log max(|num|, den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_neg(a: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: -a. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_compare(a: Fraction, b: Fraction) -> Int
docs.text: Three-way comparison via cross-multiplication. Cross-products can overflow i64 for large fractions (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_is_zero(a: Fraction) -> Bool
docs.text: Returns true iff the fraction is zero. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_num(a: Fraction) -> Int
docs.text: The numerator. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_den(a: Fraction) -> Int
docs.text: The denominator (always > 0). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_to_float(a: Fraction) -> Float64
docs.text: Converts to Float64 (numerator/denominator division). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_to_float32(a: Fraction) -> Float32
docs.text: Converts to Float32. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn fraction_to_str(a: Fraction) -> Str
docs.text: Renders as "num/den". Complexity: O(1) string building.

docs.title: fn fraction_from_str(s: Str) -> Option[Fraction]
docs.text: Parses "num/den" (optional signs on each part). None on malformed input, empty parts, or a zero denominator. Complexity: O(len(s)).

docs.title: fn fraction_reciprocal(a: &Fraction) -> Fraction
docs.text: 1/a (den/num). The zero fraction has no reciprocal; returns zero. Complexity: O(log max(|num|, den)).

docs.title: fn fraction_pow_int(a: Fraction, n: Int) -> Fraction
docs.text: a^n for integer exponents. Negative n raises the reciprocal; n == 0 returns one. n == INT_MIN returns zero (documented overflow edge). Complexity: O(log |n|).

docs.title: fn fraction_is_proper(a: Fraction) -> Bool
docs.text: Returns true iff |num| < den (a proper fraction). NOTE: |INT_MIN| wraps (documented); proper tests near the i64 extreme are degenerate. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn i64_lerp(a: Int, b: Int, t: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Integer lerp: a + (b - a) * t with t clamped to [0, 1]. For i64, t is effectively 0 or 1. NOTE: (b - a) * t can overflow i64 for extreme ranges (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_lerp(a: Float64, b: Float64, t: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Float64 lerp: a + (b - a) * t. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f32_lerp(a: Float32, b: Float32, t: Float32) -> Float32
docs.text: Float32 lerp: a + (b - a) * t. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_inverse_lerp(a: Float64, b: Float64, v: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Inverse lerp: (v - a) / (b - a), clamped to [0, 1]. If b == a, returns 0 (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn f64_remap(v: Float64, in_lo: Float64, in_hi: Float64, out_lo: Float64, out_hi: Float64) -> Float64
docs.text: Remaps v from the range [in_lo, in_hi] to [out_lo, out_hi] (linear). If in_hi == in_lo, returns out_lo (documented). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_from_float(x: Float64) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Constructs a BigFloat from a native float. NaN/inf are not representable (the underlying implementation requires finite inputs; do not pass them). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_from_str(s: Str) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Parses a decimal string ("3.14", "-1e-10", ".5"). None on invalid input. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_to_str(b: BigFloat) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal string representation at the current precision. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_with_precision(b: BigFloat, p: Int) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Re-rounds b to p significant digits (round-half-to-even), returning a fresh value with precision p. p < 1 is clamped to 1 (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_add(a: BigFloat, b: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Sum a + b, rounded to max(a.precision, b.precision). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_sub(a: BigFloat, b: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Difference a - b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_mul(a: BigFloat, b: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Product a * b. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_div(a: BigFloat, b: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Quotient a / b. None when b is zero. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_neg(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Negation. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_abs(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Absolute value. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_sqrt(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Square root. None when a is negative (Newton on the significand). Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_cbrt(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Cube root. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_exp(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat

docs.title: fn bigfloat_ln(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]

docs.title: fn bigfloat_log10(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Base-10 logarithm. None when a is not positive. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_log2(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Base-2 logarithm. None when a is not positive. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_pow(base: BigFloat, exp: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Exponentiation base^exp for arbitrary BigFloat exponent (log + exp). Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_sin(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Sine. Complexity: O(prec^2) series.

docs.title: fn bigfloat_cos(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Cosine. Complexity: O(prec^2) series.

docs.title: fn bigfloat_tan(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Tangent. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_asin(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]

docs.title: fn bigfloat_acos(a: BigFloat) -> Option[BigFloat]
docs.text: Arccosine. None when a is outside [-1, 1]. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_atan(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Arctangent. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_atan2(y: BigFloat, x: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Four-quadrant arctangent of y/x. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_sinh(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Hyperbolic sine. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_cosh(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Hyperbolic cosine. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_tanh(a: BigFloat) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Hyperbolic tangent. Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_pi(p: Int) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Pi to p significant digits (p < 1 clamped to 1). Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_e(p: Int) -> BigFloat
docs.text: Euler's number e to p significant digits (p < 1 clamped to 1). Complexity: O(prec^2).

docs.title: fn bigfloat_compare(a: BigFloat, b: BigFloat) -> Int
docs.text: Three-way comparison: -1, 0, or 1 ordering a vs b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_from_int(v: Int) -> BigInt
docs.text: Constructs a BigInt from a native integer. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigint_from_str(s: Str) -> Option[BigInt]
docs.text: Parses a decimal string (optional leading '-'/'+'). None on invalid input (empty string or non-digit character). Complexity: O(n^2) accumulation.

docs.title: fn bigint_to_str(b: BigInt) -> Str
docs.text: Decimal string representation. Complexity: O(n).

docs.text: Lowercase hexadecimal string representation ("ff", "-1a"). Complexity: O(n).

docs.text: Product a * b. Complexity: O(n^2) schoolbook, Karatsuba above 36k digits.

docs.text: Quotient a / b (truncating). None when b is zero. Complexity: O(n^2) Knuth Algorithm D.

docs.text:
base raised to a non-negative integer power exp (square-and-multiply). exp < 0 returns zero (documented). Complexity: O(log exp) multiplications.

  • Precondition: exp >= 0

docs.title: fn bigint_neg(a: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Negation. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_abs(a: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Absolute value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.text: Three-way comparison: -1, 0, or 1 ordering a vs b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.text: Whether a equals b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_lt(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether a is strictly less than b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_gt(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether a is strictly greater than b. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_bit_and(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Bitwise AND (two's-complement semantics). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_bit_or(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Bitwise OR (two's-complement semantics). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_bit_xor(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Bitwise XOR (two's-complement semantics). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigint_shift_left(a: BigInt, n: Int) -> BigInt
docs.text:
Left shift by n bits (multiply by 2^n; n < 0 treated as 0). This is a true BIT shift (distinct from xiom.bigint's decimal shift_left). Complexity: O(n^2) via the multiplications.

  • Precondition: n >= 0

docs.title: fn bigint_shift_right(a: BigInt, n: Int) -> BigInt
docs.text:
Arithmetic (floor) right shift by n bits: b >> n rounds toward -inf for negative b. n < 0 treated as 0. Complexity: O(n^2) via the divisions.

  • Precondition: n >= 0

docs.title: fn bigint_is_prime(b: BigInt) -> Bool
docs.text: Probabilistic primality test (Miller-Rabin, deterministic for n < 3.3e24). Complexity: O(k log^3 n) bigint operations.

docs.title: fn bigint_gcd(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Greatest common divisor (non-negative). Complexity: O(log n) divisions.

docs.title: fn bigint_lcm(a: BigInt, b: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text: Least common multiple; lcm(0, x) == 0. Complexity: O(gcd + mul).

docs.title: fn bigint_mod_inverse(a: BigInt, m: BigInt) -> Option[BigInt]
docs.text: Modular inverse of a mod m via extended Euclid. None when gcd(a, m) != 1 or when m is zero. The result lies in [0, |m|). Complexity: O(log m) divisions.

docs.title: fn bigint_mod_pow(base: BigInt, exp: BigInt, m: BigInt) -> BigInt
docs.text:
(base^exp) mod m via square-and-multiply. Requires m != 0 and exp >= 0; a zero modulus returns zero (documented). Complexity: O(log exp) muls.

  • Precondition: !xiom.bigint.bigint_is_zero(&m)
  • Precondition: !xiom.bigint.bigint_is_negative(&exp)

docs.title: fn bigint_factorial(n: Int) -> BigInt
docs.text:
n! as an arbitrary-precision integer. n < 0 returns zero (documented). Complexity: O(n) bigint multiplications.

  • Precondition: n >= 0

docs.title: fn bigint_binomial(n: Int, k: Int) -> BigInt
docs.text:
Binomial coefficient C(n, k). Invalid k (outside [0, n]) returns zero. Complexity: O(k) bigint multiplications/divisions.

  • Precondition: n >= 0
  • Precondition: k >= 0
  • Precondition: k <= n

docs.title: type BigRat
docs.text:
Arbitrary-precision rational number: num/den, den > 0, always reduced.

Field Type num BigInt den BigInt

docs.title: fn bigrat_new(num: BigInt, den: BigInt) -> Option[BigRat]
docs.text: Constructs a reduced BigRat from num/den, normalizing the sign to the denominator. None when den is zero. Zero maps to 0/1. Complexity: O(gcd) bigint operations.

docs.title: fn bigrat_from_int(v: Int) -> BigRat
docs.text: Constructs the BigRat v/1. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigrat_from_str(s: Str) -> Option[BigRat]
docs.text: Parses "num/den" (optional signs) or a decimal string ("3.14", "-0.5"). None on invalid input, empty parts, or a zero denominator. Complexity: O(n^2) via the bigint accumulation.

docs.title: fn bigrat_to_str(r: BigRat) -> Str
docs.text: String representation: "num" when the denominator is 1, else "num/den". Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_numerator(r: BigRat) -> BigInt
docs.text: The numerator (a copy). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_denominator(r: BigRat) -> BigInt
docs.text: The denominator (always positive; a copy). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_add(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Sum a + b: (a.numb.den + b.numa.den) / (a.den*b.den), reduced. Complexity: O(n^2) bigint operations.

docs.title: fn bigrat_sub(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Difference a - b. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigrat_mul(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Product a * b. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigrat_div(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> Option[BigRat]
docs.text: Quotient a / b. None when b is zero. The denominator sign is normalized by the reduction. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigrat_neg(a: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Negation. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_abs(a: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Absolute value. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_recip(a: BigRat) -> Option[BigRat]
docs.text: Reciprocal 1/a. None when a is zero. Complexity: O(n^2) reduction.

docs.title: fn bigrat_reduce(r: BigRat) -> BigRat
docs.text: Reduces r to lowest terms with a positive denominator. Identity when r already satisfies the invariant. Complexity: O(gcd).

docs.title: fn bigrat_is_reduced(r: BigRat) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether r is in lowest terms with a positive denominator. Complexity: O(gcd).

docs.title: fn bigrat_is_integer(r: BigRat) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether the denominator divides the numerator (i.e. r is an integer; for a reduced fraction this is den == 1). Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigrat_is_zero(r: BigRat) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether r equals zero. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn bigrat_compare(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> Int
docs.text: Three-way comparison via cross-multiplication: -1, 0, or 1. Valid because denominators are positive. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigrat_eq(a: BigRat, b: BigRat) -> Bool
docs.text: Whether a equals b. Complexity: O(n^2).

docs.title: fn bigrat_to_float(r: BigRat) -> Float64
docs.text: Converts to Float64 (bigint magnitude accumulation, then division). The result may be inf for values beyond the Float64 range (documented). Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn bigrat_to_integer(r: BigRat) -> Option[BigInt]
docs.text: The integer value of r; None when r is not integral. Complexity: O(1) (reduced form: integral iff den == 1).

docs.title: fn file_name(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: file_name returns the file-name portion of path, or None. Delegates to fs.fs_file_name. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn file_parent(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: file_parent returns the directory portion of path, or None. Delegates to fs.fs_parent_dir. Complexity: O(n).

docs.title: fn detect_eol(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Detect the line ending style. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: "lf", "crlf", "cr", "mixed" or "none". Complexity: O(n). Pure.

docs.title: fn detect_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Detect and describe the byte-order mark, or "" if absent. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: "utf-8", "utf-16le", "utf-16be", "utf-32le", "utf-32be" or "". Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn has_utf8_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data starts with the UTF-8 BOM. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the EF BB BF prefix. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn has_utf16le_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data starts with the UTF-16 LE BOM. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the FF FE prefix. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn has_utf16be_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data starts with the UTF-16 BE BOM. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the FE FF prefix. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn has_utf32le_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data starts with the UTF-32 LE BOM. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the FF FE 00 00 prefix. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn has_utf32be_bom(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data starts with the UTF-32 BE BOM. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the 00 00 FE FF prefix. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_binary(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Classify data as binary by a control-byte heuristic. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true when a NUL byte is present or control bytes exceed 30% of the sampled prefix. Complexity: O(min(n, 1024)). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_text(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Classify data as plain text by a control-byte heuristic. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true when the data is not classified as binary. Complexity: O(min(n, 1024)). Pure.

docs.title: fn detect_encoding(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Guess the character encoding. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: "utf-8", "utf-16le", "utf-16be", "utf-32le", "utf-32be", "ascii" or "binary". Complexity: O(n). Pure.

docs.title: fn magic_number(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Return the magic-number hex prefix of data. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: the lowercase hex of the first up-to-8 bytes ("" for empty input). Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn detect_mime(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Detect the MIME type by content sniffing. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: a MIME type guessed from magic bytes and text heuristics. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn mime_from_magic(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text: Detect the MIME type from magic bytes only. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: the magic-derived MIME type or "application/octet-stream". Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_image_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data matches a known image format. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/WebP/ICO signatures. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_audio_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data matches a known audio format. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for WAV/OGG/FLAC/MP3 (ID3) signatures. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_video_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data matches a known video container. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for AVI/MP4/MKV/WebM/Ogg signatures. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_pdf_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data looks like a PDF. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the "%PDF-" header. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_zip_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data is a ZIP archive. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the "PK\x03\x04" local-file header. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_gzip_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data is a gzip stream. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the 1F 8B header. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_elf_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data is an ELF binary. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the 7F 45 4C 46 header. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_pe_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data is a PE/COFF binary. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the "MZ" DOS header. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn is_macho_data(data: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Bool
docs.text: Return true if data is a Mach-O binary. Parameters: data -- the bytes to inspect. Returns: true for the Mach-O magic numbers. Complexity: O(1). Pure.

docs.title: fn fs_file_name(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: fs_file_name returns the file-name portion of path (after the last '/' or '\'), or None if path is empty or ends in a separator.

docs.title: fn fs_parent_dir(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: fs_parent_dir returns the directory portion of path (everything before the last '/' or '\'), or None if path has no parent.

docs.title: fn fs_extension(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: fs_extension returns the extension (text after the last dot in the file name), or None if there is no dot or the dot is leading/trailing. "a/b.tar.gz" -> Some("gz"); "a/b" -> None.

docs.title: fn fs_stem(path: Str) -> Option[Str]
docs.text: fs_stem returns the path with the last extension stripped, or the path unchanged if it has no extension. "a/b.tar.gz" -> "a/b.tar".

docs.title: fn fs_is_hidden(path: Str) -> Bool
docs.text: fs_is_hidden returns true if the file name starts with a dot, except for the special entries "." and "..".

docs.title: fn fs_join_parts(parts: Vec[Str]) -> Str
docs.text: fs_join_parts joins the given components with the OS path separator (env.path_separator: "\" on Windows, "/" elsewhere).

docs.title: fn fs_normalize(path: Str) -> Str
docs.text: fs_normalize collapses duplicate separators and resolves "." and ".." lexically, without touching the filesystem. Leading "/" and "C:\"-style drive prefixes are preserved. "a/b/../c//d/./e" -> "a/c/d/e".

docs.title: fn fs_with_extension(path: Str, new_ext: Str) -> Str
docs.text: fs_with_extension replaces the extension of path with new_ext, or appends it if path has no extension. "a/b.txt" + "md" -> "a/b.md".

docs.title: fn fs_split(path: Str) -> (Str, Str)
docs.text: fs_split returns (dir, file) -- the directory and file-name portions.

docs.title: fn fs_unique_path(dir: Str, name: Str) -> Str
docs.text: fs_unique_path returns dir/name if it does not exist, otherwise appends " (1)", " (2)", ... up to a maximum of 1000 attempts.

docs.text: proc_status_text formats a process exit code as "exit()". The runtime does not expose wait-status decoding (WIFSIGNALED etc.), so signals cannot be distinguished here.

docs.text: proc_command_exists returns true if the named command can be found on the system PATH. Delegates to xiom.process.command_exists, which runs "where " (Windows) or "which " (Unix) via the shell. Spawning the command itself is not a reliable existence probe, since the system()-based spawn reports the command's exit code rather than a spawn failure.

  • Postcondition: result is Ok(_) => result >= 0

  • Precondition: pid > 0

docs.title: fn is_running(pid: Int) -> Bool
docs.text:

  • Precondition: pid > 0

docs.text: Find every non-overlapping match of r in s, in left-to-right order. An empty pattern matches at every byte boundary. Complexity: O(len(s) * len(r)) per match.

docs.title: fn regex_captures(r: Regex, s: Str) -> Option[Vec[Str]]
docs.text: Capture groups of the first match of r in s. This engine has no group syntax, so the returned vector contains exactly one element: the full match text (group 0). None when there is no match. Complexity: O(len(s) * len(r)) worst case.

docs.title: fn regex_matches(pattern: Str, s: Str) -> Vec[Match]

docs.title: fn regex_replace_all(r: Regex, s: Str, replacement: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Replace every non-overlapping match of r in s with replacement. Returns s unchanged when there are no matches. Literal replacement. Complexity: O(len(s) + matches * len(replacement)).

docs.title: fn regex_split(r: Regex, s: Str) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text: Split s around every non-overlapping match of r. An empty pattern splits into individual characters. The trailing segment is always present. Complexity: O(len(s) * len(r)) worst case.

docs.title: fn regex_find_iter(r: Regex, s: Str) -> Vec[Match]
docs.text: Lazily-ordered iterator of every match of r in s, materialised as a vector in left-to-right order. Equivalent to regex_find_all. Complexity: O(len(s) * len(r)) worst case.

docs.title: fn binary_search(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Index of target in a sorted v, or None. O(log n). Requires v to be sorted in non-decreasing order.

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.text:

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.title: fn lower_bound(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Index of the first element >= target; v.len() if none. O(log n). Requires v to be sorted.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0 && result <= v.len()

docs.title: fn upper_bound(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Int
docs.text:
Index of the first element > target; v.len() if none. O(log n). Requires v to be sorted.

  • Postcondition: result >= 0 && result <= v.len()

docs.title: fn binary_search_by(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int, compare: fn(&Int, &Int) -> Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Binary search with a custom comparator: compare(&v[mid], &target). O(log n). The comparator must be a named function returning -1/0/1. Requires v to be sorted per the comparator.

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.title: fn search_range(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text:
(lo, hi) tuple: all occurrences of target span the half-open index range [lo, hi). If target is absent, lo == hi (empty range). O(log n).

  • Postcondition: result._0 >= 0 && result._1 >= result._0 && result._1 <= v.len()

docs.title: fn binary_search_float(v: &Vec[Float64], target: Float64) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Binary search for an exact float value in a sorted Vec[Float64]. O(log n). Requires v to be sorted ascending (exact IEEE-754 equality semantics: -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal; NaN never matches because NaN == NaN is false). Returns None when target is absent.

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.text:

  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 256

docs.text: Good-suffix shift table: gs[i] is the safe shift when a mismatch occurs at pattern position i. O(m). Computed from the standard suffix array.

docs.title: fn boyer_moore_search(text: Str, pattern: Str) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Start index of the first pattern occurrence in text using the full Boyer-Moore algorithm (bad-character + good-suffix tables). O(n/m) best, O(n*m) worst. Returns None when pattern is empty or longer than text.

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value + pattern.len() <= text.len()

docs.title: fn boyer_moore_search_all(text: Str, pattern: Str) -> Vec[Int]
docs.text:
Start indices of every occurrence of pattern in text (full Boyer-Moore). O(n/m) average. Empty pattern yields an empty result.

  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 0

docs.title: fn boyer_moore_horspool(text: Str, pattern: Str) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Horspool variant of Boyer-Moore: bad-character table only, keyed on the last text character of the window. O(n*m) worst, good average.

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value + pattern.len() <= text.len()

docs.title: fn rabin_karp_hash(s: Str) -> Int
docs.text: Rolling hash value of the string s. O(len). Uses the fixed base 31 and the Mersenne prime 2^31-1 as modulus; values are always in [0, mod).

docs.title: fn rabin_karp_search(text: Str, pattern: Str) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Rolling-hash substring search. O(n + m) expected, O(n*m) worst on hash collisions. Compares character-by-character when hashes match, so results are exact. Returns None when pattern is empty or longer than text.

docs.title: fn interpolation_search(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Index of target via value-proportional probing. O(log log n) average on uniformly distributed sorted Int arrays, O(n) worst. Returns Some(index) or None. Safe on unsorted data (degrades to a probe sequence).

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.title: fn interpolation_search_sorted(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

docs.title: fn exponential_search(v: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0 && result.value < v.len()

  • Postcondition: result.len() == pattern.len()

docs.title: fn linear_search[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Linear search -- O(n) worst/average, O(1) best. Scans the array sequentially from index 0. Works on unsorted data. Returns Some(index) of the first match, or None if not found.

docs.title: fn binary_search[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Binary search -- O(log n). Requires a sorted array (non-decreasing). Classic divide-and-conquer: repeatedly narrows the range by comparing the middle element against the target. Returns Some(index) if found, or None if not present.

docs.title: fn interpolation_search(arr: &Vec[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Interpolation search -- O(log log n) average on uniformly distributed sorted Int arrays, O(n) worst. Analogous to how one searches a phone book: estimates position based on value range. Returns Some(index) if found, or None if not present.

docs.title: fn exponential_search[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Exponential search on a sorted slice; returns the index or None.

docs.title: fn jump_search[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Jump search on a sorted slice; returns the index or None.

docs.title: fn lower_bound[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Int
docs.text: lower_bound -- O(log n). Returns the index of the first element >= target. If all elements are < target, returns arr.len(). Requires sorted array.

docs.title: fn upper_bound[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> Int
docs.text: upper_bound -- O(log n). Returns the index of the first element > target. If all elements are <= target, returns arr.len(). Requires sorted array.

docs.title: fn binary_search_range[T](arr: &Vec[T], target: &T) -> (Int, Int)
docs.text: binary_search_range -- O(log n). Returns (lower_bound, upper_bound) as a tuple: [lo, hi) of all indices where arr[i] == target. If target is not found, lo == hi (empty range). Requires sorted array.

docs.title: enum TomlValue
docs.text:
TOML v1 reader (the subset a package manifest needs).

Supported: comments; bare and quoted keys; [table] and [a.b] headers; basic strings with the five common escapes; literal strings; integers (decimal, optional sign, _ separators); floats; booleans; arrays of strings/ints/floats. Keys are stored section-qualified with '.' ("package.name"), in file order.

NOT in v1: dates/times, multi-line strings, inline tables, arrays-of-tables, dotted keys in assignment position. The WRITER (toml_write) emits the same subset: flat section-qualified keys, root keys first, [section] blocks in first-appearance order, the five common escapes. Errors carry the 1-based line number.

  • TStr(_0: Str)
  • TInt(_0: Int)
  • TFloat(_0: Float64)
  • TBool(_0: Bool)
  • TStrArray(_0: Vec[Str])
  • TIntArray(_0: Vec[Int])
  • TFloatArray(_0: Vec[Float64])

docs.title: fn intro_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])
docs.text:
Introsort: quicksort that switches to heapsort when the recursion depth budget is exhausted, and to insertion sort on small ranges. O(n log n) worst case, O(log n) auxiliary space. Unstable.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn insertion_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])

O(n^2) insertion sort of the whole vector; fast for small/nearly-sorted input. Stable.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn tim_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])
docs.text:
Timsort: merge sort over natural runs with insertion sort for short runs. O(n log n) worst case, O(n) best (already sorted). Stable. O(n) space.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn shell_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])
docs.text:
Gap-based insertion sort using the Ciura sequence. O(n log^2 n) average, O(n^2) worst. Unstable. In-place, O(1) space.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn bubble_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])
docs.text:
Adjacent-swap bubble sort. O(n^2) worst/average, O(n) best. Stable. Educational only.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn selection_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int])

Minimum-selection sort with O(n) swaps. O(n^2) always. Unstable.

  • Postcondition: is_sorted(v) == true

docs.title: fn partial_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int], k: Int)
docs.text: Place the smallest k elements at the front, in order. O(n*k), O(1) space. Unstable. If k >= n the whole vector becomes sorted; if k <= 0 no-op.

docs.title: fn nth_element(v: &mut Vec[Int], n: Int) -> Int
docs.text: Quickselect: the element that would land at index n in sorted order. O(n) average, O(n^2) worst. Unstable. Reorders v as a side effect. n is clamped into [0, len-1]; returns 0 for an empty vector.

docs.title: fn sort_stable(v: &mut Vec[Int])

docs.title: fn counting_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int], max_val: Int)
docs.text: Stable counting sort for values in [0, max_val]. O(n + k), stable, O(n+k) space. If max_val < 0, or if any element lies outside [0, max_val], the vector is left unchanged (documented contract).

docs.title: fn bucket_sort(v: &mut Vec[Int], buckets: Int)
docs.text: Bucket sort: distribute the elements of v into buckets value-ordered ranges and concatenate them back. Stable within each bucket. O(n + b) expected on uniformly distributed data (b = buckets), O(n^2) worst when all elements land in one bucket. Uses a flat offset table (no nested vectors -- TODO(compiler): BUG 34 -- and no Int128 index math -- TODO(compiler): BUG 35 -- both crash in this fn shape). Values whose spread exceeds i64 range (span > 2^63) may produce wrong bucket indexes; exact for any realistic dataset. Requires v to be non-empty and buckets >= 1; otherwise v is unchanged.

docs.title: fn sort_insertion[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: Insertion sort -- O(n2) worst/average, O(n) best (already sorted). Stable. Excellent for small arrays (n < ~50) and nearly-sorted data. Algorithm: builds sorted prefix by inserting each new element into place.

docs.title: fn sort_selection[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: Selection sort -- O(n2) always. Unstable. Minimal writes (O(n) swaps). Algorithm: repeatedly finds the minimum element from the unsorted tail and places it at the current position.

docs.title: fn sort_bubble[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: Bubble sort -- O(n2) worst/average, O(n) best (already sorted). Stable. Simple educational algorithm; rarely used in production. Algorithm: compares adjacent elements and swaps if out of order; largest elements "bubble" to the end each pass.

docs.title: fn sort_quick[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: In-place quicksort: average O(n log n), worst case O(n^2).

docs.title: fn sort_merge[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: In-place merge sort with O(n log n) worst case.

docs.title: fn sort_heap[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: In-place heapsort: O(n log n) worst case, O(1) extra space.

docs.title: fn sort_shell[T](arr: &mut Vec[T])
docs.text: Shell sort -- O(n log2 n) average using Ciura gap sequence. Unstable. Generalizes insertion sort with a decreasing gap. Algorithm: sorts elements at decreasing gap distances; when gap=1, it becomes ordinary insertion sort (on a nearly-sorted array).

docs.title: fn sort_counting(arr: &mut Vec[Int], max_val: Int)
docs.text: Counting sort -- O(n + k) where k = max_val. Stable. Only for Int arrays with known non-negative range [0, max_val]. Algorithm: counts occurrences of each value, then reconstructs sorted array by iterating counts in order.

docs.title: fn stable_sort_by[T](arr: &mut Vec[T], compare: fn(&T, &T) -> Int)
docs.text: Stable sort with a caller comparator (equal elements keep their order).

docs.title: fn partial_sort[T](arr: &mut Vec[T], k: Int)
docs.text: partial_sort -- places the smallest k elements at the front, in order. O(n-k) with O(1) extra space. Unstable. Selection-based: repeatedly find the minimum of the unsorted tail and swap it into position. If k >= n the entire vector becomes sorted; if k <= 0 nothing happens.

docs.title: fn str_align_left(s: Str, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Left-aligns s in a field of width bytes, padding on the right with spaces. A string already at or over the width is returned unchanged; a negative width is rejected (returns s). Params: s the source string; width the field width in bytes. Returns: the left-aligned string. Error case: none; width < 0 is a no-op. Complexity: O(width).

  • Postcondition: width < 0 => result == s

docs.title: fn str_align_right(s: Str, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Right-aligns s in a field of width bytes, padding on the left with spaces. A string already at or over the width is returned unchanged; a negative width is rejected (returns s). Params: s the source string; width the field width in bytes. Returns: the right-aligned string. Error case: none; width < 0 is a no-op. Complexity: O(width).

  • Postcondition: width < 0 => result == s

docs.title: fn str_align_center(s: Str, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Centers s in a field of width bytes, padding both sides with spaces; when the padding does not split evenly the extra space goes on the right. A string already at or over the width is returned unchanged; a negative width is rejected (returns s). Params: s the source string; width the field width in bytes. Returns: the centered string. Error case: none; width < 0 is a no-op. Complexity: O(width).

  • Postcondition: width < 0 => result == s

docs.title: fn str_align_justify(s: Str, width: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Justifies s to width bytes by distributing the extra space between the words: gaps are padded from left to right, so earlier gaps may receive one extra space. When there is only one word, or the words already fill the width, or width is negative, s is returned unchanged. Params: s the source string; width the target width in bytes. Returns: the justified string. Error case: none; width < 0 is a no-op. Complexity: O(|s| + width).

  • Postcondition: width < 0 => result == s

docs.title: fn unicode_bidi_class(c: Char) -> Str
docs.text: Bidirectional class of c (two- or three-letter code per UAX #9): "L", "R", "AL", "EN", "AN", "ES", "ET", "CS", "NSM", "WS", "B", "S", "BN", "LRE", "LRO", "RLE", "RLO", "PDF", "ON". Unmapped codepoints report "L". Params: c the character to classify. Returns: the bidi class code. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_mirrored(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c has the Bidi_Mirrored property, i.e. it has a mirrored counterpart used when the text direction flips (brackets, angle brackets, curly braces, and a few quotes/guillemets). Unmapped codepoints are not mirrored. Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is mirrored. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_mirror_char(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text: Mirror image of c: the paired bracket/quote on the other side, or c itself when c is not mirrored. E.g. '(' -> ')', ')' -> '(', '[' -> ']', '{' -> '}', '<' -> '>', '<<' -> '>>', '<' -> '>'. Params: c the character to mirror. Returns: the mirrored counterpart, or c itself. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_block(c: Char) -> Str
docs.text: Returns the Unicode block name of the character c, e.g. 'A' yields "Basic Latin" and 'Omega' yields "Greek and Coptic". Code points outside every known block yield "Undefined". Params: c the character to classify. Returns: the block name. Error case: none. Complexity: O(number of table entries).

docs.title: fn unicode_block_name(code: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Returns the Unicode block name for the block code given as a code-point hex string. Accepted forms: bare hex ("41", "1F600"), "0x..." and "U+..." prefixed, and "\u" escaped. Invalid or non-hex input yields "Undefined". Params: code the code point as a hex string. Returns: the block name, or "Undefined" when unparsable/unmapped. Error case: "Undefined" for empty, non-hex, or unmapped input. Complexity: O(|code| + number of table entries).

  • Precondition: true

docs.title: fn sb_new() -> Vec[UInt8]
docs.text:
New empty builder. Complexity: O(1).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == 0

docs.title: fn sb_push_byte(sb: &mut Vec[UInt8], b: UInt8)
docs.text:
Append one byte. Complexity: O(1) amortized.

  • Postcondition: sb.len() >= 1

docs.title: fn sb_push_str(sb: &mut Vec[UInt8], s: Str)
docs.text:
Append a whole string (byte copy; UTF-8 safe -- bytes are opaque here). Complexity: O(s.len()) amortized.

  • Postcondition: s.len() > 0 => sb.len() >= 1

docs.title: fn sb_push_int(sb: &mut Vec[UInt8], v: Int)
docs.text:
Append the decimal representation of v (sign-aware, zero-safe). Emits digits without any temporary Str allocation. Complexity: O(digits).

  • Postcondition: sb.len() >= 1

docs.title: fn sb_to_str(sb: &Vec[UInt8]) -> Str
docs.text:
Materialize the built string: single allocation, ownership of the fresh NUL-terminated buffer moves into the result Str ([XFER]). The builder vector is untouched and remains usable. Complexity: O(n).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == sb.len()

docs.title: fn sb_clear(sb: &mut Vec[UInt8])
docs.text:
Reset to empty. Complexity: O(n).

  • Postcondition: sb.len() == 0

docs.title: fn str_upper(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts all characters of s to uppercase. Returns a new string with the same byte length as s. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_lower(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts all characters of s to lowercase. Returns a new string with the same byte length as s. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_title(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Capitalizes the first letter of every word of s; remaining characters of each word are lowercased. Whitespace and separators are preserved. Returns a new string with the same byte length as s. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_swap_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Swaps the case of every letter in s; characters that are neither uppercase nor lowercase are left unchanged. Returns a new string with the same byte length as s. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_capitalize(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Uppercases the first character of s and lowercases the rest. Returns s unchanged when s is empty. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_sentence_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Capitalizes the first letter of each sentence of s. A sentence boundary is a '.', '!' or '?' character; the next alphabetic character is uppercased. Returns a new string with the same byte length as s. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_to_camel_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts s to lowerCamelCase: the first word is lowercased and each following word is capitalized; separators are dropped. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: s.len() == 0 => result.len() == 0

docs.title: fn str_to_snake_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts s to snake_case: words are lowercased and joined with '_'. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: s.len() == 0 => result.len() == 0

docs.title: fn str_to_kebab_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts s to kebab-case: words are lowercased and joined with '-'. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: s.len() == 0 => result.len() == 0

docs.title: fn str_to_pascal_case(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Converts s to PascalCase: every word is capitalized and joined without a separator. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: s.len() == 0 => result.len() == 0

docs.title: fn str_casefold(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Full Unicode case folding of s for case-insensitive comparison. ASCII, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Greek and Cyrillic uppercase letters are folded to their lowercase forms; the sharp s (ss/SS) folds to "ss" and dotted capital I (I) folds to "i" + combining dot, matching the Unicode full case-folding mapping for those characters. Params: s the string to fold. Returns: the case-folded string. Error case: none; malformed UTF-8 bytes pass through unchanged. Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn str_casefold_ascii(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: ASCII-only case folding of s: 'A'..'Z' become lowercase, every other byte is copied verbatim. No Unicode tables are consulted. Params: s the string to fold. Returns: the ASCII-folded string. Error case: none. Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn unicode_general_category(c: Char) -> Str
docs.text: Two-letter Unicode general category of c, e.g. "Lu", "Ll", "Nd", "Zs", "Po". Unmapped codepoints report "Cn" (Other/unassigned). Params: c the character to classify. Returns: the two-letter general category code. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_letter(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is a letter (categories Lu, Ll, Lt, Lm, Lo). Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is a letter. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is a decimal digit (category Nd). Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is a decimal digit. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_punct(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is punctuation (categories Pc, Pd, Ps, Pe, Pi, Pf, Po). Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is punctuation. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_symbol(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is a symbol (categories Sm, Sc, Sk, So). Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is a symbol. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_separator(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is a separator (categories Zs, Zl, Zp). Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is a separator. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_control(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is a control or format character, or otherwise falls in the "Other" (C) group: Cc, Cf, Cs (surrogates), Co (private use) or Cn (unassigned). The inverse of unicode_is_printable. Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is in category Cc/Cf/Cs/Co/Cn. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn unicode_is_printable(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text: True when c is printable, i.e. not a control/format character and not in the "Other" (C) group. Letters, marks, numbers, punctuation, symbols and separators are printable. Params: c the character to test. Returns: true when c is printable. Error case: none. Complexity: O(1).

docs.title: fn is_alphabetic(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is alphabetic.

  • Postcondition: result == ((to_int_from_char(c) >= 65 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 90) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 97 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 122))

docs.title: fn is_alphanumeric(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is alphabetic or numeric.

  • Postcondition: result == (is_alphabetic(c) || is_digit(c))

docs.title: fn is_ascii(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the code point is below 128.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) <= 127)

docs.title: fn is_control(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is a control code.

  • Postcondition: result == ((to_int_from_char(c) >= 0 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 31) || to_int_from_char(c) == 127)

docs.title: fn is_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is an ASCII decimal digit.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 48 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 57)

docs.title: fn is_lowercase(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is lowercase.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 97 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 122)

docs.title: fn is_uppercase(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is uppercase.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 65 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 90)

docs.title: fn is_numeric(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is numeric.

  • Postcondition: result == is_digit(c)

docs.title: fn is_punctuation(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is punctuation.

  • Postcondition: result == ((to_int_from_char(c) >= 33 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 47) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 58 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 64) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 91 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 96) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 123 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 126))

docs.title: fn is_whitespace(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
True when the character is whitespace.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) == 32 || to_int_from_char(c) == 9 || to_int_from_char(c) == 10 || to_int_from_char(c) == 13)

docs.title: fn to_lowercase(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text: Lowercase mapping of the character.

docs.title: fn to_uppercase(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text: Uppercase mapping of the character.

docs.title: fn to_digit(c: Char, radix: Int) -> Option[Int]
docs.text:
Numeric value in the given radix (2..36), or None.

  • Postcondition: radix < 2 || radix > 36 => result is None
  • Postcondition: result is Some(_) => result.value >= 0

docs.title: fn from_digit(n: Int, radix: Int) -> Option[Char]
docs.text:
Character for a digit value in the given radix, or None.

  • Postcondition: n < 0 || n >= radix => result is None
  • Postcondition: radix < 2 || radix > 36 => result is None

docs.title: fn len_utf8(c: Char) -> Int
docs.text:
UTF-8 encoding length of the character (1..4).

  • Postcondition: result >= 1 && result <= 4

docs.title: fn encode_utf8(c: Char, buf: &mut Vec[UInt8])
docs.text: Append the UTF-8 encoding of the character to buf.

docs.title: fn is_letter(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Alias for is_alphabetic. Returns true if c is an ASCII letter (a-z, A-Z).

  • Postcondition: result == is_alphabetic(c)

docs.title: fn is_control_char(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Alias for is_control. Returns true if c is a C0 control character or DEL.

  • Postcondition: result == is_control(c)

docs.title: fn is_hex_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a hexadecimal digit (0-9, a-f, A-F).

  • Postcondition: result == ((to_int_from_char(c) >= 48 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 57) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 65 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 70) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 97 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 102))

docs.title: fn is_binary_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a binary digit ('0' or '1').

  • Postcondition: result == (c == '0' || c == '1')

docs.title: fn is_octal_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an octal digit ('0' through '7').

  • Postcondition: result == (c >= '0' && c <= '7')

docs.title: fn is_symbol(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a symbol character (punctuation, currency, math, or modifier). Covers ASCII punctuation + common Unicode symbol ranges.

  • Postcondition: result == (is_currency(c) || is_math_symbol(c) || is_punctuation(c) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 160 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 191) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 215 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 247) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8208 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 8231) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8240 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 8286) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8592 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 8703) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8960 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 9215) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 9472 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 9599) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 9600 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 9631) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 9632 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 9727) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 9728 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 9983) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 9984 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 10175))

docs.title: fn is_currency(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a currency symbol. Covers $, cent, pound, yen, and the currency symbols block U+20A0..U+20CF.

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) == 36 || to_int_from_char(c) == 162 || to_int_from_char(c) == 163 || to_int_from_char(c) == 165 || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8352 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 8399))

docs.title: fn is_math_symbol(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a mathematical symbol. Covers +, -, *, /, =, <, >, the plus-minus sign, and the mathematical operators block U+2200..U+22FF.

  • Postcondition: result == (c == '+' || c == '-' || c == '*' || c == '/' || c == '=' || c == '<' || c == '>' || to_int_from_char(c) == 177 || c == 'x' || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 8704 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 8959))

docs.title: fn is_emoji(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c falls within basic emoji code point ranges. Covers emoticons, miscellaneous symbols, transport, supplemental symbols.

  • Postcondition: result == ((to_int_from_char(c) >= 128512 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 128591) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 127744 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 128511) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 128640 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 128767) || (to_int_from_char(c) >= 129280 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 129535))

docs.title: fn is_combining_mark(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a combining diacritical mark (U+0300..U+036F).

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 768 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 879)

docs.title: fn to_title_case(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text: Returns the title-case version of c. For a single character this is equivalent to to_uppercase.

docs.title: fn is_ascii_letter(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII letter (a-z, A-Z).

  • Postcondition: result == is_alphabetic(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII digit (0-9). Alias for is_digit.

  • Postcondition: result == is_digit(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_hex_digit(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII hexadecimal digit (0-9, a-f, A-F).

  • Postcondition: result == is_hex_digit(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_punctuation(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is ASCII punctuation (codes 33-47, 58-64, 91-96, 123-126).

  • Postcondition: result == is_punctuation(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_whitespace(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is ASCII whitespace (space, tab, newline, carriage return).

  • Postcondition: result == is_whitespace(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_control(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII control character (codes 0-31 or 127).

  • Postcondition: result == is_control(c)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_graphic(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII graphic character (codes 33-126, visible + space).

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 33 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 126)

docs.title: fn is_ascii_printable(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an ASCII printable character (codes 32-126, includes space).

  • Postcondition: result == (to_int_from_char(c) >= 32 && to_int_from_char(c) <= 126)

docs.title: fn char_to_digit_value(c: Char) -> Option[Int]
docs.text: Returns the numeric value (0-9) of a digit character, or None if c is not a digit.

docs.title: fn digit_value_to_char(n: Int) -> Option[Char]
docs.text: Returns the character representation of a single digit value n (0-9), or None if out of range.

docs.title: fn is_uppercase_ascii(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is an uppercase ASCII letter (A-Z).

  • Postcondition: result == is_uppercase(c)

docs.title: fn is_lowercase_ascii(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is a lowercase ASCII letter (a-z).

  • Postcondition: result == is_lowercase(c)

docs.title: fn to_ascii_upper(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text:
Returns the ASCII uppercase version of c. If c is not a lowercase ASCII letter, it is returned unchanged.

  • Postcondition: result == to_uppercase(c)

docs.title: fn to_ascii_lower(c: Char) -> Char
docs.text:
Returns the ASCII lowercase version of c. If c is not an uppercase ASCII letter, it is returned unchanged.

  • Postcondition: result == to_lowercase(c)

docs.title: fn is_whitespace_or_separator(c: Char) -> Bool
docs.text:
Returns true if c is whitespace or a Unicode separator character. Covers ASCII whitespace + line/paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029).

  • Postcondition: result == (is_whitespace(c) || to_int_from_char(c) == 8232 || to_int_from_char(c) == 8233)

docs.title: fn str_chunk(s: Str, n: Int) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text: Splits s into consecutive chunks of n bytes; the final chunk may be shorter. A chunk size below 1 or an empty input yields an empty vector. Params: s the source string; n the chunk size in bytes. Returns: a Vec[Str] of chunks covering s exactly once. Error case: n < 1 or s.len() == 0 => empty vector. Complexity: O(s.len()).

docs.title: fn str_chunks_reverse(s: Str, n: Int) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text: Splits s into chunks of n bytes starting from the end; the remainder (if any) forms the first chunk. A chunk size below 1 or an empty input yields an empty vector. Params: s the source string; n the chunk size in bytes. Returns: a Vec[Str] of chunks in source order (first may be shorter). Error case: n < 1 or s.len() == 0 => empty vector. Complexity: O(s.len()).

docs.title: fn str_windows(s: Str, n: Int) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text: Returns all length-n overlapping substrings (windows) of s. A window size below 1 or larger than the input yields an empty vector. Params: s the source string; n the window size in bytes. Returns: a Vec[Str] with one element per start position 0..len-n. Error case: n < 1 or len < n => empty vector. Complexity: O(s.len()).

docs.title: fn collate_compare(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
docs.text:
Compare a and b in byte-wise collation order. Returns a negative Int when a sorts before b, zero when the strings are byte-identical, and a positive Int when a sorts after b. Bytes are compared unsigned, so bytes above 0x7F sort after ASCII on every platform. Params: a, b the strings to compare. Returns: negative / zero / positive per the byte-wise ordering of a vs b. Error case: none. Complexity: O(min(|a|, |b|)).

  • Postcondition: result >= -1 && result <= 1

docs.title: fn collate_compare_numeric(a: Str, b: Str) -> Int
docs.text: Compare a and b in natural collation order: embedded runs of ASCII digits are compared numerically rather than byte-wise, so "file2" sorts before "file10". Delegates to the proven natural-order comparator. Params: a, b the strings to compare. Returns: negative / zero / positive per the natural ordering of a vs b. Error case: none. Complexity: O(|a| + |b|).

docs.title: fn collate_key(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Collation key of s: an ASCII-case-folded copy such that comparing two keys with collate_compare reproduces the case-insensitive collation order of the original strings. Bytes above 0x7F pass through unchanged. Params: s the string to key. Returns: a key string whose byte-wise order matches the collation order. Error case: none. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_shuffle(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text:
Random permutation of the characters of s via Fisher-Yates, drawing swap indices from the runtime PRNG. The result is a rearrangement of the characters of s (same byte length); the order is not specified. Params: s the string to shuffle. Returns: a random permutation of the characters of s. Error case: none; the empty string maps to itself. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_shuffle_seeded(s: Str, seed: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Deterministic shuffle of s using the given seed: the same seed always produces the same permutation via the Park-Miller sequence. The empty string maps to itself. Params: s the string to shuffle; seed the PRNG seed. Returns: the seeded permutation of s. Error case: none. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_shuffle_words(s: Str) -> Str
docs.text: Random permutation of the whitespace-separated words of s. The result rejoins the shuffled words with single spaces; the original spacing runs are not preserved (see str_reverse_words for spacing preservation). Params: s the string whose words to shuffle. Returns: the shuffled words joined by single spaces. Error case: none; a string with no words yields "". Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn str_shuffle_words_seeded(s: Str, seed: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Deterministic word shuffle of s using the given seed. Params: s the string whose words to shuffle; seed the PRNG seed. Returns: the seeded permutation of the words of s. Error case: none; a string with no words yields "". Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn str_rotate(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Rotate s right by n byte positions: a positive n moves characters toward the end of the string ("abcde" rotated right by 2 is "deabc"). A negative n rotates left. Rotating by a multiple of |s| returns s. Params: s the string to rotate; n the rotation amount in bytes. Returns: the rotated string. Error case: none; the empty string is returned unchanged. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_rotate_left(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Rotate s left by n byte positions ("abcde" rotated left by 2 is "cdeab"). A negative n rotates right. Params: s the string to rotate; n the rotation amount in bytes. Returns: the rotated string. Error case: none; the empty string is returned unchanged. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_rotate_right(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
docs.text:
Rotate s right by n byte positions; identical to str_rotate and kept as the explicit right-rotation entry point. Params: s the string to rotate; n the rotation amount in bytes. Returns: the rotated string. Error case: none; the empty string is returned unchanged. Complexity: O(|s|).

  • Postcondition: result.len() == s.len()

docs.title: fn str_rotate_word(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str
docs.text: Rotate the whitespace-separated words of s by n positions: a positive n moves words toward the end. The result rejoins the rotated words with single spaces. Params: s the string whose words to rotate; n the rotation amount in words. Returns: the word-rotated string. Error case: none; a string with no words yields "". Complexity: O(|s|).

docs.title: fn str_permutations(s: Str) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text:
All permutations of the characters of s, treating the characters as distinct (n! results for |s| = n; duplicate characters yield duplicate permutations). An empty string yields a vector containing "". The permutations are emitted in lexicographic byte order. Params: s the source string. Returns: a Vec[Str] with n! permutations. Error case: inputs longer than 8 characters return an empty vector (documented guard against an impractical 8!+ result set). Complexity: O(n! * n).

  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 0

docs.title: fn str_permutations_n(s: Str, n: Int) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text:
All n-length arrangements of the characters of s (P(|s|, n) results, ordered, without repetition). n == 0 yields [""]; n < 0 or n > |s| yields an empty vector. Params: s the source string; n the arrangement length. Returns: a Vec[Str] of n-length permutations. Error case: n < 0 or n > |s| => empty vector; large inputs are guarded as in str_permutations. Complexity: O(P(n, k) * k).

  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 0

docs.title: fn str_combinations(s: Str, n: Int) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text:
All n-length combinations of the characters of s, each kept in source order (C(|s|, n) results). n < 1 or n > |s| yields an empty vector, matching xiom.string.combine.str_combinations. Params: s the source string; n the combination length. Returns: a Vec[Str] of n-length combinations. Error case: n < 1 or n > |s| => empty vector. Complexity: O(C(n, k) * k).

  • Postcondition: result.len() >= 0

docs.title: fn str_cartesian(a: Str, b: Str) -> Vec[Str]
docs.text:
